For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the verse is a warning that the share Satan claims is not the strong only; his program targets every servant, but his share is only those who accept invocation besides God, female or otherwise, as worship.

**From Female Idols to Appointed Share**

Though only *“cursed by God who said, I will surely take an appointed share of Your servants,”* the verse moves from the single act — calling females besides Him (4:117) — to the system — taking a share. The sūrah that began from a single soul spread into countless men and women (4:1) now sees that spread claimed portionwise by the cursed. The sūrah has shown that those who were oppressed and remained while earth is wide wronged themselves (4:97) while the helpless hoped for pardon (4:99); Satan’s appointed share is those who remain in invocation besides Him where earth’s havens were available. The next verse will detail his program upon that share: mislead, delude with empty hopes, order slitting ears of cattle and altering God’s creation, where whoever takes him as guardian suffers tremendous loss (4:119).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:119

> I will certainly mislead them and delude them with empty hopes. Also, I will order them and they will slit the ears of cattle and alter Allah’s creation.” And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a tremendous loss.

**Expanded Commentary**

**I Will Certainly Mislead and Delude With Empty Hopes**

The vow continues *wa la uḍillannahum wa la umanniyannahum* — I will certainly mislead them and certainly delude them with hopes, with wishing, with *umniyah* — empty promising. *Uḍillannahum* — to lead astray, to cause deviation — was explained as Satan’s first work upon his appointed share (4:118) after curse, the *ḍalāl baʿīd* — far straying — of association (4:116). *Ummaniyahum* — to delude with hopes, to cast wishes, to promise — was read as the mechanism of misguidance: not force but hopes, as the sūrah has shown that Satan promises only delusion (4:120) and that his hopes are empty — *ghurūr* — while God’s promise is true (4:122). The sūrah has shown desires that wish you deviate greatly (4:27), and that the deceitful hide from people but God is with them where they plot by night (4:108); empty hopes delude because they hide consequence. The one who is misled thinks he is given respite as generosity — the sūrah’s *istidrāj* without name but present — while the Book says *“He delays but His plan is flawless”* (68:44 cited in sūrah 7:183). The hopes delude where the emigrant’s true hope is for ranks, forgiveness, mercy (4:96) and many havens (4:100); Satan’s hope is the counterfeit that spending to show off (4:38) or withholding bounty (4:37) is honour preserved.

**I Will Order Them and They Will Slit the Ears of Cattle**

The program *wa la āmurannahum fa la yubattikunna ādhāna al-anʿāmi* — and I will surely order, command them, and they will slit, cut, the ears of cattle — was explained as Satan ordering rites upon livestock. *Āmurannahum* — I will command — was read as Satan issuing command as if lord, in rivalry to God who commands return of trusts (4:58) and to whom the Book’s commands refer disputes (4:59). *Yubattikunna* — to slit, to cut lengthwise, to notch — *ādhāna al-anʿāmi* — ears of cattle — was explained as the Meccan custom of dedicating livestock to idols — *baḥīrah, sāʾibah, waṣīlah, ḥām* (5:103) — by slitting ears as mark, forbidding its use, devoting it to the female gods (4:117). The act was read not as pastoral technique but as worship-mark: to alter the ear is to claim ownership of the animal beyond the Creator’s intact creation. The sūrah has shown that those given a portion believe in *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* (4:51); slitting ears is the ritual of that belief. The verb *la yubattikunna* — they will surely slit — with double emphasis shows obedience: his order is executed.

**And Alter God’s Creation**

The wider command *wa la āmurannahum fa la yughayyirunna khalqa Allāhi* — and I will order them and they will alter, change, God’s creation — was explained as the generalisation of slitting ears: changing what God created intact, wholesome, upon *fiṭrah*. *Khalq Allāh* — God’s creation — was read as the form, the wholeness, the natural disposition, the law inscribed in creation, as the sūrah began from a single soul created and from it its mate (4:1) and later warned not to alter the *fiṭrah* — innate way. Commentators explained altering as physical mutilations dedicating to idols, as tattooing, as castration, as claiming the lawful as forbidden and vice versa, and morally as altering the religion — changing limits set by God (4:13–14) — and altering the self that wrongs itself (4:110). The common element was explained as Satan commanding to claim lordship over creation: to cut what God made whole and to call the cut devotion. Where the sūrah says there is no good in most secret talks except commanding charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), this is the evil command — to slit and to alter — whose compliance proves the guardian taken.

**And Whoever Takes Satan as Guardian Instead of God Suffers Tremendous Loss**

The verdict *wa man yattakhidh al-shayṭāna waliyyan min dūni Allāhi fa qad khasira khusrānan mubīnā* — and whoever takes Satan as guardian, protector, ally instead of God has certainly suffered a tremendous, manifest, clear loss — was explained with *walī* — guardian, patron, protector — the same *walī* and *naṣīr* the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45). To take Satan as *walī* instead — *min dūni Allāhi* — was read as choosing the cursed (4:118) as guardian whose promise is delusion (4:120). *Khasara khusrānan mubīnā* — suffered tremendous, clear loss — was explained as loss manifest in both worlds: in this world by slitting what was wholesome and altering what was created balanced, in the next by Hell without escape (4:121) versus Gardens forever under true promise (4:122). The sūrah has shown that whoever takes Satan as associate, what an evil associate (4:38), and that the share Satan takes is the share of those who invoke besides Him (4:117–118); to take him as *walī* is to become that share. The loss is *mubīn* — clear — because the alternative — the Book and wisdom taught (4:113), the great reward for charity and reconciliation (4:114), the forgiveness found upon seeking (4:110) — was clear, and the choice of the cutter over the Creator is clear deviation.

**A Verse That Makes Satan’s Program Concrete**

Placed after curse and appointed share (4:118), this verse makes Satan’s program concrete: mislead, delude with hopes, order slitting ears and altering creation. The sūrah that warned not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) here shows what the other path orders and what its followers execute: cutting creation to mark it for another. The sūrah that began with unity from a single soul (4:1) and that will say to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He encompasses all (4:126) sees altering creation as assault on that unity. For the weak this is protective: to alter creation is not light craft but tremendous loss, clear, because the Creator who made humanity weak yet wills to lighten (4:28) and who gives many havens (4:100) is replaced by a commander who orders cutting. The next verse will summarise the commander’s economy: he promises and deludes with empty hopes, he promises nothing but delusion (4:120), whose end is Hell without escape (4:121).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:120

> Satan only makes them ˹false˺ promises and deludes them with ˹empty˺ hopes. Truly Satan promises them nothing but delusion.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Satan Promises and Deludes With Empty Hopes**

The verse states *yaʿiduhum wa yummanīhim* — he promises them and deludes them with hopes, with *umniyah*, wishing. *Yaʿiduhum* — to promise, to hold out — was explained as Satan’s currency after being cursed and taking an appointed share (4:118) and ordering misleading, slitting ears, altering creation (4:119). The promises were explained as the hopes already named — *ummaniyahum* — empty hopes: that association is nearness, that invoking females brings intercession (4:117), that cutting cattle is devotion, that altering creation is honour, that throwing sin on the innocent cleans the thrower (4:112), that advocacy in this life will have advocacy on the Day (4:109). The sūrah has shown that those who wish you deviate wish it greatly (4:27), that the lagger wishes to share gain without sharing faith (4:73), that the regressed wish you alike in disbelief (4:89); Satan’s promising is the source wish that generates those. *Wa yummanīhim* — and he deludes with hopes — was read as keeping them in wishing — *tamannī* — so that the wish never becomes turning, as the sūrah warns that repentance delayed until death says “now I repent” is not accepted (4:18).

**Truly He Promises Nothing But Delusion**

The qualification *wa mā yaʿiduhumu al-shayṭānu illā ghurūrā* — Satan promises them nothing but delusion, deception, vanity — was explained with *ghurūr* — delusion, deceptive vanity, gloss that vanishes. *Ghurūr* was read as promise that looks like benefit but is harm, as goods neglected for a sweeping assault where weapons are unguarded (4:102) looked safe for a moment. The sūrah elsewhere says *“do not let the deceiver deceive you about God”* (31:33; 35:5) with *gharūr* as Satan’s name, showing that delusion is his title. To say he promises *only* delusion — *illā ghurūra* — was explained as exclusivity: there is no true promise in his portfolio, as the next verses contrast his delusion with Hell without escape (4:121) and with Gardens where God’s promise is always true (4:122). Early notes linked *ghurūr* to the world’s fleeting enjoyment — *matāʿ qalīl* — the little enjoyment the sūrah said is little versus the Hereafter better for the mindful (4:77), and the fleeting gain sought by denying peace (4:94); Satan promises that little as if great. The sūrah has shown that good and evil are both destined while evil from the self as means (4:79); Satan’s delusion is to make the means — altering creation, slitting ears — seem as if it changes destiny toward good.

**A Verse That Follows Altering Creation With Its True Price**

Placed after *he will order slitting ears and altering creation and whoever takes him as guardian suffers tremendous loss* (4:119), this verse follows the order with its true price: the order is paid in delusion. The sūrah that warns there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) here unmasks the secret talks that command altering: their payment is *ghurūr*. The sūrah that commands to verify reports (4:83) and to be sure before fighting (4:94) shows verification failing where hope is empty: the deluded do not verify Satan’s promise because it is a hope, not a proof. The sūrah has shown that God’s promise — *“We will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow forever; God’s promise is always true, whose word is more truthful than God’s?”* (4:122) — is tied to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40); Satan’s promise is tied to loss manifest. The verse was read as the sūrah’s ledger for transaction with Satan: he promises and deludes, you alter, you take him as guardian, you bear clear loss, and his promise, when examined, is nothing but vanity.

**The Economy of Empty Hope**

The concept *umnīyah* — empty hope, wish — was explained linguistically as wishing for what will not be attained by wishing, as the People of the Book and your wishes wish grace by wish alone — *neither by your wishes nor theirs* (4:123). Satan’s economy was described as selling hope without means: he commands slitting ears and altering, which cost the cutter, and pays with hope, which costs him nothing. The sūrah has shown that the believer’s hope is *“you hope from God what they never hope for”* (4:104) — a hope tied to ranks and mercy (4:96) and many havens (4:100) — while Satan’s hope is tied to nothing. The contrast was linked to the beginning where God created from a single soul and spread humanity (4:1) intact; to alter that creation on a hope is to damage the known for the imagined. The verse was also linked to the prior deception where advocates hoped to deceive the Prophet ﷺ yet deceived only themselves (4:113); self-deception is the product sold.

**A Short Verse That Anchors the Two Destinations**

Though only *“he promises and deludes, he promises nothing but delusion,”* the verse anchors the two destinations that follow. Immediately: *they will have Hell as home and find no escape* (4:121) — the delusion’s end near; and then: *those who believe and do good, We will admit into Gardens forever, God’s promise always true* (4:122) — the true promise’s end. The sūrah that let the defier be turned to what he turned to (4:115) and declared association far straying (4:116) here names the engine of that turning: a promise that is nothing but gloss. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the verse is a lightening: you need not be deluded, because the promise that would delude you has been labelled — *illā ghurūrā* — nothing but, so that verification — *tabayyanū* (4:94) — can dismiss it and choose the promise that is ever true.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:121

> It is they who will have Hell as their home, and they will find no escape from it!

**Expanded Commentary**

**They Will Have Hell as Home**

The verse states *ulāʾika maʾwāhum Jahannam* — it is they — those who take Satan as guardian instead of God (4:119), who follow his promises that are only delusion (4:120), who invoke female gods besides Him (4:117) — whose refuge, shelter, home is Hell, *Jahannam*. *Maʾwā* — refuge, shelter, place of return — was explained as the home that receives, as the emigrant finds *murāgham* — many havens — and abundance where God’s earth is spacious (4:100), while these find *maʾwā* as Hell, the inverse haven. The sūrah has used *maʾwā* for the self-wronger who remained where earth was wide — Hell as home, evil destination (4:97) — and for the defier left to what he chose — burning, evil destination (4:115); here the pronoun *ulāʾika* — it is they — restricts to Satan’s share — the appointed portion he claimed (4:118). *Jahannam* was read as the Fire where skins are replaced to taste punishment (4:56), where the intentional killer abides with anger and curse (4:93), where the prepared torment is humiliating for disbelievers who would sweep upon neglect (4:102). To have Hell as *maʾwā* means it is not a passing visit but the place of stay, as Gardens are *maʾwā* for those who believe and do good who stay forever (4:122).

**And They Will Find No Escape From It**

The clause *wa lā yajidūna ʿanhā maḥīṣā* — and they will find no escape, no flight, no diversion from it — was explained with *maḥīṣ* — escape, refuge from, place to incline away. *Lā yajidūna* — they will not find — contrasts with the emigrant’s *yajid* — will find — many havens (4:100) and the helpless hoped to be pardoned where finding was impossible (4:98–99). *ʿAnhā* — from it, away from it — was read as Hell’s encompassing: there is no *murāgham* from Hell, no spaciousness away from it, because the curse that took Satan as guardian cut off the only guardian who could provide escape — *“whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of God suffers tremendous loss”* (4:119) — and promises only delusion (4:120). The sūrah has said that the wronged who sought *murāgham* found it (4:100) and that prayer at fixed time (4:103) is the writ that secures times; Hell without *maḥīṣ* is the writ that secures consequence where promise was delusion. *Lā yajidūna maḥīṣā* was also compared to *“they will not find protector or helper besides God”* for whoever commits evil (4:123): no *walī* and no *naṣīr*, no escape, no diversion.

**A Verse That Seals Satan’s Economy With Its Destination**

Placed after *Satan promises only delusion* (4:120), this verse seals Satan’s economy with its destination. The program — *I will mislead, delude, order slitting ears and altering creation* (4:119) — paid in delusion, ends in Hell as home. The sūrah has shown that the deceiver would deceive none but themselves (4:113) and that throwing sin on the innocent bears slander (4:112); here self-deception’s wage is Hell without diversion. The sūrah has also shown that the believer’s hope is what the disbeliever never hopes for (4:104) — ranks, forgiveness, mercy (4:96) — and that those who believe and do good are promised Gardens where God’s promise is ever true (4:122); the deluded hope that was nothing but gloss ends where no *maḥīṣ* is found because no true promise was behind it. Where the sūrah earlier said *“God has prepared humiliating punishment for disbelievers”* where prayer was guarded (4:102), here the preparation is shelter itself — Hell as *maʾwā* — the humiliation of having no escape from the delusion’s house.

**No Escape Because No Guardian Was Taken**

The phrase *wa lā yajidūna ʿanhā maḥīṣā* was explained as consequence of taking Satan as *walī* (4:119). The sūrah has repeated that God is sufficient as Guardian and Helper (4:45), that the oppressed cry for a guardian and helper from grace (4:75), that the Messenger ﷺ is told to put trust in Him as Trustee (4:81, 4:132). To take Satan as *walī* instead of Him is to choose a guardian who was cursed (4:118) and whose promise is delusion (4:120); on the Day where advocates in this life will find no advocate before God (4:109), there will be no *maḥīṣ* because the only *walī* and *naṣīr* who could provide it was rejected. Classical notes added that *maḥīṣ* — escape place — matches *murāgham* — haven — as both are places of turning; the emigrant who turned to God finds many turnings, the follower of Satan who turned to him finds none. The sūrah that promised the emigrant his reward secured even if death overtakes (4:100) here promises the follower of Satan his loss secured where death overtakes into Hell.

**A Short Verse That Holds the Two Promises Apart**

Though only *“Hell as home and no escape,”* the verse holds the two promises apart. Immediately after: *“those who believe and do good, We will admit into Gardens under which rivers flow forever; God’s promise always true, whose word more truthful?”* (4:122); immediately before: Satan’s promise only delusion. The sūrah that judges by the Book in truth (4:105) and that shows there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) here shows that the Talker behind the evil secret talk leads to a home with no secret exit. For the weak for whom the sūrah lightens burdens, the verse is a clarification: delusion’s home has no exit, while God’s earth has many havens and His forgiveness many entries (4:100, 4:110), so that choosing the guardian who is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving over the guardian whose promise is gloss is the lightest and most spacious choice.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:122

> And those who believe and do good, We will soon admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true. And whose word is more truthful than Allah’s?

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Believe and Do Good — Into Gardens Forever**

The verse states *wa alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti sa nudkhiluhum jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhāru khālidīna fīhā abadan* — and those who believe and do good, do righteous, We will soon admit them into Gardens — orchards, enclosed gardens — under which rivers flow, to stay there forever and ever — *abadan*. *Āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt* — faith and righteous deeds — was explained as the sūrah’s shorthand for the faithful: opposed to those who take Satan as guardian (4:119), who invoke others besides Him (4:117), who follow other than believers’ path (4:115), and who will have Hell without escape (4:121). *Sa nudkhiluhum* — We will soon admit, We will enter — was read as divine assurance that admission is from Us, as the emigrant’s reward falls upon God secure (4:100) and as forgiveness is found upon seeking (4:110). *Jannātin tajrī min taḥtihā al-anhāru* — Gardens under which rivers flow — was explained as the sūrah’s repeated promise: the same phrase as for those who believe and do good earlier (4:57) and as for the obedient limits-keeping (4:13). *Khālidīna fīhā abadan* — staying therein forever and ever — was read with double emphasis — *khālidīn* and *abadan* — unlike *khālidan* alone for the intentional killer (4:93) or the self-wronger’s Hell (4:97): for belief and good, abiding is forever and ever with no exit, while Hell’s abiding is also described without *maḥīṣ* (4:121), keeping the symmetry that each *maʾwā* is lasting in its direction.

**God’s Promise Is Always True**

The affirmation *waʿda Allāhi ḥaqqan* — God’s promise as truth, truly, as right — was explained as the contrast to Satan’s promise that is nothing but delusion (4:120). *Waʿd Allāh* — God’s promise — was read as His word that Gardens are for the faithful, that good is multiplied, that ranks, forgiveness, and mercy are from Him (4:96), that many havens are found (4:100), that prayer at fixed time is writ (4:103), that whoever seeks finds forgiveness (4:110). *Ḥaqqan* — truly, as truth, as right, as due — was explained as that the promise corresponds to reality, not wish, unlike empty wishes that claim grace by belonging (4:123). The sūrah has said that the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* (4:105) — to judge by what He shows; to say His promise is *ḥaqq* is to say judgment by it will be true, as *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40). Where Satan orders cutting and altering (4:119) promising honour, God’s promise to keep creation intact ends in Gardens whose rivers flow under, not cut away.

**And Whose Word Is More Truthful Than God’s?**

The question *wa man aṣdaqu mina Allāhi qīlā* — and whose word, whose speech, whose saying, is more truthful than God’s? — was explained as rhetorical negation: none is more truthful, as earlier *“who is more truthful than God in speech?”* (4:87) where gathering on the Day about which there is no doubt was affirmed. *Qīl* — word, saying — was read as speech that judges, as *“He will gather you on the Day — about which there is no doubt, and who is more truthful than God in speech?”* (4:87) and where *“God’s word is more truthful than any”* seals the same gathering for emigrants. The question was linked to night speech displeasing to Him (4:108) and to advocacy that disputes in this life but not before Him (4:109): all speech besides His — Satan’s promising, secret plotters’ whispering — is delusion or displeasing; His *qīl* is truth. Classical notes added that *qīl* — saying — matches *waʿd* — promise — as both are speech acts; to compare whose *qīl* is more truthful after calling *waʿd* *ḥaqq* is to say: if promise is truth, the Promiser’s every saying is truth, and there is no *ghurūr* in it. The verse generalises the particular case of slander thrown on the innocent (4:112): human speech can bear *buhtān*, God’s cannot.

**A Verse That Completes the Contrast of Two Maws**

Placed after Hell as home without escape (4:121), this verse completes the contrast of two *maʾwās* — refuges — the sūrah has built since the angels’ question about spacious earth (4:97). One branch — helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99), emigrant finds many havens (4:100), traveller shortens and guards prayer (4:101–102), remembers in all postures (4:103), pursues without faltering for hope (4:104), judges by Book (4:105) — ends in Gardens forever whose promise is truth. The other — invoking others, following Satan, accepting his appointed share, cutting creation, hoping his empty hope (4:117–120) — ends in Hell without *maḥīṣ*. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) here shows that the two paths end in two homes whose endurance was named with the same verb — *khālid* — yet opposite quality: one as mercy — *Ghafūr Raḥīm* — one as humiliation prepared (4:102). For the weak the verse is the lightest of weights: belief and good, which the sūrah elsewhere defines as faith in God, Messenger, Books, angels, Last Day without distinction (4:136, 4:152) together with doing what is maʿrūf — charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — is tied to an always-true promise, while Satan’s promise is nothing but delusion.

**The Always-True Promise Against the Always-Delusive Promise**

The pairing *waʿda Allāhi ḥaqqan* versus *mā yaʿiduhumu al-shayṭānu illā ghurūrā* (4:120) was read as the sūrah’s ledger of speech: one promise true, one delusion. The question *man aṣdaqu mina Allāhi qīlā* answers the implicit question of the weak — whom to trust where advocacy is loud, where private talk is many, where the enemy is clear (4:101) and where judgment must be by what God shows (4:105): trust the Speaker whose promise is *ḥaqq* and whose *qīl* none exceeds in truth. The verse was also linked to *“God is sufficient as Witness”* (4:79) and *“God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132): His *qīl* suffices as witness, His *waʿd* suffices as trustee. The next verse will remove wishful trust in any group’s claim, so that the forever abode is tied not to wish but to belief, good, and the ever-true word.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:123

> ˹Divine grace is˺ neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book! Whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly, and they will find no protector or helper besides Allah.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Neither by Your Wishes Nor Those of the People of the Book**

The verse opens *laysa bi amāniyyikum wa lā amāniy ahla al-kitābi* — Divine grace — matter, recompense — is neither by your wishes nor wishes of the People of the Book. *Amāniy* — wishes, fancies, empty hopes — was explained as the *tamannī* — wishing — already unmasked as Satan’s delusion — *yummanīhim* (4:119–120) — and as the human wish that grace be by claim. The sūrah has shown wishes that mislead — those who wish you deviate greatly (4:27), who wish you alike in disbelief (4:89), who wish you neglect weapons for a sweep (4:102) — here it says neither set of wishes governs divine grace. *Laysa bi amāniyyikum* — not by your, Muslims’, wishes — was read as addressing the companions who might count on belief alone while committing evil, and *wa lā amāniyyi ahla al-kitābi* — nor by People of the Book’s wishes — as addressing Jews and Christians who claimed *“we are God’s children”* or *“none enters Paradise except our group.”* The sūrah has said that the People of the Book demanded a written revelation from heaven and were struck for wrongdoing (4:153) and that some Jews distort words (4:46); both groups’ wishes are set aside. Early reports linked the verse to mutual boasting between Muslims and People of the Book, where each claimed Paradise by belonging; the verse removed belonging as claim and installed deed and promise as measure.

**Whoever Commits Evil Will Be Rewarded Accordingly**

The rule *man yaʿmal sūʾan yujza bihī* — whoever commits, does, evil will be rewarded, recompensed accordingly, with it — was explained as the ledger law already given — *whoever earns sin earns only upon himself* (4:111) and *whoever earns evil or sin then throws on innocent bears slander* (4:112) — now as recompense law for all. *Sūʾ* — evil — was read broadly: associating, falling to Satan’s promises, hidden night plotting, devouring wealth, killing a believer, throwing sin. *Yujza bihī* — will be recompensed with it, rewarded accordingly — was explained as exact recompense — *jazāʾ* — the same root for the intentional killer’s *jazāʾ* is Hell (4:93) and for the believer’s *jazāʾ* is Gardens (4:122). The sūrah has said *“God does not wrong even an atom; if it is good He multiplies many times”* (4:40) — punishment is according, reward is multiplied — so *yujza bihī* is the atom-measured side. The pronoun *bihī* — with it, thereby — was read as equivalence: the evil’s own weight as recompense, not another’s, not less than atom. The Book’s promise being true (4:122) and whose word more truthful (4:122) was linked here: to say *yujza bihī* is the Most Truthful’s word about consequence, not a wish.

**And They Will Find No Protector or Helper Besides God**

The closure *wa lā yajid lahū min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — and they will find for themselves no protector, guardian, nor helper besides God — was explained with *walī* and *naṣīr* — the same pair the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45), and that the self-wronger’s advocate cannot provide on the Day (4:109). *Min dūni Allāhi* — besides God, apart from Him, short of Him — was read as the failure of every alternative guardian: clan, People of the Book status, female gods invoked (4:117), Satan the rebellious guardian (4:119) whose promise is delusion, whose abode is Hell without *maḥīṣ* (4:121). To find no *walī* and no *naṣīr* where evil is committed and not sought away (4:110) is the law’s complement to *“whoever seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving, Most Merciful”* — the only *walī* and *naṣīr* besides Him that could rescue is none. The sūrah has warned *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers”* (4:139, 4:144) and *“do not take them as allies unless they emigrate”* (4:89); here the ally beside God is declared absent where evil is choice.

**A Verse That Follows Two Gardens With the Rule of Wishes**

Placed after Gardens forever with rivers under, God’s promise ever true (4:122), this verse follows true promise with the rule that neither wishes govern grace. The sūrah has shown Satan promises and deludes with empty hopes (4:120) — *amāniy* — and contrasts it with God’s promise true; this verse names *amāniy* again as the false measure the community might substitute — *our wishes, their wishes*. The sūrah that promised great reward for commanding charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114) had framed *ibtighāʾ marḍāt Allāh* as the valid seeking, not wishful claim. *Laysa bi amāniyyikum* was therefore read as the hinge where the theology of 4:116 — *He forgives what is less than association for whom He wills* — meets practice: will is not wish. For the weak the verse is clarifying: to hope for forgiveness as helpless (4:99) and to seek it after evil (4:110) is not wish alone but act of seeking; to commit evil expecting belonging to protect is wish, and it will be *yujza bihī*.

**Not by Claim but by Recompense — With No Walī Besides Him**

The construction *laysa bi amāniyyikum* — not by wishes — followed by *man yaʿmal sūʾan yujza bihī* was read as substitution of claim by recompense. The sūrah has said that to Allah belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware (4:126, 4:131–132), and that He is sufficient as Trustee (4:132); recompense *bihī* is therefore not by your computation but by His awareness, yet measured exact as not wronging an atom. The closing *no walī nor naṣīr besides Him* generalises the particular question *who will be their *wakīl* on the Day?* (4:109) and *who will advocate before God?* (4:109) — answer: none besides Him. The verse generalises the theft case’s lesson where advocates for self-wrongers found no advocate on the Day; every evil, by whomever, Muslim or Person of the Book, finds no protector besides Him, only the recompense of the act unless forgiveness is sought and found. The next verse will set the opposite face: those who do good, male or female, with faith will enter Paradise, not wronged even by a speck (4:124).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:124

> But those who do good— whether male or female—and have faith will enter Paradise and will never be wronged ˹even as much as˺ the speck on a date stone.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Do Good — Male or Female — With Faith**

The verse states *wa man yaʿmal mina al-ṣāliḥāti min dhakarin aw unthā wa huwa muʾminun fa ulāʾika yadkhulūna al-jannata* — but those who do, who act, righteous deeds from among good acts — whether male or female — and are believers, while being faithful — will enter Paradise. *Man yaʿmal mina al-ṣāliḥāt* — whoever does righteous deeds — was explained as the Book’s shorthand for the faithful act: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114), standing firm for justice though against selves (4:135), spending from what God provided not to show off (4:38–40), striving with wealth and lives (4:95) and the good whose reward is multiplied many times over (4:40). *Min dhakarin aw unthā* — whether male or female — was read as the sūrah’s consistent equalisation where the single soul spread into countless men and women (4:1), where shares for men and women are obligatory (4:7, 4:11–12), where marry-able bonds include the believing bondwoman where harm is feared (4:25), and where helpless men, women, children are each named for pardon and for haven (4:98, 4:75). To name both was to remove the wish that grace is by belonging — *neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — and to place it on act plus faith. *Wa huwa muʾmin* — while being faithful, and he is a believer — was stressed: good alone without faith is not the entry described, as *“O believers, have faith in God, His Messenger, the Book He sent”* (4:136) commands renewal of faith as basis; the sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven (4:116) because it breaks the faith itself.

**And Will Never Be Wronged Even as Speck on a Date Stone**

The assurance *wa lā yuẓlamūna naqīrā* — and they will never be wronged even as much as the speck, the groove, on a date stone — was explained with *naqīr* — the tiny pit, speck on the stone’s back, the small hollow — the sūrah’s smallest measure. The same measure appeared where envy wishes deviation and God’s kingdom share would not give even a speck (4:53) and where enjoyment of world is little and none will be wronged even by speck (4:77) and where those given understanding do good will not be wronged (4:49). *Lā yuẓlamūna* — never be wronged — was read with the sūrah’s principle *“God does not wrong even an atom; if it is good He multiplies”* (4:40): not wronging is baseline, multiplying is grace. The sūrah has also said that whoever earns sin earns only upon himself (4:111) and whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly with no protector besides Him (4:123); here the complement is that whoever does good with faith will not be wronged even to a speck’s weight. The *naqīr* measure was therefore read as atom-plus: the smallest thing the eye sees on the stone’s back, the least deserving is not cut.

**A Verse That Follows Recompense According With Reward Without Wrong**

Placed after *whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides God* (4:123), this verse follows recompense with reward without wrong. The sūrah has moved from two homes — Hell without escape (4:121) and Gardens forever where promise is true (4:122) — through the rule of wishes — neither yours nor theirs (4:123) — to the entry — *they will enter Paradise and not be wronged a speck* (4:124). The symmetry was noted: evil is rewarded *bihī* — with it, exactly — and no *walī* besides Him rescues; good is rewarded into Paradise and not wronged even a speck, with His promise true whose speech none exceeds (4:122). Where the sūrah says *“do not consume wealth unjustly; trade by mutual consent”* (4:29) and says taking dowry unjustly bears sin (4:20), working good with faith is the trade by mutual consent with Him where no wronging occurs. The verse was also placed against the sūrah’s warning not to crave what God gave some over others but to ask of His bounties (4:32): the speck not wronged is the bounty asked and given without envy.

**Male or Female — The Sūrah’s Equality of Entry**

The phrase *min dhakarin aw unthā* was explained as the sūrah’s equality of entry. The single soul created and its mate and spread of men and women (4:1), the command to be mindful of ties (4:1), the inheritance for both (4:7), the dowry protection (4:4), the standing for justice even against yourselves (4:135) — all are instances where male and female share account before the All-Knowing. The verse generalises that sharing to Paradise entry: whether male or female, the condition is one — *and he is believer* — and the act — *does good* — and the result — *will enter Paradise*. Classical notes added that the *min* — from among good deeds — as partitive shows that not all good must be done by each, but whoever does among them with faith enters; the measure *naqīr* shows that even the smallest among them is not wronged. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book also claim by wish; here female and male alike are neither by wish but by belief and good.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Grace in Act Plus Faith**

Though only *“those who do good male or female and have faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck,”* the verse anchors grace where wishes were removed. Immediately after: *“who is better in faith than those who fully submit, do good, follow Abraham upright? God chose Abraham as close friend”* (4:125) — the model of submission. Immediately before: *whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly* (4:123) — the threat; now the promise with equal precision, secured by *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40). For the weak for whom burdens were lightened — the one who cannot marry free woman may marry believing bondwoman with faith known best to God (4:25) — this is the lightest of entries: belief and a good among goods, from whatever speck you can, and you will not be wronged a speck, because the One whose word none exceeds has promised entry and is the One who created you from a single soul and knows ties.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:125

> And who is better in faith than those who ˹fully˺ submit themselves to Allah, do good, and follow the Way of Abraham, the upright? Allah chose Abraham as a close friend.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Who Is Better in Faith Than Those Who Submit and Do Good**

The verse opens *wa man aḥsanu dīnan mimman aslama wajhahū li Allāhi wa huwa muḥsinun wa attabaʿa millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* — and who is better in faith, in religion, than those who fully submit their face, themselves, to God and are doers of good, and follow the Way of Abraham, the upright. *Man aḥsanu dīnan* — who is better in religion, in faith — was explained as rhetorical negation: none is better, as earlier *who is more truthful than God in speech?* (4:87, 4:122). *Aslama wajhahū li Allāhi* — submitted his face to God — was read as full submission, face as the noblest part and the direction of prayer, as the sūrah commands *“submit yourselves to God”* in trust. *Wa huwa muḥsin* — while being doer of good, beautiful in deed — was explained as *iḥsān* — doing good, making good, worship as if seeing — the same *muḥsin* who does charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114) and who does good male or female with faith (4:124). *Wa attabaʿa millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* — and follows the way, the creed, the community of Abraham, the upright, the inclining from crooked to straight — was read as the *ḥanīf* — pure monotheist who turns away from associators, as Abraham turned from his people’s female gods (4:117) and obeyed command without altering creation (4:119). The three — submission, goodness, following Abraham pure — were explained as the sūrah’s definition of best *dīn*, against wishes that claimed grace by belonging (4:123) and against taking Satan as guardian instead of God (4:119).

**The Way of Abraham the Upright**

The phrase *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* was explained with history. *Millah* — way, creed, path — was read as the path God made clear as noble ways of those before you (4:26), which Abraham exemplifies. *Ḥanīf* — upright, inclining, pure — was explained as one who inclines from associating (4:116) to the Single, as Abraham was not of the associators (6:161) and was tested with commands and fulfilled them (2:124). The sūrah has said that the People of the Book claim wishes yet some distort words (4:46, 4:153) and that the Qur’an came confirming your scriptures (4:47); following Abraham *ḥanīf* was read as return to the common monotheism before distortions, where invocation is only of God, not female gods nor Satan (4:117). The Way of Abraham was also linked to *“We have given descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom and great authority”* (4:54) and to *“He chose Abraham as close friend”* here — Abraham’s way is not tribal claim but submitted face and beautiful deed, the same *islām* that began from a single soul’s creation (4:1) and that remains spacious as earth’s havens (4:100).

**And God Chose Abraham as Close Friend**

The seal *wa attakhadha Allāhu Ibrāhīma khalīlā* — and God chose, took, Abraham as a close friend, intimate — was explained as *khalīl* — close friend, bosom friend, the one whose love interpenetrates — *khullah* — the heart’s core. *Ittakhadha* — took — was read as divine choosing, not human claiming; the sūrah has said that God elevates whomever He wills and knows who deserves favour (4:49, 4:70), and that *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131–132), so friendship is by His taking, not by wish. The title *khalīl* was explained with reports that Abraham’s hospitality, steadfastness after being thrown into fire, and his plea for forgiveness for his father even after being shown enmity, showed the face submitted; God’s taking him as *khalīl* is therefore not an inherited status but a response to *aslama wajhahū wa huwa muḥsin* — submitted and did good. Classical notes mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ said *“had I taken a *khalīl* among you I would have taken Abū Bakr, but your companion is God’s *khalīl*”* (Bukhārī 466, Muslim 2383, similar), showing the station’s uniqueness, yet the verse invites emulation: whoever submits and does good and follows that *ḥanīf* way is best in *dīn*.

**A Verse That Answers Wishes With Abraham’s Submission**

Placed after *those who do good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck* (4:124) and before *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware* (4:126), this verse answers wishes with Abraham’s submission. The sūrah removed *“neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book, whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) and gave Paradise by belief and good without wrong (4:124); now it asks *who is better than the submitter, the doer of good, the follower of Abraham ḥanīf?* — answer: none. The sūrah has shown Satan’s path — defying the Messenger after guidance (4:115), associating far astray (4:116), invoking females/Satan (4:117), cursed taking share (4:118), ordering cutting and altering (4:119), promising only delusion (4:120) — versus God’s path — Book in truth (4:105), wisdom taught (4:113), no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114); Abraham is the human embodiment of God’s path, who left his people’s idols, submitted face to fire, and was made *khalīl*. For the weak this is an accessible model: best *dīn* is not speculation about wishes but submission of face, beautification of deed, and following the upright way whose owner owns heavens and earth.

**The Close Friend Whose Way Is the Believers’ Path**

The phrase *sabili al-muʾminīn* — path of the believers (4:115) — was linked here to *millata Ibrāhīma*: the believers’ path is Abraham’s *ḥanīf* way where defiance after clarity is refused. The sūrah that warns not to take disbelievers as allies for honour (4:139, 4:144) and declares hypocrites in lowest depth (4:145) makes Abraham the criterion: his alliance was with the Single, his honour was *khalīl* taken by Him. The verse generalises the judgment chapter’s lesson where grace preserved the Prophet from being deceived (4:113): the preservation came via Book and wisdom teaching what he did not know; Abraham’s preservation came via *ḥanīf* submission. Both say: best faith is submitted face, goodness, and upright way, taken as friend by the One to whom all belongs. The next verse will seal that ownership: to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, and He is Fully Aware of everything (4:126).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:126

> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is Fully Aware of everything.

**Expanded Commentary**

**To God Alone Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth**

The verse states *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God, for God, belongs whatever, all that, is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — whatever is in heavens and on earth — was explained as absolute ownership: angels nearest to Him who would never be too proud to be servants (4:172), the Messiah a servant not too proud (4:172), the single soul spread into humanity (4:1), the orphans’ wealth held as trust (4:2, 4:10), the women whose dowries are gracious (4:4), the inheritance shares appointed (4:11–12), the earth made spacious for emigration (4:100), the prayer shortened on travel (4:101), and the promise true whose abode is Gardens or Hell (4:122, 4:121). *Li Allāhi* — to Him, for Him — was read as exclusive belonging, as the sūrah repeats *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:131, 4:132, 4:170) to bracket the passage on women, reconciliation, and trusteeship. The phrase was explained as the reply to invoking female gods besides Him (4:117) — they belong to Him, not beside Him — and to taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119) — the guardian taken belongs to Him, cursed (4:118). The sūrah has said that the People of the Book claim wishes yet grace is not by wishes (4:123), that Abraham was taken as close friend (4:125) — friendship with the Owner of all is the highest honour — and that whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both worlds’ rewards (4:134); ownership here is the ground of those promises.

**And God Is Fully Aware of Everything**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin muḥīṭā* — And God is Fully Aware, Encompassing, of everything, of every thing — was explained as *muḥīṭ* — encompassing, encircling, comprehending — the same name that sealed night plotting in His presence — *He is Fully Aware of what they do* (4:108) — now universalised to *bi kulli shayʾ* — of everything. *Bi kulli shayʾin* — of every thing — was read as covering the heavens and earth just said to belong to Him, the charity and kindness and reconciliation commanded (4:114), the dispute judged by what He shows (4:105), the good male or female with faith (4:124), and the speck not wronging (*naqīrā* — 4:124) and the atom not wronging (4:40). The sūrah has sealed knowledge diversely — All-Knowing, All-Wise where sin is earned (4:111), All-Hearing, All-Seeing where trusts are judged (4:58), All-Aware of what you do where verification was commanded (4:94), *Muḥīṭ* where night hides (4:108) — here *Muḥīṭ* of everything gathers them: nothing escapes perimeter because everything belongs. Early notes linked *muḥīṭ* to spaciousness: earth was said to be spacious (4:97, 4:100), yet His awareness is more spacious, encompassing the spacious.

**A Verse That Follows Best Faith With Ownership**

Placed after *who is better than those who submit, do good, follow Abraham ḥanīf, God took Abraham as friend* (4:125), this verse follows best faith with ownership that makes friendship intelligible. Abraham was taken as *khalīl* by the One to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth; his *millah ḥanīf* was submission to the Owner, not to the female gods who themselves belong to Him and are invoked only as Satan’s share (4:117–118). The sūrah has said *God suffices as Guardian and Helper* (4:45), *God is sufficient as Trustee* (4:81, 4:132), *God is sufficient as Witness* (4:79); to say *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* is to say guardianship, help, trusteeship, and witnessing are His by right of ownership. Where the sūrah taught that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114), ownership as *muḥīṭ* explains why judging by what He shows and seeking His pleasure succeeds: the Show-er and the Pleasure-owner owns and encompasses.

**The Belonging That Makes Oaths and Treaties Possible**

The sūrah repeats *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* as oath-ground for contracts the chapter has detailed: the firm commitment of marriage — *mīthāq ghalīẓ* — taken from women (4:21), the treaty — *mīthāq* — with covenanted peoples whose blood-money is delivered even when mistaken (4:92) and whose allies are excepted from hostility (4:90), and the single soul’s tie that makes family honour a due (4:1). To say all belongs to Him is to say oaths sworn by Him have owner as witness — *God is sufficient as Witness* (4:79) — and trustee — *God is sufficient as Trustee* (4:132). The sūrah has shown that those who trade a portion for misguidance and who believe in *jibt* (4:51) think oaths belong to other lords; this verse returns every *mā* — whatever — to the One whose earth is spacious and whose promise is ever true, so that settlement between spouses (4:128) and reconciliation between people (4:114) hold because the Holder holds all.

**Ownership That Makes Wishes Void and Promises True**

The pairing — *to Him belongs* and *He encompasses everything* — was explained as making *“neither by your wishes”* (4:123) void and *“God’s promise ever true, whose word more truthful?”* (4:122) true. Wishes do not move ownership; promise from the Owner does. The sūrah has moved from two abodes — Hell without escape (4:121) and Gardens forever true (4:122) — through the law of wishes, through the entry of doers of good with faith not wronged a speck (4:124), through best faith as submission to Owner and following Abraham whom Owner took as friend — to the Owner’s declaration that all belongs and all is encompassed. For the weak for whom burdens were lightened, the declaration is lightening: the One to whom your weak *ḥīlah* and *sabīl* were unknown to others (4:98) is the One who owns heavens and earth and encompasses, so your helplessness hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and your emigration where you find many havens (4:100) and your prayer shortened (4:101) are under the same Ownership. The next passage will use that ownership to teach about women: they ask regarding women, say He instructs you regarding them, instruction already revealed concerning orphan women deprived yet wished to marry, helpless children, orphans’ rights, and whatever good you do is well known to Him (4:127).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:127

> They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding women. Say, “It is Allah Who instructs you regarding them. Instruction has ˹already˺ been revealed in the Book concerning the orphan women you deprive of their due rights but still wish to marry, also helpless children, as well as standing up for orphans’ rights. And whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”

**Expanded Commentary**

**They Ask You Regarding Women — God Instructs**

The verse states *wa yastaftūnaka fī al-nisāʾi quli Allāhu yuftīkum fīhinna* — they ask you, they seek your ruling, regarding women — say, God instructs you, gives ruling, regarding them. *Yastaftūnaka* — to seek *fatwā*, ruling — was explained as the community asking the Prophet ﷺ about women’s rights, as earlier at the chapter’s start they were taught to marry orphan women with justice or marry others two, three, four where justice is feared (4:3), to give dowries graciously (4:4), and to return orphans’ property with witnesses (4:6). *Quli Allāhu yuftīkum fīhinna* — say, God gives ruling regarding them — was read as referral to the Owner to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and who is Fully Aware of everything (4:126); instruction is not by wishes (4:123) nor by Satan’s ordering to alter creation (4:119), but by the One who created from a single soul and spread men and women (4:1). The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent in truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and that wisdom was taught (4:113); here the Book judges between men and women as between peoples. Early reports linked the asking to questions about orphan girls under guardianship where the guardian desired to marry them without full dowry; the verse ties past instruction to present asking, showing a single instruction extended.

**Instruction Already Revealed — Orphan Women Deprived Yet Wished to Marry**

The reference *wa mā yutlā ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi fī yatāmā al-nisāʾi allātī lā tuʾtūnahunna mā kutiba lahunna wa targhabūna an tankiḥūhunna* — and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women you deprive — do not give — of what is prescribed, due, for them yet desire to marry them — was explained as the earlier ruling in 4:3 — *if you fear not to be just to orphan women, marry other women* — and in 4:19–21 — *not to inherit women against will and firm commitment*. *Mā kutiba lahunna* — what is prescribed, written for them — was read as dowry, inheritance, kind maintenance, the obligatory shares for women whether little or much (4:7). *Targhabūna an tankiḥūhunna* — you desire to marry them — was explained with two inclinations: *targhabūna fīhinna* — desire to marry the beautiful or wealthy orphan for her property while depriving her right — and *targhabūna ʿanhunna* — desire against them, to leave them unmarried to keep their wealth — both of which the guardian might do; the sūrah pairs both as injustice. The instruction already recited — *mā yutlā* — was read as showing the Qur’an as ongoing recital: what was revealed at the start is re-cited as answer to new asking, so that the instruction about women is not new but the same justice extended.

**Also Helpless Children and Standing Up for Orphans’ Rights**

The continuation *wa al-mustaḍʿafīna mina al-wildāni wa an taqūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* — also helpless children, also that you stand up, establish, for orphans with justice — was explained as the same inclusive justice seen where men, women, children were named for pardon and haven (4:98, 4:75). *Mustaḍʿafīn mina al-wildān* — helpless among children, deemed weak children — were those without guardian, whose shares hypocrites might diminish. *Wa an taqūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* — and that you stand up for orphans with equity, with justice, with the balance — was read as the command to *return trusts, judge fairly* (4:58) applied to orphans as the prime trust: the sūrah that warns against devouring orphans’ wealth as fire in bellies (4:10) and that commands to test orphans until judicious then return property with witnesses (4:6) here generalizes: stand up — *qūmū* — as you stand for prayer at appointed time (4:103) and for justice though against yourselves (4:135). The sūrah has said that God is sufficient as Witness and Trustee (4:132, 4:79); to stand for orphans *bi al-qisṭ* is to stand with Him as witness.

**And Whatever Good You Do Is Well Known to God**

The seal *wa mā tafʿalū min khayrin fa inna Allāha kāna bihī ʿalīmā* — and whatever good you do, of good, then indeed God is, was ever, All-Knowing of it — was explained as the encouragement matching the warning. *Mā tafʿalū min khayr* — whatever good you do — was read as the good commanded for secret talks — charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) — and the good of submitting face to Him doing good as Abraham (4:125) and the good male or female with faith entering Paradise without wrong of speck (4:124). *Fa inna Allāha kāna bihī ʿalīmā* — He is All-Knowing of it — was explained as that He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and is Fully Aware of everything knows the speck of good as He knows the speck not wronged (*naqīrā* — 4:124) and does not wrong even an atom but multiplies (4:40). The sūrah has said *“you do not know who is more beneficial”* among parents and children (4:11); here *He* knows the good done for orphan women deprived yet desired, for helpless children, for orphans stood for. For the weak this is the promise: good for the weakest — the orphan girl, the helpless child — is the most known.

**A Verse That Follows Ownership With Instruction for the Weakest**

Placed after *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware* (4:126), this verse follows ownership with instruction for the weakest owned: women asked about. The sūrah that opened by creation from a single soul and honouring ties (4:1) and that will say humans are ever inclined to selfishness yet gracious mindfulness is All-Aware (4:128) here says: the One to whom all belongs instructs you regarding them, and instruction already recited about orphan women and helpless children is that you give what is prescribed or marry others with justice, and stand for orphans with equity. The circle closes where the sūrah began with orphans’ wealth and marriage justice (4:2–4); the question reopens it, and the answer cites the earlier verses as still recited, still ruling, so that the chapter’s ethic — return trusts, judge fairly, verify reports, be sure before fighting, do not advocate for deceit — is again applied to the household. The next verses will apply that ethic within marriage: if a woman fears indifference or neglect, no blame to seek settlement which is best, though humans incline to selfishness, yet gracious mindfulness is All-Aware (4:128).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:128

> If a woman fears indifference or neglect from her husband, there is no blame on either of them if they seek ˹fair˺ settlement, which is best. Humans are ever inclined to selfishness. But if you are gracious and mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

**Expanded Commentary**

**If a Woman Fears Indifference or Neglect — No Blame to Seek Settlement**

The verse opens *wa in imraʾatun khāfat min baʿlihā nushūzan aw iʿrāḍā fa lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā an yuṣliḥā baynahumā ṣulḥā* — and if a woman fears, anticipates, from her husband perverseness, rising — *nushūz* — or neglect, turning away — *iʿrāḍ* — then no blame upon them both to seek, to effect, settlement, reconciliation between them, a settlement. *Khāfat* — feared — was explained as sensed, apprehended, with signs, as earlier *if you fear ill conduct* from women advice and measures were given (4:34) and *if you anticipate a split appoint mediators* (4:35) — fear here is the moral perception that precedes action, not mere anxiety. *Nushūz* — rising, perverseness, elevation — was read as the husband’s rising above, being high, refusing right; *iʿrāḍ* — turning aside, neglect — as withdrawal, not sharing bed, not intending, leaving hanging (4:129). *Fa lā junāḥa ʿalayhimā* — no blame upon them both — was explained as the law’s lightening where shortening prayer carries no blame (4:101), where laying aside weapons in rain carries no blame though precaution remains (4:102), and where standing for orphans must be with justice (4:127) — here settlement carries no sin nor blame. *An yuṣliḥā baynahumā ṣulḥā* — to reconcile between them with settlement — was read as any fair adjustment: she waives part of maintenance or night in exchange for keeping marriage, he returns kindness; early reports illustrated it with Sawdah bint Zamʿah offering her day to ʿĀʾishah to remain married to the Prophet ﷺ, accepted without blame. The sūrah has said that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking God’s pleasure (4:114); settlement is that reconciliation.

**Settlement — Which Is Best**

The affirmation *wa al-ṣulḥu khayr* — and settlement, reconciliation, is best, is good, is better — was explained as the sūrah’s maxim for dispute. *Al-ṣulḥ* — settlement — was read as the peace that mends, the *iṣlāḥ bayna al-nāsi* commanded as good secret talk (4:114) and as the mediators’ goal (4:35). *Khayr* — best, good — was explained as better than splitting where the woman fears *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* yet a fair settlement keeps ties honoured (4:1), as the single soul’s creation spread into families whose ties are to be honoured. The phrase was linked to *“appoint a mediator from his family and hers, if they desire reconciliation God will bring harmony”* (4:35): settlement is not the enemy of justice but its embodiment where justice is equity plus mercy. The sūrah has said humans crave what God gave some over others (4:32) and that burdens are lightened because weak (4:28); to prefer settlement where the alternative is hanging is to prefer the light, kind path where the writ of prayer still holds at fixed time (4:103). Classical notes added that *al-ṣulḥu khayr* is general: wherever reconciliation is possible, it is best, provided rights prescribed for orphan women (4:127) are not voided.

**Humans Are Ever Inclined to Selfishness**

The diagnostic *wa uḥḍirat al-anfusu al-shuḥḥ* — and selves, souls, were made present with, brought with, selfishness, stinginess, avarice — was explained as human inclination. *Uḥḍirat* — made present, brought close, kept at hand — was read as that stinginess is brought to the soul, attends it, is ever present, as *“humankind was created weak”* (4:28) and *“God does not like the stingy who withhold bounty”* (4:37). *Shuḥḥ* — selfishness, stinginess, grasping — was explained as the soul’s holding onto its share, its night, its wealth, its right, unwilling to concede where settlement requires waiving. The sūrah has shown stinginess promoting stinginess among people (4:37), and Satan’s *mā dūna* forgiveness (4:116) requires hope not delusion; here *shuḥḥ* is the barrier to settlement: each side fears losing. To name *shuḥḥ* was read as the Book’s realism before its idealism: settlement is best, yet selves are brought with selfishness, so settlement needs graciousness and mindfulness to overcome what is present with souls. The same selfishness was seen where dowry taken unjustly is sought back (4:20) and where the lagger wishes gain without risk (4:73).

**But If You Are Gracious and Mindful — God Is All-Aware**

The encouragement *wa in tuḥsinū wa tattaqū fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — but if you do good, act graciously, beautifully, and are mindful of God, then indeed God was ever All-Aware of what you do — was explained with *tuḥsinū* — to do *iḥsān*, to be gracious, to do good beautifully — the same *muḥsin* who submits face and does good following Abraham (4:125) and who does good male or female with faith (4:124). *Wa tattaqū* — and are mindful, God-wary — was read as the sūrah’s *taqwā* that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and that seals settlement between spouses (4:129) — if you do what is right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. *Fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — He is Ever Aware of what you do — was explained as that He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and knows whatever good you do (4:127) is aware of the settlement sought, of the selfishness present, of the graciousness where offered. The sūrah has sealed knowledge diversely — *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* where sin is earned (4:111), *Muḥīṭ* where night plots (4:108), *Khabīr* where verification was commanded (4:94) — here *Khabīr* fits act: He is aware of what you do in settlement where your doing is waiving and being gracious.

**A Verse That Follows Instruction for Orphans With Instruction for Wives**

Placed after instruction for orphan women deprived and helpless children (4:127), this verse follows that instruction with settlement where a wife fears rising or turning away. The sūrah that began with limits of marriage — two, three, four where justice is feared else one (4:3) — returns to marriage limits at the other end: you will never be able to be just between wives even if keen (4:129). Between those limits is this middle path — settlement is best — where the human soul’s *shuḥḥ* is named as ever present, yet graciousness and mindfulness are the act that God, All-Aware, sees. For the weak this is protective: the woman who fears *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* is not told the faith is divorce alone; no blame to seek settlement that keeps marriage with adjusted rights, and for either to be gracious and mindful is best. The next verse will state the limit of justice between wives and the ethic of inclining not wholly — do not leave the other hanging — and if you do right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful (4:129).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:129

> You will never be able to maintain ˹emotional˺ justice between your wives—no matter how keen you are. So do not totally incline towards one leaving the other in suspense. And if you do what is right and are mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

**Expanded Commentary**

**You Will Never Be Able to Be Just Between Wives Even If Keen**

The verse states *wa lan tastaṭīʿū an taʿdilū bayna al-nisāʾi wa law ḥaraṣtum* — and you will never be able, you will not be capable, to be just, equitable, even, between women — wives — even if you are keen, eager, desirous. *Lan tastaṭīʿū* — never be able — was explained as incapacity in emotional justice — *ḥubb*, inclination of heart, inclination that cannot be weighed — even where legal justice — maintenance, night, kindness — is possible. *An taʿdilū* — to be just, to equalise — was read as to make equal in love, in inclination, in the heart’s turning, which the sūrah elsewhere shows even the Prophet’s heart inclined where he was taught to say *“O God, this is my division where I have control; do not blame me where I do not”* (Abū Dāwūd 2134, graded ḥasan). *Wa law ḥaraṣtum* — even if you are keen, even with eagerness — was explained as that keenness does not create capacity where God created inclination unequal, as humanity was created weak (4:28) and *shuḥḥ* — selfishness — is ever present with souls (4:128). The sūrah has shown that marriage limits — two, three, four where justice is feared else one (4:3) — assume justice as condition; here the condition is refined: legal justice remains commanded, emotional equality is declared impossible, so that the one who cannot equalise love is not told the faith is divorce, but is taught how to incline.

**So Do Not Incline Entirely, Leaving the Other Suspended**

The command *fa lā tamīlū kulla al-mayli fa tadharūhā ka al-muʿallaqah* — so do not incline, lean, entirely, with total inclining, so that you leave her as the suspended, hanging — was explained with *mayl* — inclination, leaning, bias — the same *mayl* the hostile wished you deviate — *mayl ʿaẓīmā* — greatly (4:27) and where night plotting wished you neglect for a sweep — *maylatan wāḥidah* (4:102). *Kulla al-mayli* — entirely of inclination — was read as total turning to one and away from another: not sharing nights, not providing, not speaking, so that the wife remains *muʿallaqah* — suspended, hanging — neither married in full nor divorced free, as if tied to a rope without ground. *Fa tadharūhā ka al-muʿallaqah* — so you leave her as the hanging one — was explained as the sūrah’s protection of the wife who earlier feared *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* (4:128): the remedy there was settlement where both sought it, which is best; here the remedy is prohibition of total inclining that creates the hanging. The sūrah elsewhere says *“do not incline towards one leaving the other in suspense”* is the counterpart to *“be mindful of God”* where settlement was taught with *shuḥḥ* present (4:128); not to incline entirely is to practice *taqwā* where love cannot be equal.

**And If You Do What Is Right and Are Mindful — He Is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful**

The encouragement *wa in tuṣliḥū wa tattaqū fa inna Allāha kāna Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — and if you set right, reconcile, do good, and are mindful, then indeed God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, was ever — was explained with *tuṣliḥū* — to set right, to reconcile, to do good — the same *iṣlāḥ* as reconciliation between people (4:114) and mediators desiring reconciliation (4:35) and settlement best (4:128). *Wa tattaqū* — and are mindful, God-wary — was read as the sūrah’s *taqwā* that began with mindfulness of the Lord who created from single soul (4:1) and that seals every marriage rule: where emotional justice is impossible yet legal justice is commanded, mindfulness and setting right cover the shortfall. *Fa inna Allāha kāna Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful — was explained as the Seal that excuses what you cannot equalise while holding you to what you can — not to incline entirely. Where the intentional killer was sealed with anger and curse (4:93) and the self-wronger with not loved (4:107), the husband who cannot equalise love yet does not incline totally and is gracious and mindful is sealed with forgiveness and mercy. The same pair sealed the fear that settlement requires graciousness where *shuḥḥ* is present (4:128) with awareness — *Khabīr* — here with mercy, matching the earlier limit of justice where the sūrah says *“do not crave what God gave some over others; ask Him for bounty”* (4:32): what you cannot equalise, seek from His forgiveness.

**A Verse That Places Limit Beside Permission**

Placed after settlement is best where she fears *nushūz* or turning away and selves were made present with *shuḥḥ* (4:128), this verse places limit beside permission. The sūrah permitted settlement waiving part of right to keep marriage; here it acknowledges that perfect equalising of hearts after settlement remains impossible. The two verses together teach the household ethic after the public ethic of judging by Book (4:105) and most secret talks (4:114): private settlement is best, yet private hearts remain unequal, so do not make inequality total. The sūrah has shown that the owner of heavens and earth is Fully Aware of everything (4:126) and Whatever good you do is well known to Him (4:127); He knows the inclination you cannot weigh and He is All-Forgiving for it where you do not incline entirely and you set right and are mindful. For the weak this is protective: the wife suspended — *muʿallaqah* — is named as a wrong to be avoided, as orphan women deprived were protected from being married for profit (4:3, 4:127); protection is by prohibition of total inclining.

**The Incline That the Sūrah Has Named Two Kinds**

The word *mayl* was traced: the hostile wish you incline greatly from God’s way (4:27) is one *mayl* — away from Him; the husband’s incline totally to one wife leaving the other suspended is the other *mayl* — within what He permitted — between wives. The first *mayl* is prohibited absolutely — do not follow desires to deviate — the second is limited — do not incline entirely. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by desire and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) here warns that even lawful love can become unlawful neglect where it is total. The medicine is the sūrah’s general medicine after exposing night plotting and throwing sin — *whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving* (4:110) — here expressed as *if you set right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful*. The next verse will set the other face: if they separate, He will enrich both from His bounties, and He is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise (4:130), so that staying with settlement and leaving with enrichment are both under mercy.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:130

> But if they choose to separate, Allah will enrich both of them from His bounties. And Allah is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise.

**Expanded Commentary**

**But If They Separate — He Will Enrich Both**

The verse states *wa in yatafarraqā yughni Allāhu kullan min saʿatihī* — but if they two separate, become separate, part, God will enrich, make free of need, each from His bounty, His spaciousness, His abundance. *Yatafarraqā* — to separate, to split, to become distinct — was explained as divorce or separation after settlement was best (4:128) yet total inclining was prohibited (4:129) — where remaining together in hanging was not chosen and settlement could not hold. *Yughni* — to enrich, to suffice, to make independent — was read as God making each free of need where the other was expected to suffice, as the emigrant finds many havens and abundance where earth is spacious (4:100) and as the prayer shortened on travel is still writ at fixed time (4:103). *Kullan* — each, both, every one — was explained as each — the man and the woman — not only the husband upon whom maintenance lay nor only the wife who feared *nushūz* or *iʿrāḍ* (4:128); both are enriched. *Min saʿatihī* — from His spaciousness, His bounty, His amplitude — was explained as from His wide provision, the same *saʿah* as *murāgham kathīr wa saʿah* — many havens and spaciousness — promised to the emigrant (4:100), and as *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) whose spaciousness is the source. Early reports linked the verse to the household where settlement with waiver and reconciliation was offered yet separation was chosen: no shame in separation where enrichment is promised to both from Him.

**From His Bounties — Min Saʿatihī**

The phrase *min saʿatihī* was explained as from His amplitude that does not narrow when given, as the sūrah says *“ask God for His bounties; God has perfect knowledge of all things”* (4:32) where craving what others have is forbidden — here bounty is given to both from His bounty, not from taking between them. *Saʿah* — spaciousness — was read as breadth of provision, of dwelling, of tranquillity, of replacement — spouse, household, sustenance — as the sūrah says the single soul spread into countless men and women (4:1) showing that earth’s spaciousness holds replacements. The contrast with *shuḥḥ* — selfishness ever present with souls (4:128) — was noted: where settlement failed because *shuḥḥ* kept each grasping, separation enriched from *saʿah* removes grasping by giving each from Him, not by stripping one. Where the sūrah warns there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), separation where graciousness and mindfulness remain is itself counted as good where it removes hanging — *muʿallaqah* (4:129) — and enrichment from *saʿah* is the broad good that follows.

**And God Is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Wāsiʿan Ḥakīmā* — And God is Ever-Bountiful, Ever-Encompassing, All-Wise — was explained as suitability. *Wāsiʿ* — Wide, Bountiful, Encompassing, Spacious — was read as whose bounty is wide enough to enrich both without diminishing, as He is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126), and as earth is spacious for emigration (4:97). *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — was explained as wisdom that legislates both staying — settlement best (4:128) with prohibition of total inclining (4:129) — and leaving — enrichment from bounty where they separate — each in its wisdom, as He is All-Knowing, All-Wise where sin is earned (4:111) and where pursuit is without faltering (4:104). The sūrah has shown that God wills to make clear, to guide to noble ways, to turn in mercy, and is All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:26–28); to be *Wāsiʿ Ḥakīm* here is to be the One whose spaciousness is guided by wisdom: not enrichment that encourages frivolous divorce, but enrichment where settlement was tried and hanging remained. The two names together show that separation is not failure of law but a provision within law made by the Wide in wisdom.

**A Verse That Follows Limit With Provision**

Placed after *you will never be able to be just between wives even if keen, so do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended, yet if you set right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving* (4:129), this verse follows limit with provision. The sūrah’s ethic for the household mirrors its ethic for the battlefield: many havens where emigration is chosen (4:100), shortening where travel and fear constrict (4:101), guarding where the enemy wishes neglect for a sweep (4:102), remembrance in all postures (4:103) — here many enrichments where separation is chosen after trying settlement. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to follow other than believers’ path (4:115) does not bind spouses to hanging as piety; it says separation enriched from His bounty is better than hanging, as settlement is better than *nushūz*. For the weak this is the lightest of provisions: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement with waiving was offered, if the tie still cannot be lived without total inclining, He will suffice both from His wide bounty.

**The Wide Who Can Replace Without Diminishing**

The verb *yughni* — to enrich, to suffice — was linked to *“ask God for His bounties”* (4:32) and to *“with Him are rewards of this world and the Hereafter”* (4:134): the enrichment promised here is not a vague hope but a writ from the Wide. Classical notes added that *kullan min saʿatihī* — each from His bounty — proves that provision is not zero-sum between the two who part: His *saʿah* gives to each separately, as *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126) — so that the woman enriched is not enriched at man’s expense before God, though inter-human rights remain judged fairly as the Book judges (4:105, 4:135). The next passage will anchor that bounty in universal ownership: to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, We have commanded those given Scripture before you and you to be mindful, if you disobey to Him still belongs all, and He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:131

> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, We have commanded those given the Scripture before you, as well as you, to be mindful of Allah. But if you disobey, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy.

**Expanded Commentary**

**To God Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth — Commanded to Be Mindful**

The verse opens *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — repeated from 4:126 and to be repeated at 4:132, bracketing the passage on settlement and enrichment. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — whatever is in heavens and on earth — was explained as absolute ownership encompassing the single soul spread into humanity (4:1), the orphans’ trusts (4:2), the dowries (4:4), the inheritance shares (4:11–12), the earth made spacious (4:100), the wives between whom justice cannot be perfected (4:129) yet whose separation is enriched from His bounty (4:130). *Wa la qad waṣṣaynā alladhīna ūtū al-kitāba min qablikum wa iyyākum ani ittaqū Allāh* — and indeed We have commanded, enjoined, charged those given Scripture before you, as well as you, to be mindful of God — was explained as universal *waṣiyyah* — counsel, charge — the same mindfulness that began the sūrah — *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) — and that seals settlement — *“if you are gracious and mindful God is All-Aware”* (4:128) — and seals not inclining entirely — *“if you set right and are mindful He is All-Forgiving”* (4:129). To command those given Scripture before you and you was read as continuity: the Scriptures before and the Qur’an enjoin the same *taqwā*, as *“We have given descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom and great authority”* (4:54) and *“He taught you what you did not know, great is His favour”* (4:113) — the teaching is one.
