**But If You Disobey — To Him Still Belongs All**

The condition *wa in takfurū fa inna li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — but if you disobey, if you disbelieve, are ungrateful, then indeed to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth — was explained as the sūrah’s reminder that mindfulness is not need of the Owner. *In takfurū* — if you disbelieve, are ungrateful — was read as including both creedal disbelief that association brings (4:116) and practical *kufrān* — ingratitude — as withholding trust, inclining totally leaving the other suspended (4:129), devouring wealth unjustly (4:29), or claiming wishes as grace (4:123). *Fa inna li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — then to Him still belongs all — was explained as that disobedience does not reduce His ownership: the spaciousness that enriched both after separation (4:130) remains, the Gardens promised true (4:122) remain, the Hell without escape (4:121) remains under His dominion. The sūrah has said *“you desire world’s reward, with Him are rewards of this world and Hereafter”* (4:134) — to disobey is to refuse the *taqwā* that would have obtained both. The clause was linked to *“whoever defies the Messenger after guidance and follows other than believers’ path We let pursue what he chose then burn”* (4:115): letting pursue does not transfer ownership; Hell to which he is burned still belongs to Him, as Gardens do.

**And God Is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Ghaniyyan Ḥamīdā* — And God is Self-Sufficient, free of need, Rich, and Praiseworthy, ever praised — was explained with *Ghanī* — Rich, Independent, Free of need — and *Ḥamīd* — Praised, Praiseworthy — the same pair where hypocrites are warned for taking disbelievers as allies seeking honour through that company — *surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139). To be *Ghanī* was read as that His command to be mindful is not for His need but for servants’ good: He does not need their *taqwā*, as earth’s spacious havens (4:100) were given not because He needed emigrants but because they needed refuge. *Ḥamīd* — Praiseworthy — was explained as that He is praised though they disobey, as the sūrah says *“to Him belongs all in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126) — praise belongs to the Fully Aware who measures even the speck not wronged (*naqīrā* — 4:124). The two names together show that mindfulness — *ittaqū Allāh* — enriches the mindful, not the Praised Self-Sufficient; and ungratefulness — *takfurū* — impoverishes the ungrateful, not the Rich.

**A Verse That Brackets Settlement With Ownership and Command**

Placed after enrichment from His bounty where they separate and He is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise (4:130), this verse brackets settlement with ownership and universal command. The sūrah has moved from orphan women deprived yet desired, helpless children, orphans stood for with justice well known to Him (4:127) → wife fearing *nushūz* or turning away, settlement best though selves were made present with *shuḥḥ* yet graciousness and mindfulness are ever known (4:128) → impossibility of perfect emotional justice, prohibition of total inclining leaving hanging, setting right and mindfulness forgiven (4:129) → separation enriched from His spaciousness (4:130) — here to ground all in *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful, if you disobey to Him still belongs all, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy*. The sūrah that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* returns to *be mindful* as its abiding *waṣiyyah* for every Scripture people. For the weak this is the lightest of commands: where total justice between wives was declared impossible, mindfulness remains possible, and where separation was given, mindfulness remains the charge whose Keeper needs nothing and whose praise remains though you disobey.

**The *Waṣiyyah* That Survives Disobedience**

The phrase *wa la qad waṣṣaynā* — We have commanded, surely — was explained as a covenantal charge that survives disobedience, because ownership survives disobedience. Where the deceitful hide from people but He is with them where they plot displeasing speech (4:108) and where night plotting seems to succeed in this life but not before Him on the Day (4:109), the *waṣiyyah* to be mindful is the daylight that night cannot void, because the Night’s owner is the One commanded mindfulness. The verse generalises the household law into cosmology: the same heavens and earth that belong to Him contain both the single soul spread (4:1) and the many havens for emigration (4:100), the prayer at fixed writ (4:103) and the two abodes true (4:121–122); to be mindful within them is to live inside ownership that is Self-Sufficient yet Praiseworthy, so that obedience adds no need and disobedience subtracts nothing except from the disobedient.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:132

> To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs.

**Expanded Commentary**

**To God Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth — Again**

The verse restates *wa li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — and to God belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — the third repetition after 4:126 and 4:131, sealing the passage on women, settlement, enrichment, and universal *waṣiyyah* to be mindful. *Mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* was explained to include the same all as before: the single soul and its mate (4:1), the orphans’ wealth, the dowries, the shares, the earth spacious for haven (4:100), the wives between whom inclination is limited (4:129) yet each enriched from His bounty upon separation (4:130), and the heavens under which the fear prayer was ranked with vigilance (4:102). To repeat ownership thrice was read as emphasis after law: where the chapter legislates for the weakest — the orphan girl deprived yet desired (4:127), the wife fearing *nushūz* where settlement is best (4:128), the hanging not left (4:129) — the Legislation is grounded in Ownership, so that no wish (4:123) and no Satanic order to slit and alter (4:119) can claim title. The sūrah has said that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); to judge by that showing is to judge within His ownership, as witnesses for justice though against yourselves (4:135). Early reports noted that the Meccan assignment of daughters as female gods besides Him (4:117) and the claim of Satan’s appointed share (4:118) are both answered here: they belong to Him.

**And God Is Sufficient as Trustee of Affairs**

The seal *wa kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* — And God is sufficient, enough, as Trustee, as *Wakīl*, as Disposer of affairs, Agent — was explained with *wakīl* — trustee, agent, defender, disposer — the same *wakīl* asked about on the Day — *who will be their *wakīl*?* (4:109) — and the *wakīl* the Prophet ﷺ was told to trust — *“put trust in God, God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:81) after turning away from night contradictors. *Kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* was read as that His trusteeship suffices for every affair where spouses fear, orphans are stood for, emigrants seek haven, prayers guard. The sūrah has sealed trusteeship diversely: sufficient as Guardian and Helper (4:45), sufficient as Helper where He knows enemies (4:45), sufficient as Trustee after recording night schemes (4:81); here *sufficient as Trustee* fits ownership — because to Him belongs all, He suffices to dispose all. To take Him as *wakīl* was explained as entrusting affairs after doing what is incumbent: settlement sought (4:128), total inclining avoided (4:129), separation where needed enriched from His bounty (4:130), mindfulness kept where commanded (4:131). Where deceitful advocates seek to be *khaṣīm* for self-wrongers in this life (4:107–109) and find no *wakīl* on the Day for deceit, the believer who seeks settlement graciously finds the *Wakīl* who suffices.

**A Verse That Moves From Owner to Trustee**

Placed after *We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful, if you disobey to Him still belongs all, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131), this verse moves from Owner to Trustee. The sūrah bracketed settlement and enrichment between ownership and *taqwā*, now adds sufficiency: ownership without trusteeship would be awed but not approached; trusteeship says entrust. The sūrah has shown that those who put trust in Him and turn away from night contradictors are covered (4:81), that the emigrant who leaves home toward God and Messenger has reward secured upon Him (4:100), that the helpless hoped to be pardoned have *ʿAfuww Ghafūr* (4:99). To say *kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* is to say the same for every hanging not left and every settlement best: entrust, and He suffices. The sūrah has warned *“do not be advocate for the deceitful”* (4:105) and *“no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation”* (4:114); the *wakīl* who suffices is the secret talk’s better audience than people from whom deceit hides (4:108).

**Sufficiency That Makes Wishes Unnecessary and Promises True**

The pairing — *to Him belongs* and *He suffices as Trustee* — was explained as making *“neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book, whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) unnecessary to wish, and *“God’s promise ever true, whose word more truthful?”* (4:122) sufficient to trust. The sūrah has contrasted Satan’s promise only delusion (4:120) ending in Hell without escape (4:121) with God’s promise true ending in Gardens forever (4:122); to take the True Promiser as *wakīl* is to take the only promise that is not delusion as trustee. Where the sūrah says *“with Him are rewards of this world and Hereafter”* (4:134) for those who desire world’s reward, sufficiency as *wakīl* explains why both are with Him: He disposes both. For the weak this is direct: the orphan for whom you stand with justice (4:127), the wife suspended not left hanging (4:129), the both enriched after separation (4:130) — all are affairs whose *wakīl* suffices, so that you need not be hanging nor make another hanging, but can settle or part entrusted to the Sufficient.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Entrusting After Legislating**

Though only *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee,”* the verse anchors entrusting after legislating. The chapter has legislated from single soul to orphans to marriage to inheritance to trusts to prayer to judgment to charity to Abraham’s way, and here returns to its pillar: ownership grounds law, trusteeship executes it. The sūrah that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul and from it its mate”* (4:1) and that will say *“if He wills He can remove you and bring others, He is Most Capable”* (4:133) places between them this *wakīl* — sufficient — so that the creature who can be removed (4:133) and who can desire world’s reward (4:134) knows to whom affairs are entrusted where wishes fail and He remains.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:133

> If it is His Will, He can remove you altogether, O humanity, and replace you with others. And Allah is Most Capable to do so.

**Expanded Commentary**

**If He Will — He Can Remove You and Bring Others**

The verse states *in yashāʾ yudhhibkum ayyuhā al-nāsu wa yaʾti bi ākharīn* — if He wills, He can remove you, take you away altogether, O humanity, and bring others, replace you with others. *In yashāʾ* — if He wills, if it is His will — was explained with the will that governs ownership just declared — *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131, 4:132) — where *Wāsiʿ*, *Ghanī*, *Ḥamīd* show He does not need you. *Yudhhibkum* — to remove, to take away, to cause to go — was read as removal of generation, as He removes one people and brings another where *taqwā* is not kept. *Ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as address beyond the believers addressed for justice (4:135) to all, as the sūrah opened *“O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and here warns humanity that the single soul’s spread is not irreplaceable. *Wa yaʾti bi ākharīn* — and bring others, bring other peoples — was explained as replacement with those who are mindful where you disobey, as *“if you turn away He will replace you with another people then they will not be like you”* (47:38). Early reports illustrated *nas* here as the Meccans who invoked female gods besides Him (4:117) and took Satan as guardian (4:119); to tell them He can remove them is to tell them their claiming a share is not needed. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens where earth is spacious (4:100) — spaciousness that can receive others if you remain, and can do without you if you refuse.

**And God Is Most Capable to Do So**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿalā dhālika qadīrā* — And God is Most Capable, Powerful over that, to do that — was explained with *qadīr* — capable, powerful, measuring, determining — the One who created from single soul spread into countless (4:1) is capable to return spread to another spread. *ʿAlā dhālika* — over that, for that — removal and bringing — was read as that this is not threat only but capability, as *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) is measure, so *qadīr* over removal is measure of power. The sūrah has said He is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise where He enriches both after separation (4:130), Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy where mindfulness is commanded (4:131); to be Capable to remove is the power behind bounty and self-sufficiency: He enriches from His bounty because He can remove and bring without loss. Where the sūrah says *“with Him are rewards of this world and Hereafter”* (4:134) for those who desire world’s reward, capability to replace explains why both rewards are with Him — the Guardian and Helper sufficient (4:45) can give or withhold either.

**A Verse That Follows Trust With Warning**

Placed after *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee* (4:132) and before *whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both rewards* (4:134), this verse follows trust with warning that trust’s Sufficer can do without the entruster. The sūrah bracketed women’s law — settlement best (4:128), no total inclining (4:129), enrichment from bounty (4:130) — with universal *waṣiyyah* to be mindful (4:131) and ownership-trusteeship (4:132); now it warns *O humanity* that mindfulness is not for His need. The sūrah has warned *do not be advocate for deceit* (4:105), *no good in most secret talks* (4:114), *whoever defies the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose* (4:115); those are instances of a humanity that could be removed if it persists, as prior communities were. For the weak this is protective: the One who can remove humanity and bring others is the One who was hoped to pardon the helpless (4:99) and who gives many havens to the emigrant (4:100) — His capability to replace is the same capability to rescue, and to trust Him as *Wakīl* (4:132) where *He can* is to entrust to the Capable.

**Removal Not for His Need, but for Justice**

The address *ayyuhā al-nāsu* after two addresses *to those before you and you* to be mindful (4:131) was explained as broadening to all descendants of the single soul, reminding that the single soul’s lesson — ties are to be honoured — is the same mindfulness commanded. To say *He can remove you* after *He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* shows removal is not for need: the Self-Sufficient does not remove for lack, He removes for justice, as He let the defier pursue what he chose then burn (4:115) and made association far straying (4:116). The sūrah that warns *“stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves”* (4:135) makes humanity itself the witness here: if you do not stand, others will be brought who will. The verse generalises the sūrah’s replacement logic where *“with Him are rewards of both”* (4:134); desire for this world alone is answered not by giving the world alone, but by reminding that the World’s Owner can replace the desirer.

**A Short Verse That Makes Ownership Dynamic**

Though only *“if He wills He can remove you altogether and bring others, He is Most Capable,”* the verse makes ownership dynamic. The threefold *to Him belongs* — heavens and earth — was static — all is His; *He can remove and bring* is dynamic — He can do with His what wisdom wills. The sūrah that began with creation from single soul and spread, taught law for orphans, women, inheritance, trusts, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham, will now say *stand for justice* (4:135) to the humanity that can be removed: to stand for justice is to be the *ākharīn* — others — who are brought, not the removed. The next verse will set the choice of reward: whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both — so ask the Capable for both, not for little (4:134).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:134

> Whoever desires the reward of this world, then ˹let them know that˺ with Allah are the rewards of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Whoever Desires the Reward of This World — With Him Are Both**

The verse states *man kāna yurīdu thawāba al-dunyā fa ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* — whoever desires, wants, seeks the reward, wage, of this nearer world, then let them know, then with God — at His disposal — are the rewards of this world and the Hereafter, together. *Thawāb* — reward, return, recompense — was explained as wage for deed, as the sūrah has promised *thawāb* — fine reward — to both sitter with excuse and striver yet greater for striver (4:95–96), great reward for seeking His pleasure via charity and reconciliation (4:114), tremendous loss for taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119), and *yujza* — recompensed — for evil accordingly (4:123). *Yurīdu thawāba al-dunyā* — desires the world’s reward — was read as the shortcut: to act for world alone, as the lagger desired gain without sharing faith (4:73), as the denier of peace sought fleeting gain (4:94), as the wishers thought grace by wish (4:123). *Fa ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* — with Him are both — was explained as exclusive possession: both rewards are *ʿinda Allāh* — with Him, at His side, from His bounty — as *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) — so to desire world alone from other than Him is to seek little from the One who has much. *Wa* — and — joins the two: He has not divided them except where you divide desire; to ask Him is to obtain both, as the emigrant found many havens and abundance in earth (4:100) and the separator was enriched from His spaciousness (4:130) — world — while the believer hoping from Him finds forgiveness and mercy (4:96) — Hereafter.

**And God Is All-Hearing, All-Seeing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Samīʿan Baṣīrā* — And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, was ever — was explained with *Samīʿ* — hearing every wish, every secret talk, every advocacy in this life (4:109), every dispute judged by what He shows (4:105) — and *Baṣīr* — seeing every act, every inclination not made equal between wives (4:129), every throwing sin on innocent (4:112), every charity meant for His pleasure (4:114). *Samīʿ Baṣīr* has sealed the command to return trusts and judge fairly — *noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:58) — and now seals desire for reward: He hears the desire for world, sees the act for it, and measures accordingly without wronging even an atom but multiplying good many times (4:40). To say *with Him are both rewards* and He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing is to say seeking from Him is not unheard or unseen; the One who hears the wife fearing *nushūz* (4:128) and sees the *shuḥḥ* present with souls hears the desirer’s *yurīd* and sees whether desire is for Him or for little.

**A Verse That Follows Capability to Replace With Choice of Reward**

Placed after *if He wills He can remove you O humanity and bring others, He is Most Capable* (4:133), this verse follows capability to replace with choice of reward that determines whether you are removed or remain. The sūrah has warned *O humanity be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul* (4:1) and later *O humanity He can remove you* (4:133) — between those two *humanity* addresses lies law for orphans, women, inheritance, trust, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham, settlement, and now desire: to desire world’s reward alone from other than Him is to choose little where great is with Him. The sūrah has shown that those who took Satan as guardian instead of Him suffered tremendous loss seeking what he promised as delusion (4:119–121) while those who believed and did good found Gardens ever true (4:122); to desire world alone is to take the deluder’s little. The sūrah has said *all honour and power belongs to Him* (4:139) where hypocrites seek honour from disbelievers as allies; here *both rewards are with Him* is the same ownership: honour, as reward, is with Him alone. For the weak this is an opening: you need not envy what God gave some over others (4:32), but ask Him — with Him are both, and He hears and sees the asking.

**Both Rewards With Him Makes Single Desire Small**

The phrase *ʿinda Allāhi thawābu al-dunyā wa al-ākhirati* was explained as making single desire small. If you desire world alone, you ask the Capable who can remove and bring (4:133) for what perishes; had you asked Him you would have both — world as *murāgham* and *saʿah* (4:100), and Hereafter as Gardens forever true (4:122). The sūrah has shown that the Hereafter is better for the mindful than little enjoyment (4:77), that prayer at fixed writ (4:103) secures both, that standing firm for justice though against yourselves (4:135) secures both though self-interest seems to favour world alone. *Samīʿ Baṣīr* as seal was linked to *do not let desires cause you to deviate from justice* (4:135): desire for world’s reward deviates where hearing and seeing are not recalled. To remember He hears and sees is to recall that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) yet *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — both measured by the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Asking**

Though only *“whoever desires world’s reward, with Him are both rewards of this world and Hereafter, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing,”* the verse anchors asking. The chapter has commanded to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), to verify reports (4:83), to be sure before fighting (4:94), to judge by what He shows (4:105), to command charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114); all are acts whose reward the desirer might limit to world. The verse says ask the Owner who hears and sees for both, and you will find — as emigrant found havens, as separator found enrichment, as seeker found forgiveness. The next verse will apply that hearing and seeing to justice: stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves, parents, kin; rich or poor, God ensures interests; do not let desires deviate, if you distort or refuse, He is All-Aware of what you do (4:135).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:135

> O believers! Stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah even if it is against yourselves, your parents, or close relatives. Be they rich or poor, Allah is best to ensure their interests. So do not let your desires cause you to deviate ˹from justice˺. If you distort the testimony or refuse to give it, then ˹know that˺ Allah is certainly All-Aware of what you do.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Stand Firm for Justice as Witnesses for God Even Against Yourselves**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū kūnū qawwāmīna bi al-qisṭi shuhadāʾ li Allāhi wa law ʿalā anfusikum aw al-wālidayni wa al-aqrabīn* — O believers, be you steadfast, standing, upholders of justice, with equity, as witnesses for God even if against yourselves or parents or close kin. *Qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — upholders of justice, maintainers of equity, ever standing for fairness — was explained with *qawwām* — much standing, firm — the same root as *to stand up for orphans with justice* (4:127) and *to establish prayer* at fixed writ (4:103). *Shuhadāʾ li Allāhi* — witnesses for God — was read as testimony offered for Him, not for clan, as the sūrah commands to return trusts and judge fairly as noble command from the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:58) and to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and to verify before fighting (4:94). *Wa law ʿalā anfusikum aw al-wālidayni wa al-aqrabīn* — even if against yourselves, parents, close relatives — was explained as the Book’s severest test of the single soul’s ties (4:1): to honour ties is not to hide a kinsman’s theft by night plotting (4:108) nor to advocate for self-wrongers (4:107); to be just even against those ties is to honour the Creator of the single soul more than the soul’s branch. Early reports noted that this verse came where a dispute between parties of unequal rank pressed witnesses to favour the rich; the verse says witness for Him though the witness be against the self.

**Be They Rich or Poor — God Is Best to Ensure Interests**

The guidance *in yakun ghaniyyan aw faqīran fa Allāhu awlā bihimā* — be they rich or poor — the disputants — God is nearer, more worthy, better to ensure interests of both — was explained as prohibition of partiality by wealth. The rich might be favoured for honour or repayment, the poor pitied to tilt justice; both tilts were condemned, as the sūrah warns *all honour and power belongs to Him* (4:139) sought by taking disbelievers as allies, and warns that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — pity without truth is not those goods. *Fa Allāhu awlā bihimā* — God is nearer, more worthy of both, better guardian of both — was explained as that He owns heavens and earth (4:126) and suffices as Trustee (4:132) and is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) — guardianship of rich and poor alike belongs to Him, so the witness need not be guardian to either by tilting. The sūrah has said that the helpless men, women, children are hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and that the emigrant finds many havens (4:100) — protection is His; to stand for justice does not require protecting the poor by false testimony nor the rich by distortion, because He ensures interests better.

**So Do Not Let Desires Cause You to Deviate From Justice**

The warning *fa lā tattabiʿū al-hawā an taʿdilū* — so do not follow, do not let desires cause you to deviate, to incline from being just, from equitableness — was explained with *hawā* — desire, caprice, inclination — the same *hawā* that makes you deviate greatly if followed (4:27), that would make you follow other than believers’ path (4:115), and that makes private talk about charity insincere if for show. *An taʿdilū* — deviating from being just — was read as lest you not be just, lest you swerve; the sūrah earlier warned *if you fear ill conduct advise, then do not share beds, then discipline gently* (4:34) — justice even in household — and warned *do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended* (4:129) — justice even in polygyny. To follow *hawā* was linked to deceiving where eloquence persuades a judge to give a brother’s right as fire (Bukhārī 2680); desire there is eloquence, kin preference, pity, or greed for fleeting gain by denying peace (4:94). The command was read as the Book’s sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge by what He shows (4:105): to follow desire is to judge by what He did not show.

**If You Distort or Refuse — He Is All-Aware**

The threat *wa in talwū aw tuʿriḍū fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — and if you distort, twist — *lawy* — testimony, or refuse, turn away from giving it, then indeed God is ever All-Aware of what you do — was explained with two evasions: *talwū* — to twist, to distort, to bend the tongue, to change wording, to give ambiguous testimony — and *tuʿriḍū* — to turn aside, to refuse, to neglect to testify, to hide. Both were condemned as opposite of *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* and *shuhadāʾ li Allāh*. The sūrah has exposed those who hide from people but God is with them where they plot by night (4:108) — twisting is the daylight form of that night plotting — and who advocate in this life but will find no advocate on the Day (4:109) — refusing is the silence of that advocate where truth was needed. *Fa inna Allāha kāna bi mā taʿmalūna khabīrā* — He is Ever All-Aware of what you do — was explained as that He who is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126) and All-Aware of what you do where settlement was sought (4:128) and All-Hearing, All-Seeing where both rewards are with Him (4:134) knows twisting and refusing as He knows standing. The promise elsewhere *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) assumes the testimony that admits good; to twist it wrongs the speck.

**A Verse That Follows Universal Ownership With Universal Justice**

Placed after two humanity addresses — *We commanded those before you and you to be mindful* (4:131), *to Him belongs all, He suffices as Trustee* (4:132), *He can remove O humanity and bring others* (4:133), *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — this verse is the believers’ answer: stand firm for justice as witnesses for Him. The sūrah that began with honouring ties from a single soul (4:1), showed orphan girls deprived yet desired (4:127), wife fearing *nushūz* where settlement best (4:128), wives between whom inclination cannot be equalled (4:129), now says standing for justice may be against the very ties you honour — yourselves, parents, kin — and for the very rich or poor you once pitted — yet do not follow desire to deviate, lest you twist or turn away. The sūrah that taught verification before fighting (4:94) and judging by Book (4:105) here teaches verification before testifying: be *qawwām* — ever standing — so that twisting and refusing are not options. For the weak this is the highest protection: where wealth tempts and poverty pities, justice upheld for God is the haven as sure as many havens for the emigrant, and He who is All-Aware of what you do will not wrong a speck.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:136

> O believers! Have faith in Allah, His Messenger, the Book He has revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before. Indeed, whoever denies Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray.

**Expanded Commentary**

**O Believers — Have Faith in God, Messenger, and Books**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū āminū bi Allāhi wa rasūlihī wa al-kitābi alladhī nazzala ʿalā rasūlihī wa al-kitābi alladhī anzala min qablu* — O believers, have faith — believe, continue believing — in God and His Messenger and the Book He has sent down upon His Messenger and the Scriptures He sent down before. *Āminū* to *āmanū* was explained not as contradiction but as command to firmness, renewal, and comprehensiveness: those who already believe are told to remain believers, to increase belief, to believe without distinction, as the sūrah has shown that those who believe and do good are admitted to Gardens (4:57, 4:122) yet belief must be in the full articles. *Bi Allāhi wa rasūlihī* — in God and Messenger — was read as the two inseparably taught where obeying the Messenger is obeying God (4:80), messengers are only sent to be obeyed by His leave (4:64), and the Messenger is taken as judge without resistance (4:65). *Al-kitābi alladhī nazzala ʿalā rasūlihī* — the Book He revealed to His Messenger — was explained as the Qur’an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) whose word none is more truthful than (4:122). *Wa al-kitābi alladhī anzala min qablu* — and the Scriptures He revealed before — was read as the Books given before — Torah, Gospel — before distortion, matching *“Worship God alone, associate none”* (4:36) and *“We commanded those given Scripture before you and you to be mindful”* (4:131) — the command is one. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book claim wishes (4:123) and distort words (4:46); to believe in Books before is to believe in them as revealed before distorting hands altered them, not to follow altered claim.

**And Whoever Denies — Has Gone Far Astray**

The threat *wa man yakfur bi Allāhi wa malāʾikatihī wa kutubihī wa rusulihī wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri fa qad ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — indeed whoever denies — covers, disbelieves in — God, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray, wandered far — was explained with five articles. *Yakfur* — to deny, to cover — was read as the denial that makes association not forgiven (4:116) and that makes following other than believers’ path burning (4:115). The five — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — were explained as the Book’s summary of faith, matching *“whoever associates has gone far astray”* (4:116) where *ḍalālan baʿīdan* — far straying — also sealed; here the same seal for denying any of the five. Angels were read as the recorders of night schemes (4:81), the takers of souls asked *what were you doing?* (4:97), the supporters of prayer guard (4:102); to deny angels is to deny those realities. Books and messengers were read as the conveyors of the Book in truth and wisdom taught (4:113); Last Day as the Day about which there is no doubt where all will be gathered (4:87) and gathered together hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell (4:140). *Ḍalla ḍalālan baʿīdā* — gone far astray — was linked to going far after guidance became clear (4:115); denial of these articles after clarity is the farthest distance, because it denies the very witnesses who prove clarity.

**A Verse That Follows Justice With Creed**

Placed after *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves rich or poor, do not follow desire, if you twist or turn away He is All-Aware* (4:135), this verse follows justice with creed that secures it. The sūrah has judged between people by Book, warned no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114), warned defying the Messenger and following other than believers’ path (4:115), named association far straying (4:116), female gods and Satan’s share (4:117–118), Satan’s orders and delusion (4:119–120), two abodes true (4:121–122), wishes not by wish (4:123), good with faith not wronged (4:124), best faith submission following Abraham whom God took as friend (4:125), ownership and encompassing (4:126), instruction for orphan women and helpless children (4:127), settlement best though selves brought with *shuḥḥ* (4:128), impossible emotional equality yet do not incline entirely (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130), universal command to be mindful though He is Self-Sufficient (4:131), sufficiency as Trustee (4:132), capability to replace humanity (4:133), both rewards with Him Hearing and Seeing (4:134); now faith in the full articles is the root that makes justice — *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — possible without twisting. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by desire (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here names the content that desire most attacks — God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day — after which far straying is the fruit.

**Belief Commanded to Believers — Renewal Not Repetition**

The command *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū āminū* was explained as renewal, firmness, and widening: to believers who believed in part — in God but not Messenger, in this Book but not those before, in God and Books but not angels or Last Day — the command is to believe entirely, without making distinction between God and messengers saying *we believe in some and disbelieve in others desiring a compromise* (4:150). The sūrah has shown that making distinction is the compromise of those who deny — they make distinction and desire to forge compromise (4:150) — here the command closes that compromise: have faith in God, Messenger, the Book He revealed to His Messenger, and Scriptures He revealed before, and in angels and Last Day implied — no selecting. Where the sūrah later says *those who believed then disbelieved then believed again then increased in disbelief — He will neither forgive nor guide* (4:137), redoubled belief is shown as fragile where articles are not firm; *āminū* here is the firming before that warning.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Law in Last Day**

Though only *“believe in God, Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before, whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray,”* the verse anchors law in Last Day. The justice just commanded — standing though against selves and parents, not distorting — has no motive without Last Day where advocates in this life will find no advocate before God (4:109) and where those gathered together in Hell will be hypocrites and disbelievers (4:140). To deny Last Day after guidance clear is to make the *yujza* — recompensed accordingly — for evil (4:123) unintelligible, and to deny Books and messengers is to make judging by what He shows (4:105) unintelligible, and to deny angels is to make recording of night schemes (4:81, 4:108) unintelligible. For the weak this is the lightest anchoring: to have faith — renewed, entire — in the Hearing, Seeing (4:134) who owns heavens and earth (4:132) and who will not wrong a speck (4:124) is to entrust justice to the *Wakīl* who suffices, the Self-Sufficient who does not need.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:137

> Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed and again disbelieved—˹only˺ increasing in disbelief—Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Way.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Believed Then Disbelieved — Then Increased**

The verse states *inna alladhīna āmanū thumma kafarū thumma āmanū thumma kafarū thumma izdādū kufrā* — indeed those who believed then disbelieved, then believed then disbelieved — then only increasing in disbelief, adding disbelief. *Āmanū thumma kafarū* — believed then disbelieved — repeated twice was explained as oscillation, not mere lapse: belief then denial, then return to belief then again denial, yet not as repentance accepted soon after error (4:17) but as performance, as hypocrisy’s rhythm. *Thumma izdādū kufrā* — then increased, added, in disbelief — was read as that the second disbelief is not return to first level but increase: associating after far straying (4:116), taking Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119), invoking female gods (4:117) — each step adds. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose (4:115) and whoever associates has gone far astray (4:116); to oscillate between belief and denial after clarity is to defy after clarity repeatedly, making guidance not firm. Early reports linked the verse to Jews who believed in Moses then disbelieved in Jesus then believed? The generality was stressed: whoever trades belief for disbelief and returns only to trade again, increasing, is meant — the hypocrite described as *“torn between belief and disbelief, belonging neither to these nor those”* (4:143) and who seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142).

**Allah Will Neither Forgive Nor Guide to Right Way**

The seal *lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum wa lā li yahdiyuhum sabīlā* — Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to a way — the Right Way — was explained with two negations: no forgiveness and no guidance. *Li yaghfira lahum* — to forgive them — was read as that *“whoever commits evil then seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving”* (4:110) has a condition — seeking after evil before death’s saying *now I repent* (4:18); these increase in disbelief instead of seeking, so forgiveness is not. *Wa lā li yahdiyuhum sabīlā* — nor guide them to a way, to path — was read as *sabīla* — way — the same *sabīl* the sūrah wills to make clear as noble ways (4:26), Satan wishes the deviant far path (4:60), believers’ path is not to be left (4:115); those who oscillate and increase have closed the path by repeatedly turning. The phrase *lam yakun li yaghfira* — He will not forgive — was linked to *“He does not forgive associating, forgives what is less”* (4:48, 4:116): increase in disbelief is shown to settle into the unforgiven associate-level where pardon is not, unless the oscillation is broken by firm belief. The sūrah has said *“whoever is left to stray you will never find a way”* (4:88, 4:143) — *lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — here the way not found is forgiveness and guidance, because they left it.

**A Verse That Follows Firm Belief With Description of Unfirm**

Placed after *O believers, have faith in God, Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before, whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray* (4:136), this verse follows firm belief commanded with description of unfirm belief that oscillates. The sūrah has commanded *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — ever standing for justice (4:135) — and said both rewards are with Him (4:134) and He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133); oscillation is the opposite of standing: to stand is to remain, to oscillate is to be removed. The sūrah has shown that *“had it not been for grace they would have deceived you yet they deceive only themselves”* (4:113) — oscillation deceives only self, increasing its disbelief, not harming the Prophet. Where the sūrah will give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:138–139) and will declare not to sit with those who deny or ridicule revelations else you are like them (4:140), this verse is the theological root: belief then disbelief then belief then increase is the hypocrite’s creed.

**Increase in Disbelief After Light Was Clear**

The phrase *thumma izdādū kufrā* — then only increasing in disbelief — was explained as that disbelief has degrees, as the sūrah’s *ḍalālan baʿīdan* — far straying — has degrees: to associate is far (4:116), to defy the Messenger after clarity and follow other than believers’ path is left to stray (4:115), to invoke Satan instead of Him is tremendous loss (4:119). Increase was linked to making distinction between God and messengers, believing in some and disbelieving in others desiring compromise (4:150), which is itself increase where the compromise is after guidance clear. The sūrah’s arithmetic of good — multiplied many times over (4:40) — has counterpart in evil’s increase: persistence after oscillation does not stay level but adds, as *šuḥḥ* present with souls (4:128) adds when not overcome by graciousness. The seal *lan yaghfira wa lā yahdiyuhum* was therefore read as consequence of addition: where repentance soon after error is pardon (4:17), increase after oscillation is the opposite direction, so forgiveness and guidance are not.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Hypocrisy Before Its Portrait**

Though only *“those who believed then disbelieved then believed again then increased, He will neither forgive nor guide to Right Way,”* the verse anchors hypocrisy before its portrait. Immediately after: *“give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, seeking honour”* (4:138–139) — portraits of oscillation made alliance. Immediately after: *“when you hear revelations denied or ridiculed do not sit in that company else you are like them, He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell”* (4:140) — company of oscillation. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here warns that desire to keep options open — belief then disbelief — ends with neither forgiveness nor way, because the One who is Self-Sufficient (4:131) and whose promise is ever true (4:122) does not guide the one who increased after being shown. For the weak this is clarifying: belief is not a wish by which grace is claimed (4:123) nor a wavering between sides like those who wait to see what happens (4:141), but firm faith that finds Him All-Forgiving when it seeks after evil (4:110).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:138

> Give good news of a painful punishment to hypocrites,

**Expanded Commentary**

**Give Good News of Painful Punishment to Hypocrites**

The verse states *bashshiri al-munāfiqīna bi anna lahum ʿadhāban alīmā* — give good news, announce, to hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment. *Bashshir* — to give good news, to announce joy — was explained as irony: to announce painful punishment as if good news, because the hypocrite’s own announcement is deceit — they seek to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142), they show prayer to be seen (4:142), they wait to see what happens to you and say to whichever side wins *were we not with you?* (4:141). *Al-munāfiqīn* — hypocrites — was read as those who believed then disbelieved then believed again then increased (4:137) and who are torn between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) and who will be in lowest depth of Fire without helper (4:145). *Bi anna lahum ʿadhāban alīman* — that for them is painful punishment — was explained as *alīm* — painful, aching — the same *alīm* prepared for those who consume orphans’ wealth after warning (4:10’s Fire) and for those who knowingly persist then say now I repent (4:18). The sūrah has traced hypocrisy from the community divided into two groups about them (4:88) where some wished you alike in disbelief (4:89) to the double-faced who plunge into *fitnah* (4:91), to the lagger who stays and envies (4:72–73), to the plotters by night (4:108); here the announce is not warning but recompense — *painful punishment* — for the territory between belief and disbelief where they tried to keep both.

**A Verse That Follows Oscillation With Irony**

Placed after *those who believed then disbelieved then increased, He will neither forgive nor guide* (4:137), this verse follows oscillation with irony: the good news for the one who increased in disbelief after believing is painful punishment. The sūrah has shown that honour and power belongs to God (4:139) where hypocrites seek honour from disbelievers as allies, and that sitting with those who deny or ridicule revelations makes you like them and gathered together in Hell (4:140); the painful punishment is the announcement for that alliance and that sitting. The sūrah has also shown that the deceitful’s night speech displeases Him (4:108) and that advocacy for self-wrongers in this life will find no advocate on the Day (4:109); painful punishment is the Day’s answer to the night’s delight. Where the sūrah elsewhere says *“do not consume wealth unjustly, God is ever Merciful to you”* (4:29) yet *“whoever does this unjustly We will burn in Fire, easy for God”* (4:30) — easy where threats are — this painful punishment is the Fire easy for the One who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133).

**The Good News That Is Not Good**

The verb *bashshir* — give good news — was explained to show that hypocrisy inverts news: what they took as good — advantage with both sides, honour through company with disbelievers (4:139), safety from you and from their people while plunging into hostility (4:91) — is announced as painful. The sūrah has said that the Devil promises only delusion (4:120) — his good news is delusion; God’s *bashshir* here is true news — painful. The contrast was linked to *“those who believe and do good, We will admit into Gardens … whose word more truthful?”* (4:122) — their good news is Gardens true; hypocrites’ good news is *alīm* true. Classical notes added that *bashshir* for punishment appears where mockery preceded — the hypocrites mock revelations with those who deny or ridicule (4:140) — so the reply mocks the mocker with true phrase.

**A Short Verse That Opens the Hypocrite Portrait**

Though only *“give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites,”* the verse opens the hypocrite portrait that follows. Immediately: *who choose disbelievers as allies instead of believers, do they seek honour through that company? Surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139) — portraits of their alliance. Then: *He has already revealed that when you hear revelations denied or ridiculed do not sit in that company else you are like them, He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) — portraits of their sitting. Then: *those who wait to see what happens to you, saying to each winner were we not on your side?* (4:141) — portraits of their waiting. All are branches of the oscillation that neither forgives nor guides (4:137). For the weak this is a clearing: where you were divided into two groups about hypocrites (4:88) and told not to take them as allies unless they emigrate (4:89), the painful punishment is the news that the division is not equal — to ally with disbelievers for honour is not the community’s way, as *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* (4:125) was not alliance with many.

**Painful Punishment as Measure of Deception’s Pain**

The attribute *alīm* — painful — was explained as measure where deception sought to avoid pain: the lagger sought to avoid disaster by lagging (4:72), the emigrant sought many havens to avoid oppression (4:100), the self-wronger sought advocacy to avoid blame (4:107); hypocrisy seeks to avoid pain of standing — *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* (4:135) — by belonging to neither side (4:143). The sūrah says pain is shared — *if you suffer they suffer* (4:104) — yet the hypocrite who belongs nowhere suffers twice: belonging without hope and pain without reward. The painful punishment is therefore not arbitrary but the hypocrite’s own avoided pain returned as lasting pain, as Hell without escape (4:121) was the delusion’s end. The next verses will name the seeking that makes it painful — honour sought through wrong company — and the sitting that makes company like them.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:139

> who choose disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour and power through that company? Surely all honour and power belongs to Allah.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Who Choose Disbelievers as Allies Instead of Believers**

The verse states *alladhīna yattakhidhūna al-kāfirīna awliyāʾa min dūni al-muʾminīna* — those who take disbelievers as allies, guardians, close protectors instead, apart from, the believers. *Yattakhidhūna awliyāʾ* — to take as allies — was explained with *walī* — guardian, protector, helper — the same *walī* God alone suffices as (4:45), the help the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75), the trustee who suffices (4:132). *Min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers, apart from believers, short of believers — was read as choosing the other company while believers are available, as earlier *“do not take them as allies unless they emigrate”* (4:89) where alliance was conditioned on emigration, and *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) where alliance is warning. The sūrah has traced *awliyāʾ* from the lagger who had no bond — *ka an lam takun baynakum wa baynahu mawaddah* — as if no affection between you (4:73) — to the double safety seekers (4:91), to the treaty people excepted (4:90), to Satan taken as guardian instead of Him (4:119); here the *awliyāʾ* taken are disbelievers instead of believers, for the hypocrites who oscillate (4:137, 4:143) the natural alliance is the side that promises *ʿizzah* without *qisṭ*.

**Do They Seek Honour and Power Through That Company?**

The question *ayabtaghūna ʿindahumu al-ʿizzata* — do they seek, desire, pursue honour, might, power, *ʿizzah*, at their side, with them, through that company? — was explained with *ʿizzah* — honour, might, power, invincibility — the same *ʿizzah* Satan rejected when cursed (4:118) and claimed as share. *Abtaghā ʿindahum* — to seek at their side, with them — was read as seeking honour where honour is not: with those who disbelieve, whose schemes are weak (4:76) and whose abode is Hell without escape (4:121) versus Gardens true (4:122). The sūrah has shown that honour was claimed by *jibt* and *ṭāghūt* believers who declared disbelievers better guided (4:51) and who wish you deviate (4:44); to seek *ʿizzah* among disbelievers instead of believers is to repeat that evaluative reversal — to call weakness honour. Early reports linked the verse to hypocrites who cultivated Quraysh for protection and status in Madinah while claiming belief; the question was read as exposing the transaction: alliance for honour where alliance for God was available as Garden and as self-sufficient ownership (4:131).

**Surely All Honour and Power Belongs to God**

The answer *fa inna al-ʿizzata li Allāhi jamīʿā* — then surely all, entirely, honour and power belongs to God — was explained with *jamīʿan* — entirely, all together — the same totality as *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126, 4:131) repeated thrice, and as *with Him are both rewards* (4:134). *Al-ʿizzata li Allāhi* — honour belongs to Him — was read as that *ʿizzah* is not transferred by taking allies; it is His to give to whom He wills — *“you, the best *dīn* submits face and follows Abraham whom He took as friend”* (4:125) — friendship with the Owner of honour is honour. The sūrah has said that God suffices as Guardian and Helper (4:45) and suffices as Trustee (4:132) and is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131); to seek *ʿizzah* beside Him is to seek the encompassed (4:126) among the encompassed. The phrase was linked to *“do they seek honour through that company? Surely all honour belongs to Him”* as the sūrah’s ownership applied to honour: as all in heavens and earth belong to Him, all honour belongs to Him, so the seeker who takes disbelievers as allies seeks at the side of those who own nothing.

**A Verse That Names the Transaction Behind Oscillation**

Placed after *give good news of painful punishment to hypocrites* (4:138), this verse names the transaction behind oscillation: they believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137), torn between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) because they sought *ʿizzah* where alliance seemed to give it. The sūrah has shown that whoever defies the Messenger after guidance and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose (4:115) — choosing disbelievers as allies is that following — and that associating is far straying (4:116) — seeking *ʿizzah* among associators is that straying’s economy. Where the sūrah says *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God though against yourselves* (4:135) not letting desires deviate, seeking honour from wrong company is the desire that deviates: to witness for disbelievers to gain *ʿizzah* instead of witnessing for God though against yourselves is the precise inversion. For the weak this is steadying: honour is not with the company that wishes you deviate (4:27), nor with Satan’s delusion promise (4:120), but with Him whose earth is spacious (4:100) and whose promise ever true (4:122).

**Honour That Is Entirely His Leaves No Honour With Them**

The word *jamīʿan* — entirely, all together — was explained to leave no remainder with those chosen as allies: if all honour is His, none is at their side to give. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens from Him (4:100), the doer of good male or female enters Paradise not wronged a speck (4:124) because grace is His, the best faith is submission to Him (4:125) — honour is that friendship. To choose disbelievers as *awliyāʾ* instead of believers is therefore not a neutral social choice but a theological claim that honour is elsewhere, which the ownership verses deny: *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* — honour included. The next verse will show the company that seeks such honour in sitting: when you hear revelations denied or ridiculed do not sit in that company unless they speak other talk, else you are like them, and He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:140

> He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s revelations being denied or ridiculed, then do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic, or else you will be like them. Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell.

**Expanded Commentary**

**When You Hear Revelations Denied or Ridiculed — Do Not Sit**

The verse states *wa qad nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi an idhā samiʿtum āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear God’s signs, revelations, being denied, covered, or mocked, ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in another discourse, other topic. *Nazzala ʿalaykum fī al-kitābi* — He has revealed to you in the Book — was explained as the earlier revelation referenced at 6:68 — *when you see those who engage in Our signs then turn away until they engage in other talk* — the sūrah’s cross-reference where sitting with mockers is prohibited, recited again here for hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139). *Āyāti Allāhi yukfaru bihā wa yustahzaʾu bihā* — signs denied or ridiculed — was explained as the denial that makes association far straying (4:116) and the ridicule that is the mocker’s weapon, as the sūrah has shown that those given a portion distort words and say *“we hear and disobey”* (4:46) and that Satan promises only delusion (4:120). *Fa lā taqʿudū maʿahum* — do not sit with them — was read as prohibition of company, not merely speech, matching *no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — sitting where signs are ridiculed is the secret talk without those goods. *Ḥattā yakhūḍū fī ḥadīthin ghayrih* — until they engage in another topic, plunge into other talk — was read as the limit: leaving until the subject changes, as *“do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic”* is the translation’s phrasing.

**Or Else You Will Be Like Them**

The consequence *innakum idhan mithluhum* — surely you, then, are like them, similar — was explained as moral assimilation: sitting where signs are denied or mocked without protest or leaving makes the sitter like the denier and mocker, even where he claims belief. *Mithluhum* — like them — was read with the sūrah’s assimilation language where *“when you hear revelations denied do not sit in that company”* elsewhere makes the sitter like them because silence endorses. The sūrah has shown that the sitter with treaty people is excepted from hostility (4:90), that the constructor of ambiguity is warned *“do not take them as allies”* (4:89), and that witnesses for God must be against even selves (4:135); to sit is the sitter’s testimony that the denied sign is not worthy of standing. Early notes linked the verse to hypocrites who kept company with Quraysh mockers for honour (4:139): to seek honour among mockers while revelations are ridiculed is to be like the mocker where honour was sought. The phrase was also linked to *whoever distorts testimony or refuses* (4:135) — sitting is refusing testimony where signs need testimony as witnesses for Him.

**He Will Gather Hypocrites and Disbelievers Together in Hell**

The gathering *inna Allāha jāmiʿu al-munāfiqīna wa al-kāfirīna fī Jahannama jamīʿā* — surely God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together, entirely, in Hell — was explained with *jāmiʿ* — gatherer — the same gatherer who will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87) and who gathered revelation as Book with truth (4:105). *Jamīʿan* — all together, entirely — was read as that sitting together in mockery in this life — *taqʿudū maʿahum* — ends as being gathered together in Hell: company chosen becomes company assigned. The sūrah has shown that the hypocrite oscillates between neither believers nor disbelievers (4:143) yet *innakum idhan mithluhum* counts the sitter as like the disbeliever; gathering together makes that likeness abiding — *khālidīn* — without escape (4:121) as that gathering is *“what an evil destination”* for self-wrongers (4:97). The phrase was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, God’s promise ever true”* (4:122) versus *“Hell as home no escape”* (4:121): the sitting that was for *ʿizzah* (4:139) ends in gathering for humiliation, as the guarded prayer’s preparation was humiliating punishment for disbelievers (4:102). For the weak this is the lightest of warnings: to rise from mocking company is not enmity but survival, as not sitting is the Book’s instruction.

**A Verse That Follows Honour Sought With Company Prohibited**

Placed after *who choose disbelievers as allies seeking honour, surely all honour belongs to God* (4:139), this verse follows honour sought with company prohibited. The hypocrites sought honour through company with disbelievers (4:139); the verse says the company where signs are denied or mocked is precisely where you may not sit lest you be like them — so honour sought there is gathered as humiliation. The sūrah has shown that trusteeship suffices (4:132), that He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133), that both rewards are with Him (4:134); to sit with mockers for worldly *ʿizzah* is to desire world’s reward from beside Him where both rewards are with Him. The sūrah has also shown that standing for justice as witnesses for Him though against yourselves (4:135) requires leaving where justice is mocked; to remain seated where signs are denied is to distort testimony. The verse generalises the sūrah’s procedure: where report is heard of security or fear verify through Messenger and authority (4:83), and where a bearer of peace offers *salām* be sure (4:94), here where a sitter hears signs denied verify by leaving until other talk.

**Gathering Together as the Company’s End**

The verb *jāmiʿ* — gatherer — was explained to show that company in this life where secret talks had no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) was rejected, while company where signs are mocked was chosen; the other world repays company with company: hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell, believers and doers of good together in Gardens (4:122). The sūrah that warned *do not be advocate for deceitful* (4:105) and *do not advocate for self-wrongers* (4:107) and asked *who will advocate before God on the Day?* (4:109) here says advocates in this life who sat with mockers will be gathered with the mocked-for — not as advocates but as like — *mithluhum*. The next verse will show their waiting: those who wait to see what happens to you, saying to winners on each side *were we not on your side?* (4:141) — waiting is the posture of sitting extended into battlefield.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:141

> ˹The hypocrites are˺ those who wait to see what happens to you. So if Allah grants you victory, they say ˹to you˺, “Were we not on your side?” But if the disbelievers have a share ˹of victory˺, they say ˹to them˺, “Did we not have the advantage over you, yet we protected you from the believers?” Allah will judge between ˹all of˺ you on the Day of Judgment. And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Wait to See What Happens to You**

The verse states *alladhīna yatarabbaṣūna bikum* — those who wait, watch, lie in wait in expectation regarding you. *Yatarabbaṣūna* — to wait, to watch, to await outcome — was explained as the hypocrites’ posture between the community divided into two groups about them (4:88) and the gathering of hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140). To wait regarding you — *bikum* — was read as waiting upon believers’ affairs, battles, and turns, as the lagger waited — *la yabṭiʾannakum* — to lag behind and say if you suffer *God blessed us for not being there* and if you gain *would we had been with them* (4:72–73), and as party waiting for the Prophet’s judgment to be deceived (4:113). The waiters here are the same who took disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) and sat where revelations were mocked lest they be like them (4:140); waiting is sitting’s extension into war: not sitting in mosque where signs are denied, but lying in wait between armies to see who wins. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens by moving (4:100), that the traveller shortens and guards prayer by moving in ranks (4:101–102); the waiter moves toward neither haven nor rank but stays to see.

**If You Win They Claim — Were We Not With You?**

The first face *fa in kāna lakum fatḥun mina Allāhi qālū a lam nakun maʿakum* — so if there is for you a victory, an opening, from God, they say to you — believers — were we not with you, on your side? — was explained with *fatḥ* — victory, opening — as God’s opening, the same opening invoked for the oppressed where *“appoint for us a saviour, helper”* from grace (4:75). *A lam nakun maʿakum* — were we not with you — was read as the claim of *walāyah* — alliance — after victory, as the sūrah later says they will say *“were we not on your side?”* to share gain. The claim was linked to *“as if there had been no bond between you”* (4:73) where the lagger says after gain *would we had been there* — the waiter here says after victory *were we not there* — both seek gain without sharing faith. Early reports noted that such waiters remained in Madinah, not going forth as commanded in groups or together (4:71), yet claimed share after. The sūrah has warned *“do not take them as allies unless they emigrate”* (4:89); the waiter’s *were we not with you?* is the emigration not done yet claimed.

**If Disbelievers Have Share They Say — Did We Not Have Advantage Yet Protected You?**

The second face *wa in kāna li al-kāfirīna naṣībun qālū a lam nastahwidh ʿalaykum wa namnaʿkum mina al-muʾminīn* — but if disbelievers have a share, a portion, they say to them — did we not have the advantage, gain mastery over you, yet we protected, prevented you from the believers? — was explained with *naṣīb* — share, portion — lesser than *fatḥ* — opening — showing even a small share for disbelievers makes the waiter turn. *A lam nastahwidh ʿalaykum* — did we not gain mastery, encompass you, have advantage over you — was read as claim of power over the disbelievers: we could have delivered you to believers, we had upper hand. *Wa namnaʿkum mina al-muʾminīn* — yet we protected you from the believers, we held believers back — was read as claim of protection: by not fighting with believers, by conveying information, by saying we held them off. The two claims mirror the lagger’s double speech and the double safety seekers who wish safety from you and from their people yet plunge into *fitnah* whenever returned (4:91). The sūrah that warned *Satan promises only delusion* (4:120) here shows human promisers who promise both sides delivery.

**God Will Judge Between You on Resurrection Day**

The adjudication *fa Allāhu yaḥkumu baynakum yawma al-qiyāmati* — then God will judge, decide, between you — all of you — on the Day of Standing — was explained as the sūrah’s gathering promise: He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140) after being gathered on the Day about which there is no doubt (4:87) and after being asked at soul-taking *what were you doing?* (4:97). *Yaḥkumu baynakum* — will judge between you — was read as between believers, hypocrites, and disbelievers, between the waiter and both winners he courted, between the *fatḥ* and *naṣīb* claims. The sūrah has said the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105), and that He is sufficient as Trustee (4:132) and Witness (4:79); on the Day the Judge is not eloquence that might sway a human court where *“some may be more eloquent and I give his brother’s right as fire”* (Bukhārī 2680), but the All-Knowing who knows what was in hearts (4:63) and who is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108). The judgment separates the waiter’s *“were we not with you?”* from the true *with-ness* — *maʿiyyah* — that is with the believers for Gardens (4:122).

**And He Will Never Grant Disbelievers a Way Over Believers**

The assurance *wa lan yajʿala Allāhu li al-kāfirīna ʿalā al-muʾminīna sabīlā* — and God will never grant, make, for disbelievers over believers a way, a path, an argument — was explained with *sabīl* — way, path, proof, dominance — the same *sabīl* the sūrah said He will guide to noble ways (4:26), the path believers follow (4:115), and the *sabili al-muʾminīn* not to be left. To grant no *sabīl* for disbelievers over believers was read as promise that final argument and final dominance are not given to disbelief over faith, as *“He will judge between you”* ensures the argument is not the waiter’s double claim. Early authorities debated worldly reading — never granting disbelievers a way over believers in proof — versus eschatological — the Day — where gathering separates; the sūrah holds both: on the Day no *sabīl* remains, and in this world where God wills to make clear and guide to noble ways (4:26) the believer’s *sabīl* is protected where he stands for justice (4:135). The promise was also linked to *all honour belongs to Him* (4:139): *sabīl* over believers as honour is not granted to disbelievers, though *naṣīb* or *fatḥ* in battle may be. For the weak this is steadying: waiting between sides promises no *sabīl* over you, as He who owns heavens and earth (4:126) grants none.

**A Verse That Follows Gathering With Waiting and Judgment**

Placed after gathering hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), this verse follows gathering with waiting that made gathering inevitable and with judgment that decides waiting. The hypocrites who believed then disbelieved then increased (4:137), announced as painful punishment (4:138), who chose disbelievers as allies for honour (4:139), sat where revelations were mocked (4:140), now wait between armies to claim *were we not with you?* to whichever side wins. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) here exposes the waiter’s desire: to belong without standing, to be *qawwām* nowhere yet claim *maʿiyya* everywhere. The next verses will anatomise that waiting: they seek to deceive God but He outwits them, they stand for prayer to be seen hardly remembering (4:142), torn between neither believers nor disbelievers, whoever He leaves to stray you will find no way (4:143).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:142

> Surely the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He outwits them. When they stand up for prayer, they do it half-heartedly only to be seen by people—hardly remembering Allah at all.

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Hypocrites Seek to Deceive God — But He Outwits Them**

The verse opens *inna al-munāfiqīna yukhādiʿūna Allāha wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — surely the hypocrites seek to deceive, to trick, God, but He is outwitting, deceiving them, repaying their deceit. *Yukhādiʿūna* — to seek to deceive, to pretend, to show other than what is — was explained as hypocrisy’s essence: belief then disbelief then increased (4:137), taking disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139), sitting where revelations are mocked (4:140), waiting between winners to claim *were we not with you?* (4:141). To deceive God was explained as showing Islam before believers while hiding alliance with disbelievers, as plotting by night what displeases Him while He is with them (4:108) and hiding from people but not from the Encompassing (4:108). *Wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — but He outwits them, He is their deceiver in return — was read as that His outwitting is recompense: He lets them pursue what they chose (4:115), gathers them with disbelievers together in Hell (4:140), will judge between all on the Day (4:141), and leaves to stray whom He leaves (4:143). The sūrah has said that God is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108) and knows what is in hearts (4:63); deception cannot reach Him, it returns. Early notes linked *khādiʿuhum* to *makr* — planning — where *“they plot and God plots, God is best of plotters”* (3:54); the outwitting is His plan that gathering together is the outcome of sitting together.

**When They Stand for Prayer — Half-Heartedly, To Be Seen**

The sign *wa idhā qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti qāmū kusālā yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — and when they stand up for prayer, head to prayer, they stand lazy, sluggish, half-heartedly, showing off to people, to be seen — was explained with *qāmū ilā al-ṣalāti* — standing to prayer — the same standing commanded as *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — ever standing for justice (4:135) — and *qūmū li al-yatāmā bi al-qisṭ* (4:127) — here the hypocrites stand to prayer as witnesses not for Him but for people. *Kusālā* — lazy, heavy, sluggish — was explained as heaviness where the sūrah earlier said prayer at appointed writ (4:103) and guarded prayer under arms (4:102) requires vigilance; their laziness is the opposite of vigilance and of pursuit without faltering (4:104). *Yurāʾūna al-nāsa* — they show off to people, make seen — *riyāʾ* — was read as the same showing off condemned where they spend wealth to show off and do not believe in God or Last Day (4:38) — *spending to be seen* — here *standing to be seen*. The sūrah has shown that there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114); to stand to be seen is to seek people’s pleasure, the *ʿizzah* sought among disbelievers (4:139), not His.

**Hardly Remembering God at All**

The remainder *wa lā yadhkurūna Allāha illā qalīlā* — and they hardly remember, mention, invoke God at all, except a little — was explained with *yadhkurūna* — to remember, to mention — the same *adhkurū Allāha* commanded standing, sitting, lying down when prayer is finished (4:103). The sūrah has shown that remembrance in all postures is prayer’s extension; hypocrites remember a little — *qalīlan* — the minimum to be seen, not the standing, sitting, lying remembrance. *Illā qalīlan* — except a little — was explained as little in quantity and little in sincerity, as the sūrah says they stand lazily to be seen — their few remembrances are for seen-ness. Classical notes added that the *qalīl* matches the world’s little enjoyment — *matāʿ qalīl* (4:77) — that hypocrisy trades Gardens forever (4:122) for little seen-ness. The seal contrasts with *“whose word more truthful than God’s?”* (4:122) and *“God is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132): to remember little is to trust little.

**A Verse That Follows Waiting With Deception and Lazy Prayer**

Placed after those who wait to see what happens and claim belonging to winners (4:141), this verse follows waiting with the prayer that reveals waiting’s creed: to deceive God, to stand lazy to be seen, to remember little. The sūrah has shown prayer shortened and guarded (4:101–102) and remembered in all postures (4:103) as the believer’s discipline that does not falter in pursuit for hope (4:104); the hypocrite’s prayer deforms each — standing yet lazy, guarded yet to be seen, remembering but little. The sūrah that commands *stand firm for justice as witnesses for God even against yourselves* (4:135) shows the hypocrite’s witness is for people to be seen; the sūrah that says *with Him are both rewards, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing* (4:134) shows He hears lazy standing and sees showing off. The verse was read as the hypocrite’s litmus after the announcement of painful punishment (4:138) and honour sought elsewhere (4:139): painful punishment is for those whose prayer is for sight, not for Him.

**Deception Outwitted Becomes Being Gathered Together**

The phrase *wa huwa khādiʿuhum* — He outwits them — was linked to *“He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell”* (4:140): outwitting is gathering. The hypocrite deceives by sitting where signs are mocked as if not like them, yet the verse says *then you are like them* (4:140); on the Day the like-ness becomes gathering together. The sūrah has shown that whoever takes Satan as guardian instead of Him suffers tremendous loss (4:119) and that Satan promises only delusion (4:120); to stand for prayer to be seen is to take people as guardians instead of Him, whose delusion is *ʿizzah* seen. For the weak this is diagnostic: where you stand for prayer after fear, stand vigilant not lazy, remember standing, sitting, lying — much — not little, and seek His pleasure not people’s sight, for He who can remove humanity if He wills (4:133) outwits the deceiver by the very gathering the deceiver thought to avoid by waiting.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:143

> Torn between belief and disbelief—belonging neither to these ˹believers˺ nor those ˹disbelievers˺. And whoever Allah leaves to stray, you will never find for them a way.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Torn Between — Belonging Neither to Believers Nor Disbelievers**

The verse opens *mudhabdhabīna bayna dhālika lā ilā hāʾulāʾi wa lā ilā hāʾulāʾi* — torn, wavering, suspended between that, between this and that, belonging neither to these — believers — nor to those — disbelievers. *Mudhabdhab* — torn, swayed, fluttered, shaky — was explained as the hypocrites’ oscillation already named — believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137), waiting to see what happens to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, standing lazy to be seen (4:142). *Bayna dhālika* — between that — was read as between belief and disbelief, between the host with many havens (4:100) and the host without escape (4:121), between Gardens true (4:122) and Hell prepared. *Lā ilā hāʾulāʾi wa lā ilā hāʾulāʾi* — neither to these nor to those — was explained as that their alliance — *awliyāʾ* — taken from disbelievers instead of believers seeking honour (4:139) did not make them of disbelievers, nor did their standing for prayer to be seen (4:142) make them of believers; they remain between. The sūrah has shown two companies — hypocrites and disbelievers gathered together in Hell (4:140) versus those who believe and do good in Gardens forever (4:122) — and said *“do not sit with mockers else you are like them”* (4:140); the torn are those who sat and are like yet not counted fully until gathering makes like permanent. The image was also linked to the double safety seekers who wish safety from both sides (4:91) yet belong to neither where *fitnah* returns.

**And Whoever God Leaves to Stray, You Will Never Find a Way**

The seal *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu fa lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — and whoever God leaves to stray, causes to stray, leaves straying, you will never find for them a way — was explained with *yuḍlil* — to leave to stray, to allow deviation, to not guide — after they turned to what they chose. *Man yuḍlili Allāhu* matches *“do you wish to guide those left by God to stray?”* (4:88) where regressed hypocrites were allowed to regress because of misdeeds, and *“We will let them pursue what they chose”* (4:115) after defying the Messenger and following other than believers’ path. *Fa lan tajida lahū sabīlā* — you will never find for them a way — was explained as *sabīl* — way, path, argument, means — the same *sabīl* the sūrah said He will guide to noble ways (4:26), the path believers follow (4:115), and the way He will never grant disbelievers over believers (4:141).
