To find no way for the left-to-stray torn is to say no argument rescues, no alias of *ʿizzah* (4:139) provides way, no sitting as like them (4:140) provides way, no waiting as with winners (4:141) provides way, no outwitted deception (4:142) provides way. Early reports noted that the *mudhabdhab* is like sheep between two flocks, or like a lost beast between herders — the image emphasises belonging to none, found by none.

**A Verse That Follows Lazy Prayer With Wavering Belonging**

Placed after *they seek to deceive God but He outwits, they stand lazy to be seen hardly remembering* (4:142), this verse follows lazy prayer with wavering belonging that lazy prayer manifests. The sūrah has shown prayer as witness for Him even against selves (4:135), as remembrance standing, sitting, lying (4:103), as guarded under arms — the hypocrite’s lazy standing to be seen is witness for people, remembrance little, guard for show; the fruit is being *mudhabdhab* — neither these nor those. The sūrah has shown the community divided into two groups about hypocrites (4:88) asking *why are you two groups regarding hypocrites?*; here the hypocrite is himself two groups in one person — neither these nor those. The sūrah that commands to be mindful (4:131), to entrust to Him as *Wakīl* (4:132), to believe without wavering (4:136) here says wavering ends with no *sabīl* to be found, because the One who can remove and bring others (4:133) removes way from the torn.

**The Left to Stray After Many Clarities**

The phrase *wa man yuḍlili Allāhu* was explained as divine leaving after many clarities: association far astray (4:116), female gods invoked as Satan (4:117), Satan cursed taking share (4:118), ordering cutting and altering (4:119), promising only delusion (4:120), two abodes declared true (4:121–122), wishes not by wish (4:123), good with faith not wronged (4:124), best faith submission following Abraham (4:125), ownership and encompassing (4:126), instruction for orphan women (4:127), settlement best though selfishness present (4:128), impossible emotional equality yet do not incline entirely (4:129), enrichment after separation (4:130), universal command to be mindful (4:131), sufficiency as Trustee (4:132) — after all that, to remain *mudhabdhab* is not ignorance but straying left. The sūrah has said *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26–28) — clarity was given; wavering after clarity is the human turning that He lets be. For the weak this is a call to belong: where the sūrah says *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) next, the wavering between alliances is the proof to abandon, by choosing believers as like — *mithluhum* — for Gardens.

**A Short Verse That Freezes the Hypocrite Between**

Though only *“torn between neither these nor those, whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way,”* the verse freezes the hypocrite between. Immediately after: *O believers, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God proof against yourselves?* (4:144) — choose side. Immediately after: *hypocrites will be in lowest depth of Fire, you will never find helper* (4:145) — except those who repent, mend, hold fast to God and are sincere will be with believers and God will grant believers great reward (4:146). The torn between is therefore not a permanent station offered; it is the station that will be resolved either into lowest depth or into being with believers, according to whether repentance, mending, holding fast and sincerity replace wavering. The verse generalises the particular case of waiting between winners (4:141): waiting between is straying left, for whom no way will be found.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:144

> O believers! Do not take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Would you like to give Allah solid proof against yourselves?

**Expanded Commentary**

**O Believers — Do Not Take Disbelievers as Allies Instead of Believers**

The verse states *yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattakhidhū al-kāfirīna awliyāʾa min dūni al-muʾminīna* — O believers, do not take disbelievers as allies, guardians, protectors, instead of, apart from, believers. *Lā tattakhidhū awliyāʾ* — do not take as allies — repeats the same prohibition as *who choose disbelievers as allies instead of believers seeking honour* (4:139) where honour belongs to Him entirely, but now as direct command after the portrait of the torn between neither these nor those for whom no way is found (4:143). *Min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers, apart from them — was explained as choosing the other company while believers are available, as earlier *do not take them as allies unless they emigrate* (4:89) conditioned alliance on hijra, and as *those who are allies of a treaty people excepted* (4:90) honoured treaty, but this alliance is apart from believers altogether. The sūrah has traced *awliyāʾ* from the single soul’s family ties (4:1), to dowry and inheritance ties, to the emigrant’s haven, to Satan taken as guardian instead of Him suffering tremendous loss (4:119); to take disbelievers as guardians instead of believers is to take the cursed guardian’s share (4:118). Early reports illustrated the command where hypocrites cultivated disbelievers for protection against believers, assuming the believers’ trusteeship — *kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* (4:132) — was insufficient; the verse says trusteeship suffices, do not seek other.

**Would You Give God Solid Proof Against Yourselves?**

The question *a turīdūna an tajʿalū li Allāhi ʿalaykum sulṭānan mubīnā* — do you want to give, to make, for God against you a clear, manifest warrant, proof, authority? — was explained with *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant, manifest proof, evident authority — the same *sulṭān mubīn* given to you over the double-faced who do not withdraw or offer peace (4:91) — *We have given you clear warrant over such people*. Here the *sulṭān* is inverted: instead of clear warrant for you against the hostile turners, you give God clear warrant against yourselves by allying with disbelievers instead of believers. *Tajʿalū li Allāhi ʿalaykum* — to make for God against you — was explained as furnishing the prosecution evidence by act: to take allies instead of believers while the Book with truth judges between people (4:105) and while standing firm for justice though against yourselves is commanded (4:135) is to write your own proof. The sūrah has shown that association is not forgiven (4:116) and leaves far straying, and that the gathered hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140) is the gathering of the like — *mithluhum*; to give *sulṭān mubīn* against yourselves is to make that gathering just, because the proof — *ʿizzah* sought among disbelievers (4:139), sitting where signs are mocked (4:140), waiting to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted (4:142) — is manifest.

**A Verse That Follows Torn Between With Choice**

Placed after *torn between neither these nor those, whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way* (4:143), this verse follows the frozen between with a choice and its evidence. The torn between is told: do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers — decide the between. The sūrah has shown that guidance was made clear, noble ways taught, turning offered (4:26–28), and that He can remove you O humanity and bring others (4:133) — removal is the consequence of giving Him clear warrant against yourselves by choosing the other alliance. The sūrah has also shown that *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — to seek reward from disbelievers as allies is to seek little where both are with Him whose awareness is *Khabīr* of what you do (4:135, 4:128). The question *a turīdūna* — do you want? — was read as the Book’s appeal to will: do you intend to give proof against yourselves, or would you rather stand for justice even against yourselves and find Him All-Forgiving where you set right and are mindful (4:129–130)? The choice is not between honour and humiliation invented, but between proof for you — *sulṭān* over hostile turners (4:91) — and proof against you — *sulṭān* for Him over you.

**Alliance Instead of Believers as Proof**

The phrase *min dūni al-muʾminīn* — instead of believers — was explained to show that alliance with disbelievers is not forbidden where treaty or haven requires intercourse — the sūrah excepted those allied to treaty people (4:90), allowed laying aside weapons in rain yet keep precaution (4:102), and promised many havens among people (4:100); the prohibition is taking them as *awliyāʾ* — intimate guardians — instead of believers, as the oppressed cry for guardian and helper from grace (4:75) — guardian is to be from Him. Early notes added that the *sulṭān mubīn* against yourselves is not a metaphorical phrase but the record: night plotting with them (4:108) while He is with you, advocating for self-wrongers among them (4:107), hiding from people not from the Encompassing (4:108), will be brought as witness. Where the emigrant’s reward falls upon God secure (4:100), the ally-taker’s proof falls against himself secure, because the Trustee sufficient (4:132) keeps record that encompasses everything (4:126).

**A Short Verse That Anchors Proof in Alliance**

Though only *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?”* the verse anchors proof in alliance. Immediately after: *hypocrites will be in lowest depths of Fire and you will never find helper* (4:145) — except those who repent, mend, hold fast and are sincere will be with believers and God will grant believers great reward (4:146) — proof either stays or is erased by repentance and holding fast. The sūrah that warns not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) names this alliance as the desire that deviates: to seek protection or honour from those who disbelieve is to deviate from *qawwāmīn bi al-qisṭ* — ever standing for justice. For the weak this is the lightest protection: where you feared rising or turning away in household and were given settlement best (4:128), here you fear alliance with disbelievers for honour; the lightest is to belong with believers, whose path is submission following Abraham — best faith — whose friend is the Owner of heavens and earth, and not to give against yourselves the manifest proof whose gathering is together in Hell.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:145

> Surely the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire—and you will never find for them any helper—

**Expanded Commentary**

**Hypocrites Will Be in the Lowest Depths of the Fire**

The verse states *inna al-munāfiqīna fī al-darki al-asfali mina al-nāri* — surely the hypocrites will be, are, in the lowest depth, the bottom layer, the nethermost reach, of the Fire. *Dark* — depth, level, abyss — *asfal* — lowest — was explained as the deepest layer of Hell, below disbelievers gathered together with hypocrites (4:140), below the self-wronger’s Hell as home (4:97), below the defier’s burning (4:115), below the follower of Satan’s Hell without escape (4:121). *Mina al-nāri* — of the Fire — was read as the Fire whose preparation was humiliating for disbelievers where prayer was guarded (4:102), whose truth is contrasted with Gardens true (4:122), whose lowest depth is for those who deceive God while He outwits them (4:142), stand lazy to be seen (4:142), are torn between neither these nor those (4:143), and take disbelievers as allies giving God clear warrant against themselves (4:144). Early reports noted that the Fire has layers — *darakāt* — unlike Paradise’s *darajāt* — elevated ranks (4:96) — the lowest *dark* is for hypocrisy because hypocrisy is lowest in deceit: to invoke female gods besides Him and Satan (4:117) is open, to deceive while claiming belief is hidden and therefore lower. The sūrah has shown that the sitter where signs are mocked is like them (4:140) and will be gathered together; the lowest depth is the belonging of the torn who belonged to none.

**And You Will Never Find for Them Any Helper**

The clause *wa lan tajida lahum naṣīrā* — and you will never find for them any helper, protector, supporter — was explained with *naṣīr* — helper — the same *naṣīr* the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45) and that disbelievers as allies were sought for instead of believers (4:144). To find no *naṣīr* for hypocrites was read as that no *walī* and no *naṣīr* remains where they gave Him clear proof against themselves (4:144) and where *“whoever God leaves to stray you will never find a way”* (4:143). The phrase *lan tajida* — you will never find — was addressed to the Prophet ﷺ and to every searcher: no helper will be found for them, as the deceitful’s advocates in this life found no advocate before God on the Day (4:109) and no *wakīl* (4:109). The lowest depth without helper contrasts with Gardens promised to those who believe and do good where rivers flow and promise is true (4:122) and with enrichment from His bounty for those who separate (4:130). Where the emigrant finds many havens (4:100) and many refuges, the hypocrite finds lowest Fire and no helper, because heavens and earth belong to the One they deceived while He was with them at night plotting (4:108).

**A Verse That Follows Clear Warrant Against Selves With Depth Without Helper**

Placed after *do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?* (4:144), this verse follows the warning that taking that alliance gives clear *sulṭān* against yourselves with the consequence that follows manifest proof: lowest depth, no helper. The sūrah has built hypocrisy’s proof step by step: oscillation (4:137), announcing painful punishment (4:138), seeking honour among disbelievers (4:139), sitting where signs are mocked as like them (4:140), waiting to claim with winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, standing lazy to be seen remembering little (4:142), torn between neither (4:143), taking allies instead of believers (4:144) — lowest depth is the depth of that accumulation, as Gardens’ *darajāt* are the elevation of accumulated good where charity, kindness, reconciliation were commanded (4:114) and where prayer was guarded and remembered (4:102–103). Where the sūrah says *“do not let desires deviate from justice; if you distort or refuse He is All-Aware”* (4:135), hypocrisy deviates maximally — twisting testimony and refusing it — so depth is maximal and helper none.

**Lowest Depth as Counter to Elevated Ranks**

The *dark asfal* — lowest depth — was read as counter to *darajātin minhu* — ranks from Him (4:96) where strivers are elevated above sitters though both promised good. The sūrah has *darajāt* for strivers (4:96), forgiveness and mercy, and *darakāt* implied here for hypocrites; the lowest *dark* is the opposite pole to elevated ranks, as Hell without *maḥīṣ* (4:121) is opposite to Gardens forever. The sūrah that warns *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) says depth is not unheard or unseen; the All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) and Fully Aware muḥīṭ of everything (4:126) measures as not wronging even atom (4:40) yet depth for hypocrisy is atom-measure exact after many clarities rejected. For the weak this is clarifying: to be torn between (4:143) and to take disbelievers as allies (4:144) is not a safe middle — it is lowest; to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is to be with believers, whose path the next verse makes open by repentance, mending, holding fast, sincerity.

**A Short Verse That Holds the Gate Open One More Verse**

Though only *“hypocrites in lowest depths of the Fire, you will never find helper,”* the verse holds the gate open one more verse: its dash — *—* — in translation signals the exception — *illā alladhīna tābū* — except those who repent, mend, hold fast to God, and are sincere in devotion, they will be with believers and God will grant believers great reward (4:146). The sūrah has shown that whoever commits evil then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110), that seeking forgiveness is commanded between prohibitions to advocate (4:106), that whoever earns sin bears it upon self yet can seek and find (4:111, 4:110); depth without helper is the wage where none of those is done. The mercy that is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving (4:99) and All-Forgiving, Most Merciful (4:96) is not cancelled by depth — except — so that the lowest depth is not a fate sealed by lineage but by persisting in wavering and alliance, and the gate is sincerity after repentance.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:146

> except those who repent, mend their ways, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their devotion to Allah; they will be with the believers. And Allah will grant the believers a great reward.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Except Those Who Repent, Mend, Hold Fast, and Are Sincere**

The verse states *illā alladhīna tābū wa aṣlaḥū wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāhi wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāhi* — except those who repent, turned, and mended, set right, and held fast, clung, to God, and made their religion, devotion, sincere, pure for God. *Tābū* — to repent, to return — was explained with *tawbah* as the sūrah’s return after evil soon after error (4:17) before death’s *now I repent* (4:18), after deceit (4:106–110), after *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds”* (4:110). *Wa aṣlaḥū* — and mended, set right — was explained as mending what was corrupted: where night plotting disordered (4:108), where throwing sin on innocent burdened (4:112), where honour was sought among disbelievers (4:139), where sitting where signs are mocked made like them (4:140) — mending is *iṣlāḥ bayna al-nāsi* the good secret talk (4:114). *Wa iʿtaṣamū bi Allāhi* — and held fast to God, clung — was explained as the same *iʿtiṣām* commanded where those who believe in God and hold fast to Him will be admitted into mercy and guided through Straight Path (4:175), and where the emigrant to God has reward secured (4:100). *Wa akhlaṣū dīnahum li Allāhi* — and made devotion sincere, pure, for Him — was read as *ikhlāṣ* — purity from showing off where they stood lazy to be seen (4:142) and spent to show off (4:38); sincerity is the opposite of *riyāʾ* and of seeking *ʿizzah* among disbelievers (4:139). The four were explained as the hypocrite’s reversal: repentance reverses oscillation (4:137), mending reverses night plotting, holding fast reverses alliance with disbelievers instead of believers (4:144), sincerity reverses standing to be seen.

**They Will Be With the Believers**

The promise *fa ulāʾika maʿa al-muʾminīna* — then those — the repentant, mending, holding, sincere — will be with the believers, among them, counted as them — was explained with *maʿa* — with, together — the same *maʿa* the waiters claimed falsely — *were we not with you?* (4:141) — now true. To be *with believers* was read as not merely spared from lowest depth (4:145) but transferred to the other gathering: hypocrites and disbelievers gathered together in Hell (4:140) versus believers gathered with honourable company — prophets, truthful, martyrs, righteous (4:69). The sūrah has shown that those who obey God and Messenger will be with those blessed (4:69) and that whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than believers’ path is left to that path (4:115); those who repent and are sincere are returned to the believers’ path — *sabili al-muʾminīn* — after being torn between neither (4:143). The phrase was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, God’s promise ever true”* (4:122): to be with believers is to share that promise whose word none exceeds.

**And God Will Grant Believers a Great Reward**

The seal *wa sawfa yuʾti Allāhu al-muʾminīna ajran ʿaẓīmā* — And God will grant the believers, will give them, a great, mighty reward — was explained with *sawfa* — will, soon — certainty as the emigrant’s secured reward (4:100), and *ajran ʿaẓīmā* — great reward — the same *ajr ʿaẓīm* promised to those who command charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) and to strivers above sitters (4:95–96). To promise *ajr ʿaẓīm* to believers now inclusive of the repentant sincere was read as that their repentance does not make them second-class believers; mercy makes them believers. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) yet *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124); the sincere repentant’s good is now counted among that good. Where the hypocrites sought honour among disbelievers because all honour belongs to Him (4:139), great reward is the honour given to believers — not sought beside Him — because with Him are both rewards (4:134).

**A Verse That Follows Lowest Depth With Highest Return**

Placed after *hypocrites in lowest depths of Fire, you will never find helper* (4:145), this verse follows lowest with return. The sūrah has announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138), shown honour sought wrongly, sitting where mocked, waiting between, deceiving, lazy prayer, wavering, alliance giving clear proof against selves (4:138–144); here the same hypocrites — the *munāfiqīn* — are given four steps: repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing”* (4:147) — punishment is not needed where gratitude and faith are; these four are the gratitude and faith made operational. The sūrah that asks *“was not God’s earth spacious enough to emigrate?”* (4:97) and promises many havens (4:100) here says earth’s spaciousness includes a haven from lowest depth to being with believers, via sincerity. For the weak the sūrah lightens: where standing for justice though against yourselves was hard (4:135), holding fast to God is the stand; where settlement is best (4:128), mending is the settlement with Him; where *shuḥḥ* was present (4:128), sincerity removes it.

**Four Verbs That Reverse Four Hypocrisies**

The four — *tābū, aṣlaḥū, iʿtaṣamū, akhlaṣū* — were read as stepwise remedy for the hypocrite’s four defects: *tābū* heals oscillation (4:137) where belief was left, *aṣlaḥū* heals secret talk without good (4:114) where night plot and slander harmed, *iʿtaṣamū* heals alliance instead of believers (4:144) where trust was placed elsewhere, *akhlaṣū* heals *riyāʾ* — showing off — where prayer was for people (4:142). The verse generalises the judgment chapter’s medicine where *“whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving”* (4:110) — seeking is *tābū*, mending is *aṣlaḥū*, holding fast is reliance on *Wakīl* sufficient (4:132), sincerity is doing for Him not for show. The next verse will state the principle that makes these four sufficient: why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful — He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing (4:147), so that those with Him are promised great reward not out of need but appreciation.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:147

> Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and faithful? Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Why Should God Punish You If You Are Grateful and Faithful?**

The verse opens *mā yafʿalu Allāhu bi ʿadhābikum in shakartum wa āmantum* — what will God do with your punishment, why should He punish you, if you are grateful and have faith, are thankful and believing. *Mā yafʿalu bi ʿadhābikum* — what would He do with punishing you, what need for your punishment — was explained as rhetorical negation: He has no need to punish, as He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) though you disobey still to Him belongs all, and He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet does not punish where gratitude and faith are. *In shakartum wa āmantum* — if you are grateful and faithful — was read with *shukr* — gratitude, thankfulness — and *īmān* — faith, belief — the two that make the four — repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere (4:146) — the gratitude and faith that replace being torn between neither (4:143) and taking allies instead of believers (4:144). *Shakartum* was explained as gratitude shown in act: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114), doing good male or female with faith (4:124), submitting face doing good following Abraham (4:125), standing for justice (4:135), holding fast to Him (4:175). *Wa āmantum* — and have faith — was explained as comprehensive faith in God, Messenger, Books, angels, Last Day (4:136) renewed without wavering (4:136) — steadfast versus the oscillation that increased (4:137). Early reports linked the verse to the repentant hypocrites just promised being with believers and great reward (4:146): why should He punish if they are now grateful and faithful? The sūrah has shown that whoever seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving after evil (4:110) and that He forgives what is less than association for whom He wills (4:116); gratitude and faith are the seeking made character.

**Allah Is Ever Appreciative, All-Knowing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Shākiran ʿAlīmā* — And God is ever Appreciative, Thankful, Rewarding, All-Knowing — was explained with *Shākir* — Appreciative, Grateful, Repaying — the One who appreciates the grateful, rewards *shukr* with increase — *“if you are grateful I will increase you”* (14:7). *Shākir* was read as that He rewards the thankful who is grateful with great reward, as *“He will grant believers a great reward”* (4:146) and *“great is His favour upon you”* (4:113). *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — was explained as knowing gratitude and faith where they are hidden, as He is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126), All-Aware of what you do (4:128, 4:135), All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) — nothing of *shukr* or *īmān* escapes. The pairing *Shākir ʿAlīm* was linked to *Shākir Ḥamīd*? Actually *Shākir ʿAlīm* fits context where *shukr* is repaid: He knows gratitude, appreciates it. The sūrah has sealed many acts with knowledge names — *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* where sin is earned (4:111), *Muḥīṭ* where night plots (4:108); here *Shākir ʿAlīm* seals grateful faith as the act He rewards.

**A Verse That Follows Repentance With Principle**

Placed after *except those who repent, mend, hold fast, are sincere, they will be with believers and He will grant believers great reward* (4:146), this verse follows repentance with principle that explains why repentance works: why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? The sūrah has announced painful punishment to hypocrites (4:138) and lowest depth without helper (4:145) — yet showed exception; the principle answers implied question: does He punish because He needs to? — *mā yafʿalu* — He has no need, as He is Self-Sufficient (4:131) and suffices as Trustee (4:132). Where He can remove and bring others (4:133), He does not need to keep punishing. Where with Him are both rewards (4:134), He needs not withhold. The principle therefore transforms threat into invitation: the same God who declared *“neither by your wishes”* (4:123) and *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) says His *ʿadhāb* is not sought for itself; gratitude and faith remove its cause, and being Appreciative He rewards them. The sūrah’s ethic — stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), have faith entire (4:136) — is therefore not burden but gratitude that He appreciates.

**Grateful and Faithful as the Antidote to Hypocrisy**

The pair *shakartum wa āmantum* was explained as antidote to hypocrisy’s pair — deceiving and showing off (4:142): gratitude is sincerity in devotion where *riyāʾ* was, faith is holding fast where alliance instead of believers was. The sūrah has shown that Satan promises only delusion (4:120) — gratitude for true promise (4:122) counters delusion; that there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — grateful action commands those three. The verse was linked to *“if you are grateful, I will increase you; if you are ungrateful, My punishment is severe”* (14:7), showing that *shukr* increases the good while *kufr* — ingratitude — resembles the disbelief increase (4:137). The seal *Shākir ʿAlīm* therefore says: He who commanded to return trusts (4:58) will repay trust kept; He who knows what is in hearts (4:63) knows whether *shukr* was present with *shuḥḥ* (4:128) and whether *īmān* remained where *hawā* pulls (4:135).

**A Short Verse That Holds Needlessness and Appreciation Together**

Though only *“why should He punish you if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing,”* the verse holds needlessness and appreciation together. The chapter that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* (4:1), showed ownership to Him of heavens and earth, sufficiency as Trustee, capability to replace (4:126–133), warned not to take allies instead of believers lest you give clear proof against yourselves (4:144), declared lowest depth without helper (4:145) yet opened except for four — now says punishment itself is not His need, gratitude and faith are what He appreciates and knows. For the weak this is the lightest of principles: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), to be grateful where settlement waives and faithful where trust is held is not heavy, because the Appreciative knows it and will not punish where it is. The next passage will turn from principle to law of speech: He does not like negative thoughts voiced except by wronged, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing (4:148).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:148

> Allah does not like negative thoughts to be voiced—except by those who have been wronged. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

**Expanded Commentary**

**God Does Not Like Negative Thoughts Voiced — Except by Wronged**

The verse states *lā yuḥibbu Allāhu al-jahra bi al-sūʾi mina al-qawli illā man ẓulim* — God does not like, does not love, the loud voicing — *jahr* — of evil, bad, of speech, except by those who have been wronged, oppressed. *Al-jahra bi al-sūʾi mina al-qawli* — to voice evil loudly, to proclaim bad speech — was explained as public negative speech, complaint, accusation, vile talk, prayer against, as the sūrah has shown that those who hide from people but God is with them where they plot displeasing speech (4:108) have *sūʾ al-qawl* — evil speech — that He dislikes, and that advocates who dispute in this life for wrongdoers use evil loud speech (4:107–109). *Lā yuḥibbu* — does not like — parallels *does not like the deceitful sinner* (4:107) and *does not like the stingy boastful* (4:37); to voice *sūʾ* loudly is disliked as *shuḥḥ* and *khiyānah* are. *Illā man ẓulim* — except those who have been wronged — was explained as permission for the oppressed who cried for a helper — *mustaḍʿafīn* who cry *“deliver us from land of oppressors, appoint for us a saviour and helper”* (4:75) — to voice their wrong, to complain of oppression, to invoke against oppressor, to report injustice. The sūrah elsewhere commands to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) and permits settlement best (4:128) yet acknowledges *“no good in most secret talks”* (4:114); public *sūʾ* is the broad prohibition where secret plotting was already condemned, with exception for the wronged as the previous exception for helpless (4:98) — not every loud complaint is evil, the wronged’s is allowed.

**Allah Is All-Hearing, All-Knowing**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Samīʿan ʿAlīman* — And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, was ever — was explained with *Samīʿ* — hearing every *jahr* — loud voicing — and every *najwā* — secret talk — (4:114) and every night plot displeasing (4:108) — and *ʿAlīm* — knowing whether loud voicing is *sūʾ* or complaint of wronged, whether settlement sought graciously (4:128) or inclination total (4:129). *Samīʿ ʿAlīm* has sealed the command to return trusts and judge fairly (4:58) as *Samīʿ Baṣīr*, and the both rewards are with Him (4:134) as *Samīʿ Baṣīr*; here *Samīʿ ʿAlīm* fits speech: He hears loud evil and knows its motive, as He hears the oppressed cry (4:75) and knows the *ḥīla* absent (4:98). Early reports illustrated *man ẓulim* with one whose property was usurped or who was wronged by a spouse’s *nushūz* and who voices it for redress, not for slander — He hears and knows the difference between reporting wrong for justice and throwing sin on innocent as *buhtān* (4:112). The pairing says: public evil speech is disliked, yet He hears the wronged’s allowed voicing and knows its equity.

**A Verse That Follows Grateful Faith With Discipline of Loud Speech**

Placed after *why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing* (4:147), this verse follows grateful faith with discipline of loud speech. The sūrah has shown that whoever is grateful and faithful, He appreciates and knows; to voice *sūʾ* loudly is ingratitude in speech, as the deceitful’s night speech displeases Him (4:108) and advocates’ dispute for self-wrongers in this life is loud *sūʾ* — therefore *He does not like*. The exception *except wronged* was read as the sūrah’s justice: the oppressed whose help was commanded to be fought for (4:75), whose earth is made spacious (4:100), whose prayer is shortened and guarded (4:101–102) — their loud voicing is not *sūʾ* but *ḥaqq* — demand for right. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good* (4:114) except three, now warns *loud evil has no love* except one — the wronged’s. The sūrah that says *He wills to make clear* (4:26) and *taught you what you did not know* (4:113) makes loud evil undesirable because knowledge and wisdom will judge it as *ʿAlīm* hearing as *Samīʿ*.

**Loud Evil Versus Allowed Complaint**

The distinction — *jahr bi al-sūʾ* disliked versus *man ẓulim* allowed — was explained as same distinction as *no good in most secret talks* except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114): many loud complaints have no love, except the complaint of the wronged seeking charity of justice, kindness, reconciliation. The sūrah has shown that *ṣulḥ* — settlement best (4:128) — is sought where she fears *nushūz*, and that settlement may involve voicing grievance — that voicing is the *man ẓulim* allowed, not *sūʾ*. The *man ẓulim* was linked to *“do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended”* (4:129) — the suspended’s voicing of being suspended is allowed as wronged. Classical notes added that the wronged may invoke God against oppressor, or report oppressor to authority (4:59 referral), but not transgress beyond measure — the loud voicing remains measured by the All-Hearing.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Speech Between Love and Hearing**

Though only *“He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing,”* the verse anchors speech between love and hearing. The chapter has commanded to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), to verify reports (4:83), to be sure before fighting (4:94), to judge by what He shows (4:105), to command charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114), to stand for justice even against yourselves (4:135); all require voicing, but the verse adds qualifier: voicing *sūʾ* for its own sake is not loved, voicing wrong for justice is allowed and heard by the All-Hearing. For the weak this is the lightest of speeches: where you are wronged — the orphan deprived (4:127), the wife suspended (4:129), the party whose testimony is twisted — you may voice, and the One who can remove humanity (4:133) hears and knows, appreciates gratitude (4:147) yet dislikes loud *sūʾ* where no wrong was done. The next verse will set the higher ethic: whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil — surely He is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable (4:149) — so that the allowed voicing may still be surpassed by pardoning.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:149

> Whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil—surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Whether You Reveal or Conceal a Good or Pardon Evil**

The verse states *in tubdū khayran aw tukhfūhu aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾin* — whether you reveal, display, a good, make it apparent, or conceal it, hide it, or pardon, efface, an evil, bad deed. *Tubdū khayran* — to reveal a good — was explained as doing good openly: charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) where secret talk except those three has no good, and standing for justice as witnesses for Him even against yourselves (4:135) where testimony is revealing good. *Aw tukhfūhu* — or conceal it, hide it — was explained as doing good secretly: the charity waived charitably as blood-money (4:92) or dowry graciously waived (4:4), the good hidden where showing would be *riyāʾ* — showing off (4:38, 4:142). Both — revealing and concealing — were read as equal where intention is His pleasure, as *“whether you reveal or conceal a good”* the sūrah says both are known. *Aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾin* — or pardon an evil, overlook, efface a bad from another — was explained as pardoning the forgivable wrong done to you, after the permission for the wronged to voice loudly (4:148) was given; pardoning after voicing is the higher. *ʿAfā* — to pardon, to efface — the same root as *ʿAfuww* — Ever-Pardoning — the Name that seals. The sūrah has shown that settlement is best where she fears *nushūz* (4:128) and that settlement involves mutual graciousness; pardoning evil is that graciousness where grievance was voiced.

**Surely God Is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable**

The seal *fa inna Allāha kāna ʿAfuwwan Qadīrā* — surely God is, was ever, Ever-Pardoning, effacing, Most Capable, Powerful — was explained with *ʿAfuww* — much effacing, wiping away trace — the name that seals the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) and the reminder that He is Ever-Pardoning before prayer where purity is sought (4:43). *Qadīr* — Most Capable, Powerful over all — was explained as that He pardons though capable to punish, as He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet appreciates gratitude (4:147), as He owns heavens and earth (4:126) yet forgives what is less than association (4:116). To be *ʿAfuww Qadīr* was read as that pardoning evil after being wronged is divine imitation: you pardon though you are capable to voice and retaliate, as He pardons though He is Most Capable to punish. The pairing was linked to *“He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing”* (4:148) — the wronged is allowed to voice, yet the higher is to pardon, because the All-Hearing hears the wronged’s voicing and the *ʿAfuww Qadīr* shows the pardon that surpasses it. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant’s reward is secured though He could withhold (4:100), and that both rewards are with Him though He could give none; *ʿAfuww Qadīr* is that generosity made character for the believer.

**A Verse That Follows Permission to Voice With Invitation to Pardon**

Placed after *He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing* (4:148), this verse follows permission to voice with invitation to pardon that is higher than permission. The structure mirrors the household law: *settlement best* (4:128) after *fear of nushūz* is invitation beyond permission; *do not incline entirely* (4:129) is permission bounded; here *whether you reveal or conceal good or pardon evil* is invitation beyond the permission that the wronged may voice loudly. The sūrah has shown that most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation (4:114) — revealing or concealing good is that charity; and that standing for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is the good voiced where needed — pardoning evil is the good that forgives where justice’s voice could have condemned. Where the deceitful hide from people but He is with them displeased (4:108) and advocates dispute for self-wrongers (4:107), pardoning evil is the believer’s opposite: he effaces despite being wronged.

**Revealing or Concealing — Both Known, Both Rewarded**

The equalisation — *in tubdū … aw tukhfūhu* — was explained as removing show: whether good is displayed or hidden, it is good before Him who owns heavens and earth (4:126) and who is Fully Aware (4:126) and All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134). To reveal is not automatically *riyāʾ*, to conceal not automatically sincerity; both are *khayr* where sought for His pleasure (4:114). The verse was linked to *“everyone will find whatever good they did present”* (?) and to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): the revealed atom and the concealed atom are both present before the *ʿAlīm*. The addition *aw taʿfū ʿan sūʾ* was read as the highest *khayr*: pardoning the evil done to you is good concealed as forbearance, yet its effacement is most like His *ʿafw*. The sūrah has said *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing”* (4:147) — gratitude for good is shown by doing good whether revealed or hidden, and pardoning evil is gratitude that He is *ʿAfuww*.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Forbearance in Capability**

Though only *“whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil, surely He is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable,”* the verse anchors forbearance in capability. The chapter has commanded to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), to verify reports, to be sure before fighting, to judge by what He shows, to command charity, to stand for justice; all involve power to reveal good or to voice evil; the verse says the higher use of power is to pardon, as the Higher is Pardoning though Capable. For the weak this is the lightest of strengths: where you were wronged — the orphan whose wealth was devoured, the wife suspended, the party whose testimony was twisted — you may voice as wronged is allowed, yet if you pardon while capable, you meet the Name *ʿAfuww Qadīr* where He meets you. The next passage will turn from speech and pardon to creed: those who deny Him and His messengers making distinction between Him and messengers desiring compromise — they are true disbelievers, humiliating punishment prepared (4:150–151).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:150

> Surely those who deny Allah and His messengers and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” desiring to forge a compromise,

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Deny God and Messengers and Wish to Distinguish**

The verse opens *inna alladhīna yakfurūna bi Allāhi wa rusulihī wa yurīdūna an yufarriqū bayna Allāhi wa rusulihī* — surely those who deny, cover, God and His messengers and wish, intend, to make distinction, to separate, between God and His messengers. *Yakfurūna bi Allāhi wa rusulihī* — to deny God and messengers — was explained as denial that makes association far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after guidance clear following other than believers’ path (4:115). *Yurīdūna an yufarriqū bayna Allāhi wa rusulihī* — to wish to make distinction between God and messengers — was read as claiming belief in God without messengers, or in some messengers without others, as the sūrah has shown that the People of the Book demanded a written revelation from heaven yet demanded greater from Moses *show God visible* and were struck (4:153), and later said *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* (4:157) while denying him. To separate God from messengers was explained as theological *tafrīq* — dividing — where the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows the Messenger (4:105) and where obedience to Messenger is obedience to God (4:80): to claim God without Messenger is to claim a judge without showing. Early reports linked the verse to Jews who believed in Moses but disbelieved in Jesus and Muhammad ﷺ, and to Christians who believed in Jesus but disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ, both making distinction.

**Saying — We Believe in Some and Disbelieve in Others**

The speech *wa yaqūlūna nuʾminu bi baʿḍin wa nakfuru bi baʿḍin* — and they say, we believe in some and disbelieve in others, in some messengers we believe and in others we disbelieve — was explained as the distinction’s formula, the same compromise condemned where *“O believers, have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before”* (4:136) commanded comprehensive faith without selecting. *Nuʾminu bi baʿḍ* — we believe in some — was read as the partial faith that wishes grace by belonging — *neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — here the wish is *we believe in some messengers* as our group. *Wa nakfuru bi baʿḍ* — we disbelieve in some — was read as denial of those sent before and after, as the sūrah will say *they are true disbelievers* (4:151) and *those who believe in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards* (4:152). The sūrah has shown that those who believed then disbelieved then believed then increased (4:137) make similar speech; the formula *we believe in some and disbelieve in others* was explained as hypocrisy’s creedal side: to be *mudhabdhab* between neither these nor those (4:143) doctrinally. The phrase was linked to *“they say we hear and disobey”* (4:46) where Jews distort words; here distortion is selection of messengers.

**Desiring to Forge a Compromise**

The intention *wa yurīdūna an yattakhidhū bayna dhālika sabīlā* — and they wish, intend, to take, to forge between that — between belief in some and disbelief in some — a way, a path, a compromise — was explained with *sabīl* — way — the same *sabīl* the sūrah guides to noble ways (4:26), Satan wishes the deviant far path (4:60), believers’ path not to be left (4:115), and association far straying (4:116). *Bayna dhālika sabīlā* — between that a way — was read as seeking a middle way that is neither belief nor disbelief, neither *īmān* nor *kufr*, but a compromise doctrine where God is accepted and some messengers rejected. The sūrah has shown that *settlement is best* (4:128) where equitable compromise between spouses is good, but compromise between God and messengers is not settlement; it is *tafrīq*. The sūrah has also shown that *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — to take a way between believing and denying is the secret talk that has no good. The verse generalises the particular hypocrisy of waiting between winners (4:141) into theology: waiting between messengers to believe some and disbelieve some is desiring a *sabīl bayna dhālika* that is not a *sabīl* but straying left where no way is found (4:143).

**A Verse That Follows Pardon With Distinction**

Placed after *whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil, surely He is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable* (4:149) and after *He likes not loud evil except by wronged* (4:148), this verse follows pardon with distinction that refuses pardon where distinction persists without seeking. The sūrah has taught that grateful and faithful will not be punished because He is Appreciative, All-Knowing (4:147), and that repentance with mending, holding fast, sincerity makes hypocrites with believers (4:146); those who make distinction between God and messengers do not repent, do not mend, do not hold fast, do not make sincere — they desire a way between. The sūrah that began *“have faith in God, His Messenger, Book, Scriptures before”* (4:136) now defines the opposite as *“surely those who deny God and messengers wishing to make distinction”*; the comprehensive faith there is the remedy to distinction here. For the weak this is clarifying: where settlement between spouses is best (4:128) and settlement is desired, distinction between God and messengers is never settlement; to believe in some and disbelieve in others is not waiving part of right to keep marriage, it is claiming right to select the Sender.

**The Distinction That the Sūrah Has Named Two Kinds**

The phrase *yufarriqū bayna Allāhi wa rusulihī* was contrasted with the two distinctions the sūrah has condemned: distinguishing between *wishes* — *your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — and distinguishing between *messengers* — *we believe in some and disbelieve in others*. Both are *tafrīq* that seeks a *sabī l bayna dhālika* where none is, and both are answered with comprehensive faith: *believe in God, Messenger, Book and Scriptures, angels, Last Day* (4:136) and *believe in God and His messengers accepting all* (4:152). The verse was read as the sūrah’s answer to compromise theology: the only *sabīl* that is — is the believers’ path (4:115), submission fully to Him doing good following Abraham ḥanīf (4:125) — not a path between distinguishing. The next verse will declare the verdict: they are indeed the true disbelievers, and We have prepared for disbelievers a humiliating punishment (4:151).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:151

> they are indeed the true disbelievers. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.

**Expanded Commentary**

**They Are Indeed the True Disbelievers**

The verse completes *ulāʾika humu al-kāfirūna ḥaqqan* — they are — those who deny God and messengers and wish to distinguish between Him and His messengers saying *we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) — indeed, truly, the disbelievers in truth, the true disbelievers. *Ḥaqqan* — truly, in truth, as right, as due — was explained as the Book’s verdict after judgment by what He shows (4:105) that distinguishing God from messengers is not compromise but *kufr* in full, as *“whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray”* (4:136). *Humu al-kāfirūna* — they are the disbelievers — was read with emphasis: not merely among disbelievers, but they are them, for the sūrah has shown that taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers gives Him clear warrant against yourselves (4:144) and sitting where revelations are denied makes you like them (4:140); to make distinction between God and messengers is that like-ness made creed, so the verdict is *ḥaqq* — true — as God’s promise is *ḥaqq* (4:122) and Book was sent *bi al-ḥaqq* with truth (4:105). The sūrah has said *“they do not believe except few”* where hearts were sealed for disbelief (4:155); here *ḥaqqan* marks those few who believe as distinct from those truly disbelievers. Early reports added that hypocrisy’s *mudhabdhab* between neither these nor those (4:143) is not neutral: to desire a way between distinguishing is *ḥaqqan* disbelief.

**And We Have Prepared for Disbelievers a Humiliating Punishment**

The preparation *wa aʿtadnā li al-kāfirīna ʿadhāban muhīnā* — and We have prepared, made ready, for disbelievers a humiliating, degrading, debasing punishment — was explained with *aʿtadnā* — prepared, as the humiliating punishment was prepared for disbelievers where prayer was guarded under arms (4:102: *We have prepared humiliating punishment for disbelievers*), and for those given a portion who hide bounty (4:37: *humiliating punishment for disbelievers*), and will be for those who oppose the Messenger (4:115: *humiliating punishment* implicit). *ʿAdhāban muhīnā* — humiliating punishment — was read as humiliation corresponding to the *ʿizzah* — honour — they sought among disbelievers as allies (4:139) where *all honour belongs to Him entirely* — the honour sought among the wrong company becomes humiliation prepared. The sūrah has shown that the intentions to deceive God while He outwits (4:142) and to deceive the Prophet while grace protects (4:113) end in humiliation where deception’s honour is inverted. Where the sūrah says *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, would you give God clear proof against yourselves?”* (4:144) — *sulṭān mubīn* — preparation of humiliating punishment is the proof made sanction, because proof against yourselves was made clear by distinguishing.

**A Verse That Completes Distinction With Verdict**

Placed after *those who deny God and messengers wishing to distinguish saying we believe in some and disbelieve in others desiring a way between* (4:150), this verse completes distinction with verdict: they are indeed true disbelievers, We have prepared for disbelievers humiliating punishment. The sūrah has shown that belief was commanded as comprehensive — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before* (4:136) — steadfast, not selective, as the Way of Abraham pure (4:125) was not selective among associates; to be selective among messengers is to undo that comprehensive faith. The sūrah has shown that those who believe and do good are in Gardens true where promise is *ḥaqq* (4:122), while those who disbelieve are in Hell without escape (4:121); humiliating punishment is the disbeliever’s analog to honour sought. The phrase *aʿtadnā* — prepared — was linked to *“We have prepared humiliating punishment for disbelievers”* where guarded prayer stands (4:102): as prayer under arms guards against the enemy who wishes you neglect for a sweep (4:102), humiliating punishment guards against the theology that wishes you accept half the messengers and reject half as compromise. Elsewhere the Book ties that guard to *“Gardens under rivers where they abide forever”* (4:122) — comprehensive faith is the Gardens’ price, distinction its loss, and the comparison steadies the choice.

**Ḥaqqan Disbelief After Ḥaqqan Promise**

The word *ḥaqqan* — truly — for disbelievers was contrasted with *ḥaqqan* for promise: *waʿda Allāhi ḥaqqan* — promise ever true (4:122). The sūrah has used *ḥaqq* for Book — *bi al-ḥaqq* — and for promise and for verdict; truth is one. To call them *kāfirūna ḥaqqan* is to say the judgment that they are disbelievers is not by wish — *neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book* (4:123) — but by truth, as the sūrah says *whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly* (4:123) — distinction is evil rewarded accordingly where honour was sought. Where the sūrah says *“whose word more truthful than God’s?”* (4:122) — none — *ḥaqqan* here is His word: they are true disbelievers. For the weak this is clarifying: where settlement between spouses is best (4:128) and settlement is desired, compromise between God and messengers is never best; it is *ḥaqqan* disbelief whose preparation is humiliating.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Creed Before Its Opposite**

Though only *“they are indeed true disbelievers, We have prepared for disbelievers humiliating punishment,”* the verse anchors creed before its opposite — the subsequent verse will describe believers who accept all messengers receiving rewards (4:152). The two verses together frame the choice after distinction was described: desire a way between distinguishing and be counted true disbeliever with humiliating preparation, or accept all without rejecting any and be given rewards with forgiveness and mercy. The passage after that will turn to the People of the Book demanding a book from heaven (4:153).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:152

> As for those who believe in Allah and His messengers—accepting all; rejecting none—He will surely give them their rewards. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Believe in God and Messengers — Accepting All, Rejecting None**

The verse states *wa alladhīna āmanū bi Allāhi wa rusulihī wa lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* — and those who believe, have faith, in God and His messengers and did not make distinction between any of them, any one among them. *Āmanū bi Allāhi wa rusulihī* was explained as the comprehensive faith just commanded — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — now as description of its people. *Wa lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* — and did not make distinction between any one of them — was read as the opposite of *wishing to make distinction between God and messengers saying we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) where verdict was *true disbelievers, humiliating preparation* (4:151). To not distinguish between any messenger was explained as to accept all — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — all are God’s, none rejected. The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven yet demanded greater — *show God visible* from Moses (4:153) — and then took calf; distinguishing among messengers is that demand’s theology: to accept Moses but not Jesus or Muhammad ﷺ is modern calf after clear signs. To not distinguish was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — comprehensive belief is part of that good, as *millata Ibrāhīma ḥanīfā* (4:125) included all prophets in Abraham’s way.

**He Will Surely Give Them Their Rewards**

The promise *ulāʾika sawfa yuʾtīhim ujūrahum* — then to those — the comprehensive believers — He will surely, will soon, give them their rewards, their wages — was explained with *sawfa* — will, soon — certainty as the emigrant’s secured wage (4:100) and great reward for commanding charity (4:114) and great reward for being with believers after repentance (4:146). *Ujūrahum* — their rewards, wages — was read as *ajr* — wage — the same *ajr* that hypocrites sought as *ʿizzah* among disbelievers (4:139) but belong to Him entirely (4:139) and are both rewards with Him (4:134) — the believers’ wage is from Him, not from company sought. The verse generalises the promise where *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — the comprehensive believer is that doer; and *“who is better than those who submit face doing good following Abraham?”* (4:125) — submission includes accepting all messengers, so reward is friendship as Abraham was taken *khalīl* (4:125). Early notes linked *ujūrahum* to *“God wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26): wages are the mercy guided to.

**And God Is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu Ghafūran Raḥīmā* — And God is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful, was ever — was explained with *Ghafūr* — much forgiving, covering — and *Raḥīm* — ever merciful — the pair that seals grateful faith not punished (4:147), seeking forgiveness found (4:110), and universal pardon for less than association (4:116). To seal comprehensive belief with *Ghafūr Raḥīm* was read as that those who believe in all messengers still have faults needing cover, as the sūrah has shown that strivers need forgiveness among ranks (4:96) and emigrants find havens though weakness remains (4:100). *Ghafūr Raḥīm* here contrasts with *ʿadhāban muhīnā* — humiliating punishment prepared for true disbelievers (4:151) — showing that distinction’s wage is humiliation, comprehensiveness’s wage is forgiveness and mercy besides reward. Where the sūrah says *“He does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) and *“you will never be wronged even speck on date stone”* (4:124), the comprehensive believer’s reward is the atom not wronged yet multiplied many times; the Seal says the Multiplier is Forgiving, Merciful.

**A Verse That Follows True Disbelief With True Belief**

Placed after *they are indeed true disbelievers, We have prepared for disbelievers humiliating punishment* (4:151), this verse follows true disbelief with true belief and its opposite preparation: not humiliating punishment prepared but rewards given and forgiveness, mercy. The sūrah has moved from the passage on women, settlement, enrichment (4:127–130) through universal command to be mindful (4:131), trusteeship, capability, both rewards (4:131–134), standing for justice (4:135) with five articles of faith (4:136), oscillation without forgiveness or way (4:137), announcement of painful to hypocrites (4:138), alliance for honour (4:139), sitting where mocked as like them (4:140), waiting between winners (4:141), deceiving while being outwitted, lazy prayer (4:142), torn between (4:143), alliance giving clear proof (4:144), lowest depth without helper (4:145) except four — repent, mend, hold fast, be sincere (4:146) — the principle *why punish if grateful and faithful?* (4:147) — the discipline of loud evil except by wronged (4:148) and pardoning though capable (4:149) — distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150); here the opposite distinction — not distinguishing between any messenger — is rewarded. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) names comprehensive acceptance as the just faith.

**The Comprehensive Faith That Mirrors Comprehensiveness of Revelation**

The phrase *lam yufarriqū bayna aḥadin minhum* was explained as mirroring *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him”* (4:163): revelation is comprehensive, so faith is comprehensive. To accept all and reject none is to say the single soul spread into humanity (4:1) received guidance spread through prophets one after another, all from the Owner to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126). The sūrah has shown that the People of the Book demanded a single book from heaven as sign yet had demanded visible God from Moses (4:153); to accept all prophets is to accept that the Book’s descent is with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166), and God alone suffices as Witness, so that no demand for visible proof suspends belief in any messenger. For the weak this is the lightest completeness: where settlement between spouses is best (4:128) and where enrichment after separation is from His spaciousness (4:130), the comprehensive believer’s settlement with revelation is to take all, not to slit and alter (4:119), and his enrichment is rewards, forgiveness, mercy.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:153

> The People of the Book demand that you ˹O Prophet˺ bring down for them a revelation in writing from heaven. They demanded what is even greater than this from Moses, saying, “Make Allah visible to us!” So a thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf for worship after receiving clear signs. Still We forgave them for that ˹after their repentance˺ and gave Moses compelling proof.

**Expanded Commentary**

**The People of the Book Demand a Book From Heaven**

The verse opens *yasʾaluka ahlu al-kitābi an tunazzila ʿalayhim kitāban mina al-samāʾi* — the People of the Book ask you, demand of you, that you bring down upon them a book from the sky, a revelation in writing from heaven. *Ahlu al-kitābi* — People of the Book — was explained as Jews and Christians given Scripture before you — the same before you commanded to be mindful (4:131) — whose wishes are not the measure (4:123) and who were given a portion yet trade it for misguidance (4:44). *Yasʾaluka* — ask, demand — was read as challenging demand, as the sūrah has shown that they demand what is greater than this from Moses — *“make God visible”* — a demand that exceeds bringing a book from heaven. *An tunazzila kitāban mina al-samāʾ* — to bring down a book from heaven — was explained as requesting a written revelation descending as sheets, a physical book, as the Meccans demanded signs and as earlier they asked Moses to show God. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and that God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166); to demand a book from heaven as condition is to condition belief on spectacle. Early reports noted this demand followed the Prophet’s recitation of comprehensive faith (4:152): they said, if you are among messengers, bring a book as Moses brought tablets, otherwise we make distinction as before (4:150) — the sūrah exposes demand as continuation of distinguishing.

**They Demanded Greater Than That From Moses — Show Us God Visible**

The reminder *fa qad saʾalū Mūsā akbara min dhālika fa qālū arinā Allāha jahratan* — yet they demanded of Moses greater than that, saying show us God plainly, visibly, openly — was explained with *akbara min dhālika* — greater than that — the book from heaven. *Arinā Allāha jahratan* — show us God manifest, visibly, openly — was explained as demand for theophany, to see the Lord with eyes, as the sūrah elsewhere recounts *“they said, O Moses, we will not believe until we see God plainly, so the thunderbolt seized them”* (2:55). *Jahratan* — openly, plainly, manifestly — was read as that they demanded vision of the Ownership declared *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware* (4:126) — to see the Fully Aware plainly before believing the revealed Book. Elsewhere the Book notes that God suffices as Witness (4:166) and that disbelievers will be asked *what were you doing?* at soul-taking (4:97); to demand visible God is to refuse the witness of Book and angels. Classical notes added that Moses’ people demanded this after being delivered through sea and given manna, showing that spectacle does not produce faith where distinction remains.

**So a Thunderbolt Struck Them — Then They Took the Calf After Clear Signs**

The consequence *fa akhadhat-humu al-ṣāʿiqatu bi ẓulmihim* — so the thunderbolt seized them, struck them, for their wrongdoing — was explained with *ṣāʿiqah* — thunderbolt, striking — the same punishment that seized others who demanded signs with wrongdoing. *Bi ẓulmihim* — for their wrong, injustice — was read as that demand for visible God was injustice, as associating is far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose (4:115). *Thumma ittakhadhū al-ʿijla min baʿdi mā jāʾathumu al-bayyinātu* — then they took the calf for worship after clear signs came to them — was explained with *ʿijl* — calf — the golden calf worshipped while Moses was on the Mount, after receiving *bayyināt* — clear signs, evidences — the staff, the sea parted, the Mount raised over them (4:154). To take the calf for worship after clear signs was read as the chapter’s illustration of distinguishing: they demanded visible God and, when not given, took a visible calf — the worst substitution: from demanding the Most High visible to worshipping the lowest. Elsewhere the chapter notes they invoke female gods besides Him as Satan (4:117) and slit ears and alter creation (4:119); calf worship is the same — altering creation of respected animal into object of worship, then worshipping it.

**Still We Forgave Them and Gave Moses Compelling Proof**

The mercy *fa ʿafawnā ʿan dhālika wa ātaynā Mūsā sulṭānan mubīnā* — still We pardoned them for that, after their repentance, and We gave Moses clear, compelling, manifest authority, proof — was explained with *ʿafawnā* — We pardoned, effaced — the same root *ʿAfuww* — Ever-Pardoning (4:99, 4:149) — who pardons though Most Capable (4:149). The chapter has already noted that whoever wrongs themselves then seeks forgiveness finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110) and that the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99); here the calf-takers were forgiven after repentance where *“kill yourselves”* after calf was commanded (2:54). *Sulṭānan mubīnā* — clear warrant, compelling proof — was explained as the manifest authority Moses was given: tablets, the Mount raised, the *bayyināt* — clear signs — the sūrah will enumerate as Mount raised for covenant, *“enter the gate with humility, do not break Sabbath, firm covenant”* (4:154). The phrase *sulṭān mubīn* appears where hostile turners are given clear warrant over them (4:91) and where giving God clear warrant against yourselves is warned (4:144); here Moses’ *sulṭān mubīn* is the proof against those who demanded greater than a book.

**A Verse That Frames Demand With Forgiveness**

Placed after comprehensive belief rewarded with forgiveness and mercy (4:152) versus distinction as true disbelief with humiliating preparation (4:151), this verse frames demand for a book from heaven with history of greater demand — visible God — thunderbolt, calf after clear signs, yet pardon and compelling proof. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people and that God bears witness with His knowledge (4:166); to demand a book from heaven as condition is to condition acceptance of that witness on another witness. The sūrah that warns *“do not go to extremes regarding your faith, say nothing about God except truth, the Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him, do not say Trinity”* (4:171) here shows that extremes begin as demands for spectacle and end as calf worship — the visible made god when the Invisible is demanded visible. For the weak this is opening: where the calf after clear signs was forgiven after repentance, the sincere repentant with believers (4:146) is within that forgiveness, and Moses’ *sulṭān mubīn* is the proof that distinguishes demand from faith.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:154

> We raised the Mount over them ˹as a warning˺ for ˹breaking˺ their covenant and said, “Enter the gate ˹of Jerusalem˺ with humility.” We also warned them, “Do not break the Sabbath,” and took from them a firm covenant.

**Expanded Commentary**

**We Raised the Mount Over Them for Their Covenant**

The verse states *wa rafaʿnā fawqahumu al-ṭūra bi mīthāqihim* — and We raised the Mount — *al-Ṭūr* — Sinai, the mountain — over them, above them, because of their covenant, for breaking their covenant. *Rafaʿnā fawqahum* — We raised above them — was explained as God lifting Sinai over the Children of Israel as canopy until they accepted the covenant at Moses’ return, after the calf after clear signs had been forgiven and Moses given compelling proof — *sulṭānan mubīnā* (4:153). *Bi mīthāqihim* — for their covenant, with their covenant — was read as because the covenant required lifting as warning, as the sūrah has shown that *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126) and He is *Muḥīṭ* — encompassing (4:126) — the Mount raised is His ownership displayed. The sūrah has traced *mīthāq* — covenant — from the firm commitment of marriage — *mīthāq ghalīẓ* (4:21) — to treaty with covenanted peoples (4:90, 4:92) — to the firm covenant with the Children of Israel; to raise a mountain over them for breaking it was explained as the visible *sulṭān mubīn* that Moses was given (4:153) made physical, so that the covenant not kept remains above until kept.

**Enter the Gate With Humility and Do Not Break the Sabbath**

The commands *wa qulnā lahumu udkhulū al-bāba sujjadan wa qulnā lahum lā taʿdū fī al-sabti* — and We said to them, enter the gate — the gate of Jerusalem, the town — prostrating, with humility, bowing — and We said to them, do not transgress, exceed, in the Sabbath — were explained as two covenant details that display obedience versus demanding visible God (4:153). *Udkhulū al-bāba sujjadan* — enter the gate in prostration, bowing, humbled — was read as the entry into Jerusalem after wandering, where *“enter the gate with humility and say *ḥiṭṭa* — relief, forgiveness — We will forgive and increase the doers of good”* (2:58). To enter humbly was explained as the opposite of invoking female gods besides Him (4:117); to be told *lā taʿdū fī al-sabti* — do not transgress the Sabbath, do not exceed limits on the seventh day — was read as that the Sabbath was made test for them, as the sūrah elsewhere recounts the Sabbath-breaking town turned to apes (7:166). Both commands were linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — humility at the gate and restraint on the Sabbath are *ḥanīf* submission following Abraham whom He took as friend (4:125), not altering creation by hunting on the forbidden day.

**And We Took From Them a Firm Covenant**

The closure *wa akhadhnā minhum mīthāqan ghalīẓā* — and We took from them a firm, strong, solemn covenant — was explained with *ghalīẓ* — firm, weighty, strong — the same *mīthāq ghalīẓ* taken from women upon marriage (4:21) where dowry is not taken back unjustly — here the covenant with the community at Sinai. *Akhadhnā* — We took — was read as divine taking as witness, as *“God bears witness to what He sent”* (4:166) — the covenant is witnessed by the Mountain raised and by the gate entered. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); the firm covenant is the Book’s predecessor where the Mount was the witness. Early reports noted that the firmer the covenant, the firmer the punishment for breaking it — the thunderbolt struck them for demand greater than a book (4:153) — yet the *ʿafw* — pardoning — after calf showed the covenant also carries forgiveness where sought (4:110). The firm covenant was also linked to *taqwā* commanded to those before you and you (4:131) — *be mindful* — the covenant is the form of that *waṣiyyah*.

**A Verse That Follows Calf Forgiven With Mountain Raised**

Placed after the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven, demanded greater — visible God — were struck, took the calf after clear signs, yet were pardoned and Moses given compelling proof (4:153), this verse follows pardon with the covenant’s display: Mount raised over them for covenant, gate with humility, Sabbath not transgressed, firm covenant taken. The sequence — demand, thunderbolt, calf, pardon, proof — now — Mount raised — shows that pardon is not cancellation of law but renewal of law with visible witness. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth and God bears witness with His knowledge (4:166); the Mount raised is that witness made physical, as the emigrant’s many havens are earth made spacious (4:100). For the weak this is steadying: where you feared that firm covenant is too heavy, the Mount raised shows the covenant is not lighter than mountain, yet the Gate entered with humility shows it is entered bowed, not proudly, and Sabbath restraint shows it is kept by not doing, not only by doing, and the Pardoning after calf shows that where it was broken, return is through repentance still open.

**The Firm Covenant Above as Guardian**

The image — Mount above them for covenant — was explained as that the sūrah’s ownership — *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126) — becomes canopy, as prayer under arms was canopy guarded (4:102) and trusteeship suffices (4:132). The firm covenant — *ghalīẓ* — that is taken from them parallels the firm commitment taken from wives where wealth is entrusted (4:21); both teach that God’s earth is spacious (4:100) but covenant is not spacious to break. The verse generalises the sūrah’s warning *do not consume wealth unjustly* (4:29) into *do not transgress the Sabbath* — both are limits. The next verse will name the breaking: for breaking their covenant, rejecting His signs, killing prophets unjustly, saying *our hearts are unreceptive* — He sealed hearts for disbelief, so they believe only few — (4:155).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:155

> ˹They were condemned˺ for breaking their covenant, rejecting Allah’s signs, killing the prophets unjustly, and for saying, “Our hearts are unreceptive!”—it is Allah Who has sealed their hearts for their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few—

**Expanded Commentary**

**For Breaking Covenant, Rejecting Signs, Killing Prophets**

The verse opens *fa bi mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum wa kufrihim bi āyāti Allāhi wa qatlihim al-anbiyāʾa bi ghayri ḥaqq* — so for their breaking their covenant, and rejecting His signs, and killing the prophets — *anbiyāʾ* — without right. *Bi mā naqḍihim mīthāqahum* — for their breaking their covenant — corresponds to the firm covenant taken at the Mount raised over them and the gate with humility and Sabbath restraint (4:154): where Mount was raised for covenant, they broke it. *Wa kufrihim bi āyāti Allāhi* — and rejecting, covering His signs — was explained as denying the *bayyināt* — clear signs — after which calf was taken (4:153) and Mount raised (4:154): staff, sea, manna, cloud, tablets — all *sulṭān mubīn* Moses was given. *Wa qatlihim al-anbiyāʾa bi ghayri ḥaqq* — and killing prophets without right, unjustly — was explained as murdering some prophets where *“whenever a messenger came with what souls desired not, you grew arrogant, some you denied, some you killed”* (2:87), culminating later with attempt on Jesus, son of Mary, messenger of God (4:157). The sūrah has traced murder’s weight: devouring orphans’ wealth is fire (4:10), killing a believer intentionally is Hell with anger and curse (4:93), throwing sin on the innocent bears slander (4:112) — killing prophets without right is the furthest throw: to throw God’s word back by killing its carrier. The phrase was linked to *“they were condemned for breaking covenant”* as the sūrah’s ledger where *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123).

**And for Saying — Our Hearts Are Unreceptive**

The addition *wa qawlihim qulūbunā ghulf* — and for saying, their word, *our hearts are wrapped, unreceptive, enclosed, covered* — was explained as excuse for rejecting signs: *ghulf* — wrapped, covered, uncircumcised, sealed — as they said *our hearts are covered* we cannot hear the Book with truth (4:105). The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth that God bears witness to with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166), and that He is sufficient as Trustee (4:132); to say *our hearts are ghulf* is to claim the heart cannot receive witness, where earlier the sūrah says *“they hardly comprehend anything”* (4:78) not because heart is *ghulf* but because they hardly reflect. *Ghul f* was read as their claim that hearts are closed and cannot hear, as if ownership of heavens and earth (4:126) cannot open them, where the sūrah elsewhere says *He has sealed their hearts for disbelief, so they believe only few* — sealing is not excuse but consequence.

**It Is God Who Has Sealed Hearts for Disbelief**

The correction *bal ṭabaʿa Allāhu ʿalayhā bi kufrihim* — rather, it is God who has sealed, stamped, upon them, over hearts, for their disbelief, because of their disbelief — was explained as divine sealing after human rejection. *Ṭabaʿa* — to seal, to stamp, to imprint — was read as the same sealing after breaking covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets without right — the sūrah’s causality: disbelief precedes sealing, sealing confirms disbelief. *Bi kufrihim* — for their *kufr*, because of their covering — was explained as that He left to stray where they pursued what they chose: *We will let them pursue what they chose* (4:115) after defying the Messenger, and *whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way* (4:88, 4:143) — sealing is that leaving. The phrase was linked to *“God has condemned them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except few”* (4:46) where some Jews take words out of context — sealing there also followed distortion. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — sealing is not where gratitude and faith are, but where *kufr* repeats.

**So They Do Not Believe Except for Few**

The outcome *fa lā yuʾminūna illā qalīlā* — so they do not believe — will not believe — except for a little, except a few — was explained with *qalīl* — little, few — as little belief after sealing, as the sūrah says *we took calf after clear signs yet forgave* (4:153) — some repented — and *but those well-grounded in knowledge among them believe in what was revealed to you and before you* (4:162) — few stand firm.
