The sūrah has shown that *“whoever believes in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards”* (4:152) — the few who believe except few are those who accepted all without distinction (4:150–152). *Illā qalīlan* — except a few — was linked to the beginning where *“you were divided into two groups about hypocrites while God allowed regression because of misdeeds”* (4:88) — few remained straight. The exception preserves hope where the lowest depth for hypocrites also allowed *except those who repent* (4:146): sealing is not absolute where a few believe.

**A Verse That Binds Broken Covenant to Sealed Hearts**

Placed after Mount raised for covenant, gate with humility, Sabbath restraint, firm covenant (4:154), this verse binds broken covenant to sealed hearts after rejecting signs and killing prophets unjustly and saying hearts are *ghulf*. The sūrah has shown that to Allah belongs whatever is in heavens and earth and He is Fully Aware (4:126), that He suffices as Trustee (4:132), that with Him are both rewards (4:134); to claim *our hearts are ghulf* before such Owner and Aware is to refuse the Trust, so sealing is the Trusteeship withdrawn where trust was broken. The verse generalises the particular hypocrisy of waiting between (4:141) into covenantal history: the People of the Book who demanded a book from heaven as condition and demanded visible God (4:153) are the same who broke covenant, rejected signs, killed prophets, claimed hearts are closed — sealing follows claiming closed. The next verses will continue that condemnation: for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary, and boasting *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* — but they killed not nor crucified — it was made to appear so — they have no knowledge, only assumptions — they certainly did not kill him (4:156–157).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:156

> and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary,

**Expanded Commentary**

**And for Their Denial and Outrageous Accusation Against Mary**

The verse continues *wa bi kufrihim wa qawlihim ʿalā Maryama buhtānan ʿaẓīmā* — and for their denial, their *kufr*, and their word against Mary, their saying upon Mary as a tremendous, mighty slander — *buhtān ʿaẓīm*. *Bi kufrihim* — for their denial — was explained as continuation of the accumulated causes for condemnation — breaking covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets unjustly, saying hearts are *ghulf* sealed for disbelief (4:155) — now denial as such and slander against Maryam. *Wa qawlihim ʿalā Maryama buhtānan ʿaẓīmā* — and their saying against Mary as mighty slander — was explained with *buhtān* — slander, calumny, false accusation that bewilders — the same *buhtān* and manifest sin borne by whoever throws sin on the innocent (4:112), now against the innocent Maryam, mother of the Messiah. *ʿAẓīm* — mighty, tremendous, great — was explained as that slander against Maryam is not private insult but defamation of the *ṣiddīqah* chosen, the Word through her — *“the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was but messenger of God and His Word through Mary and spirit from Him”* (4:171), whose mother was *“above women of the worlds”* in reports. Those who consume orphans’ wealth consume fire (4:10) and throwing sin on the innocent bears slander (4:112); to slander Maryam with unchastity — accusing the pure who was given a spirit — is the throw of sin upon the purest, therefore *ʿaẓīm*. Early reports noted that the Jews who rejected Jesus accused Maryam of *zina* — fornication — to deny his messengership, as they denied all messengers where distinguishing is true disbelief (4:151); the verse names the slander as *buhtān ʿaẓīm* because it combines denial of a prophet with defamation of his mother.

**A Verse That Continues Broken Covenant With Mary’s Slander**

Placed after broken covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets, saying hearts are *ghulf* sealed (4:155), this verse continues the same condemnation with the next instance: denial and mighty slander against Mary. Demand for a book from heaven and the greater demand — *show God visible* — were struck, followed by the calf after clear signs yet forgiven (4:153), and the Mount raised for firm covenant (4:154); slander against Mary is the next breaking: after calf — idol — after rejecting signs, they reject the sign of Mary’s purity and Jesus’ birth without father as Word. The later reminder that *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — all accepted without distinction (4:152) — shows that to slander Mary is to reject that chain that includes Jesus. The verse was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — Mary believed and did good; to accuse her is to refuse that good. For the weak this is protective: where orphan women deprived yet wished to marry are protected from being married for profit (4:127), Mary the most deprived — alone — is protected by God naming slander against her as *ʿaẓīm*.

**The *Buhtān* That Mirrors Throwing Sin on the Innocent**

The word *buhtān* — mighty slander — was explained to mirror *iḥtamala buhtānan wa ithman mubīnā* — bears slander and manifest sin — where one throws sin on the innocent (4:112). There the innocent was a neighbour Jew accused of theft; here the innocent is Maryam, accused to deny messengership. Earlier passages note that *“there is no good in most secret talks except charity, kindness, reconciliation”* (4:114); slander of Mary is the evil secret talk that has no good. Elsewhere the Book teaches that *“He does not like loud negative speech except by wronged”* (4:148) — accusation against Mary is negative speech not by wronged but by wrongdoer, therefore not allowed, therefore not liked, therefore *ʿaẓīm*. That same teaching was linked to *“He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing”* (4:148): the accusers of Mary voiced *buhtān ʿaẓīm* where they were not wronged but wronging.

**Denial that Precedes Slander**

The pairing *wa bi kufrihim wa qawlihim* — and for their denial and their saying — was explained to show that slander follows denial: denial of Jesus as messenger makes slander of Mary as pretext, as those who wish to make distinction between God and messengers say *we believe in some and disbelieve in some* (4:150) — to disbelieve in Jesus they slander his mother. Association is far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose (4:115); denial and slander here are that defiance applied to the Messiah. Early notes added that Maryam’s chastity was attested by *“We breathed into her Our spirit”* (66:12) and by Jesus speaking in cradle; to deny the son is to need to deny the mother, so *buhtān* becomes necessary. The shortness — *and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary* — was read as the sūrah’s compression where the next verse expands denial into boasting *we killed the Messiah* (4:157) — denial moves from slandering mother to boasting murder of son, both false.

**A Short Phrase That Anchors Accusation as Cause of Condemnation**

Though only *“and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary — mighty slander,”* the phrase anchors accusation as cause of condemnation beside breaking covenant and killing prophets. The shortness makes the history — demand, thunderbolt, calf, Mount, gate, Sabbath, breaking, rejecting, killing, saying hearts are *ghulf*, denial, slander — a litany of one people’s repeated breaking, yet the sūrah will still note *but those well-grounded in knowledge among them believe* (4:162) — few — so that the *buhtān ʿaẓīm* is not extended to all. The next verse will complete that denial: boasting *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* — but they killed not nor crucified, it was made to appear, they have no knowledge only assumptions, they certainly did not kill him (4:157).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:157

> and for boasting, “We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.” But they neither killed nor crucified him—it was only made to appear so. Even those who argue for this ˹crucifixion˺ are in doubt. They have no knowledge whatsoever—only making assumptions. They certainly did not kill him.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Boasting — We Killed the Messiah, Son of Mary, Messenger of God**

The verse continues *wa qawlihim innā qatalnā al-masīḥa ʿĪsā ibna Maryama rasūla Allāhi* — and for their saying, their boast, *indeed we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of God*. *Qawlihim* — their saying — was explained as continuation of *“and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary”* (4:156) — now the boast. *Innā qatalnā al-masīḥa* — we killed the Messiah — *masīḥ* — anointed, Messiah — was read as Jesus, *ʿĪsā ibnu Maryam*, whose mother was slandered as *buhtān ʿaẓīm* (4:156) and whose son they claim to have killed. *Rasūla Allāhi* — the messenger of God — was explained as their own designation with irony: they say *messenger of God* mockingly while claiming to have killed him, as they said *our hearts are ghulf* (4:155) mockingly while hearts were sealed for disbelief. The sūrah has shown that killing prophets without right is part of condemnation (4:155) — to boast of killing the Messiah is the apex: to claim murder of a messenger sent without distinguishing (4:152) and of the Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171). Early reports noted this boast was by Jews who did not kill Jesus but claimed credit, while the attempt was by Roman authority at their instigation; the Qur’anic *we killed* attributes the pride to them as the planners, as夜 plotting is attributed though God is with them (4:108).

**But They Killed Not Nor Crucified — It Was Made to Appear**

The correction *wa mā qatalūhu wa mā ṣalabūhu wa lākin shubbiha lahum* — but they killed him not and they crucified him not, but it was made to appear so to them, made similar, made like — was explained as divine negation. *Wa mā qatalūhu* — they killed him not — *wa mā ṣalabūhu* — nor crucified — double negation was read as absolute: the act claimed — *qatalnā* — did not occur upon him. *Wa lākin shubbiha lahum* — but it was made to appear so to them, made to seem like him — was explained as a likeness cast onto another killed in his stead, or as the event made ambiguous so that observers differed, so that the boasters thought they killed him while God raised him. The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — He saw the plotting and raised. Classical reports differed: some said a disciple was made to resemble Jesus and was killed; others said one of the plotters was; all agree *shubbiha lahum* means resemblance was made. The verse was linked to *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40): to claim killing the messenger is to claim wronging the atom mostWeight; the correction says wrong did not reach him.

**Those Who Argue for Crucifixion Are in Doubt — No Knowledge Only Assumptions**

The addition *wa inna alladhīna ikhtalafū fīhi la fī shakkin minhu mā lahum bihī min ʿilmin illā ittibāʿa al-ẓann* — and surely those who disputed, differed, concerning him — about him, crucifixion — are surely in doubt regarding him, in *shakk* — doubt, suspicion — not having any knowledge concerning it except following assumption, conjecture — was explained with *ikhtalafū* — to differ — the same difference the community was warned not to make between God and messengers (4:150) and not to fall into other than believers’ path (4:115). *La fī shakkin minhu* — in doubt regarding him — was read as that those who argue for *we killed* are not agreed: some say killed, some say crucified, some say neither, all in *shakk*, as the sūrah elsewhere says those given a portion distort words (4:46). *Mā lahum bihī min ʿilmin illā ittibāʿa al-ẓann* — they have no knowledge whatsoever except following *ẓann* — assumption — was explained as that their claim lacks *ʿilm* — knowledge — the sūrah has contrasted *ẓann* with *ḥaqq* — *promise ever true* (4:122) versus delusion (4:120) — *ẓann* is Satan’s currency. Where God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge (4:166) and angels bear witness, the crucifixion claim is *ittibāʿ al-ẓann* — following conjecture — not witness.

**They Certainly Did Not Kill Him**

The seal *wa mā qatalūhu yaqīnan* — and they certainly did not kill him, not in certainty — was explained with *yaqīn* — certain, firm, sure — negated as *they killed him not with certainty* — they have no certain killing, and *they certainly did not kill him* — emphatic. The adverb *yaqīnan* was read as again negating the boast *qatalnā* — we killed — with certainty’s opposite: not only did they not kill, they have no certainty that they did. The sūrah has shown that *“He wills to make clear”* (4:26), *“taught you what you did not know”* (4:113), *“most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation”* (4:114) — boasting murder is not clear but doubtful; the decisive word is that they did not kill him in truth, as the next verse says *rather God raised him to Himself, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:158). For the weak this is an anchor: where loud negative speech is allowed to the wronged (4:148) and pardoning is higher (4:149), loud boasting *we killed the messenger* is the loudest *sūʾ* not allowed where no wrong was done to the boaster.

**A Verse That Completes Denial With Correction and Doubt**

Placed after breaking covenant, rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming hearts are *ghulf* sealed (4:155), denial and mighty slander against Mary (4:156), this verse completes denial with boasting of murder corrected and doubt exposed. The litany — demand greater than a book, thunderbolt, calf after clear signs yet forgiven, Mount raised, gate with humility, Sabbath not transgressed, firm covenant, then breaking, rejecting, killing, saying *ghulf*, denying, slandering Mary, boasting killing Messiah — is the sūrah’s history of a people given Scripture before you commanded to be mindful (4:131) yet whose mindfulness was broken. The correction — not killed, not crucified, it was made to appear, disputants are in doubt, no knowledge but following assumption, certainly not killed — was read as the Book’s truth against assumption, as the Book was sent *bi al-ḥaqq* with truth (4:105) and *waʿduhu ḥaqq* (4:122). The next verse will set the truth: rather God raised him to Himself, He is Almighty, All-Wise (4:158), and every one of People of the Book will believe in him before his death and on Resurrection Day he will be witness against them (4:159).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:158

> Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself. And Allah is Almighty, AllWise.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Rather God Raised Him to Himself**

The verse states *bal rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayhi* — rather, nay, but God raised him, lifted him, up to Him, to Himself. *Bal* — rather — was explained as correction to *they killed him not nor crucified, it was made to appear* (4:157), where boasting *we killed the Messiah, son of Mary, messenger of God* was negated; *rather* His raising is the truth. *Rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayhi* — God raised him to Him — was explained as God lifting Jesus alive to Himself, as He raised the Mount over them for covenant (4:154) — raising Mount as warning, raising Jesus as honour — the sūrah’s two raisings: one over breakers to frighten, one of the messenger to preserve. *Ilayhi* — to Him, to Himself — was read as to His presence, to the heavens, as the sūrah elsewhere says *“He raised him to Himself”* and the sūrah says *O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Me”* (3:55). Early reports noted that Jesus was raised while his likeness was cast on another; the *shubbiha lahum* — made to appear — is explained by *rafaʿahu* — raised. Scripture has shown that God suffices as Trustee (4:132) and bears witness with His knowledge (4:166); raising the messenger is His trusteeship executed, as He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet here removes the messenger from killers and brings him to Himself, preserving the line of revelation. The phrase was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — raising is the Gardens’ prototype: honour of nearness.

**And God Is Almighty, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīmā* — And God is Almighty, All-Powerful, All-Wise, was ever — was explained with *ʿAzīz* — Almighty, Mighty, invincible — the One who can raise against killers, as He is *Qadīr* — Most Capable to remove humanity (4:133) and *Qadīr* to pardon though capable to punish (4:149) — here *ʿAzīz* is capability to protect messenger where boasters claim killing. *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — was read as wisdom that made likeness to appear to boasters while raising, that let disputants remain in doubt following assumption (4:157), and that will make his future testimony decisive. *ʿAzīz Ḥakīm* was also the seal for messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers (4:165), showing that raising Jesus preserves the messenger lineage until the final messenger — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him”* (4:163) — all sent by the Almighty, All-Wise. Where the sūrah says *all honour belongs to Him entirely* (4:139) sought by taking disbelievers as allies, Jesus raised to Him is the honour given to the messenger whose *ʿizzah* boasters thought they terminated.

**A Verse That Follows Not Killed With Raised**

Placed after thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount, gate, Sabbath, firm covenant, then breaking, rejecting, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf*, denying, slandering Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed nor crucified, it was made to appear, disputants in doubt, no knowledge but assumption, certainly not killed (4:153–157), this verse follows *not killed* with *raised*. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126, 4:131) — raising to Him is raising within His ownership; His heavens are the *maḥīṭ* — encompassing (4:126) — that can receive. The sūrah has shown that *“He does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) — to raise the messenger whom they wrongly boasted killing is not wronging the atom but preserving it. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) sees boasting murder as the worst secret talk made loud boast; raising is its rebuttal as public honour.

**Raising as the Sūrah’s Reply to Visible Demand**

The raising *rafaʿahu Allāhu ilayhi* was linked to the initial demand — *bring down a book from heaven* (4:153) and *show God visible* — the demand for visible spectacle: those who demanded visible God and then took visible calf are now shown that the visible messenger they boasted visible killing was made invisible by raising — spectacle’s opposite. Where Moses’ people saw the Mount raised over them as warning for covenant, the Messiah’s people who boasted murder are shown that God raises whom He wills. The verse was read with *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah…”* (4:163) — revelation continues, messengers are many, raising one does not end mission; the final reminder — *“there are messengers We told you and others We did not, and to Moses He spoke directly”* (4:164) — shows His *kalām* reaches directly and His raising reaches powerfully. For the weak this is an anchor: where the Messiah was wronged by boasters while being God’s Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171) not too proud to be servant (4:172), His raising shows the servant honoured though boasters claimed killing.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Witness to Come**

Though only *“Rather God raised him to Himself, He is Almighty, All-Wise,”* the verse anchors the witness to come: the raised Messiah will be believed in by many before the end, and will stand as witness on the Day. The sūrah that bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166) makes that future testimony part of its proof. The next passage will turn from history of the Book’s People to law general: forbidden foods, usury, and unjust wealth — painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but great reward for those grounded in knowledge who believe in what was revealed to you and before. That reward is the *ajran ʿaẓīmā* — great reward — He keeps for the grounded in knowledge (4:162).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:159

> Every one of the People of the Book will definitely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Judgment Jesus will be a witness against them.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Every One of the People of the Book Will Believe in Him Before His Death**

The verse states *wa in min ahli al-kitābi illā la yuʾminanna bihī qabla mawtihī* — and there is none among the People of the Book except he will surely believe in him before his death, before their death, before his. *In min ahli al-kitābi illā* — there is none among People of the Book except — was explained as universal quantifier: every one of the Jews and Christians given Scripture before you (4:131) will believe. *La yuʾminanna bihī* — will surely believe in him — was read with emphasis: the same *la* + *nūn* as Satan’s vow, now as God’s oath; belief will be in Jesus — *ʿĪsā ibnu Maryam* — the Messiah whom they boasted killing but did not, whom God raised to Himself (4:157–158), the Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171). *Qabla mawtihī* — before his death — was read two ways: before the death of the Person of the Book — each will believe when death nears and truth becomes clear, as *“repentance not accepted when death is starting and he cries now I repent”* (4:18) — too late; and before the death of Jesus himself upon his return before the Hour, when he will descend and break cross, as reports state (Bukhārī 3448; Muslim 155). Both readings were kept: the People of the Book will see before their own death the truth of Jesus, and collectively before Jesus’ own second death the People of the Book will believe. The sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers saying we believe in some and disbelieve in some desire a way between (4:150) — they are true disbelievers (4:151); this belief before death is the undoing of that distinguishing, as the People of the Book finally accept Jesus as messenger not god.

**And on the Day He Will Be a Witness Against Them**

The second clause *wa yawma al-qiyāmati yakūnu ʿalayhim shahīdā* — and on the Day of Standing, of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them, upon them — was explained with *shahīd* — witness — the same witness as *“We will bring a witness from every community and bring you as witness against yours”* (4:41) where the Prophet ﷺ is witness against his community, and *“God bears witness and angels bear witness”* (4:166) — here Jesus will be witness against those who made distinction. *ʿAlayhim* — against them, upon them — was read as that Jesus will testify: they said we killed the Messiah, we slandered Mary with mighty *buhtān* (4:156), they said our hearts are *ghulf* (4:155) — he will witness that they knew and denied, as the soul-takers will ask *what were you doing?* (4:97). *Yawma al-qiyāmati* was explained as the Day about which there is no doubt where He will gather you (4:87) and gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (4:140); witness on that Day decides gathering. Classical notes added that his being *shahīd* against them fits his raising: he who was raised above boasting murder now descends as witness that murder did not occur, and the *shubbiha lahum* — made to appear — will be clarified by the one raised.

**A Verse That Follows Raised With Belief Before Death**

Placed after *rather God raised him to Himself, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:158), this verse follows raised with belief before death and witness on the Day. The sequence — demand, thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing prophets, hearts *ghulf* sealed, denial, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised — now belief in him before death, witness on the Day — shows that history of the Book’s People does not end with calf or *shubbiha* but with belief and witness. The sūrah has shown that *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him”* (4:163) — all accepted without distinction (4:152); the People of the Book’s belief in Jesus before his death is the correction of distinction where Jesus is among those prophets. For the weak this is an opening: where loud negative speech about Mary was not allowed (4:148), belief in the son of Mary before death is the speech that repairs, and the raised witness who was not too proud to be servant (4:172) will witness that repair.

**Before His Death — Two Times for Witness**

The phrase *qabla mawtihī* was explained to keep two times for witness: before the death of each of the People of the Book — at the threshold where angels take souls and ask *what were you doing?* (4:97) — truth becomes clear but too late as repentance at death is not accepted (4:18); and before the death of Jesus upon his return — a communal time where the People of the Book will believe while still alive before the Hour, as *“there are messengers We told you and others We did not”* (4:164) shows knowledge is with Him. To say *every one will believe in him before his death* was therefore read not as claim that all die as believers — because humiliating punishment was prepared for true disbelievers (4:151) — but as that at death’s veiling removed, each will see, yet seeing after sight is too late for those who increased in disbelief (4:137). The witness on the Day — *shahīdan ʿalayhim* — is the sūrah’s *“how will it be when We bring witness from every community and you as witness against yours?”* (4:41) — here Jesus is that witness for his community.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Future Belief to Past Boast**

Though only *“Every one of People of the Book will definitely believe in him before his death, and on the Day Jesus will be witness against them,”* the verse anchors future belief to past boast *we killed* (4:157). The boast said we killed the messenger; the witness will say they did not, but doubted, following assumption. The sūrah that bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166) makes the raised messenger’s future belief and witness part of that knowledge, so that the *“bring down a book from heaven”* demand (4:153) is answered not with a book from heaven but with a witness from heaven raised and returned. The next verses will turn from history to law: forbidden foods to Jews for wrongdoing and hindering, taking interest despite prohibition, consuming wealth unjustly — painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but those well-grounded in knowledge who believe in what was revealed to you and before — to them great reward (4:160–162).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:160

> We forbade the Jews certain foods that had been lawful to them for their wrongdoing, and for hindering many from the Way of Allah,

**Expanded Commentary**

**We Forbade the Jews Certain Foods For Their Wrongdoing**

The verse states *fa bi ẓulmin mina alladhīna hādū ḥarramnā ʿalayhim ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — so for wrongdoing, injustice, from those who became Jews, became *hādū*, We forbade them good things, pure foods, that had been lawful for them. *Bi ẓulmin mina alladhīna hādū* — for wrong, injustice, from those who are Jews — was explained as the same *ẓulm* that struck them with thunderbolt for demand greater than a book (4:153) — *because of their wrongdoing* the Mount was raised (4:154), covenant broken, signs rejected, prophets killed without right, hearts claimed *ghulf* sealed (4:155), Mary slandered with mighty *buhtān* (4:156), boasted killing Messiah not killed (4:157). *Ḥarramnā ʿalayhim ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — We forbade them good things that had been permitted — was explained as foods once *ḥalāl* made *ḥarām* as discipline, as Levitical prohibitions of certain fats and meats that remain in Jewish law — the sūrah elsewhere says *“every food was lawful to Children of Israel except what Israel forbade himself before Torah”* (3:93) — here additional forbidding is for *ẓulm*. *Ṭayyibāt* — good, pure, wholesome — was read as the good that was forbidding is not evil in itself — the foods are *ṭayyib* — pure — but forbidden as recompense, as the sūrah says *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) — here reward is forbidding of *ṭayyibāt*. The sūrah has shown that *“We forbade certain foods for wrongdoing”* is counterpart to *“We forgave them after calf yet gave Moses clear proof”* (4:153): forgiveness for calf did not cancel consequence for ongoing wrong.

**And For Hindering Many From the Way of God**

The addition *wa bi ṣaddihim ʿan sabīli Allāhi kathīran* — and for their hindering, blocking, turning away many from the way, the path of God — was explained with *ṣadd* — to hinder, to bar, to turn away — the same *ṣadd* that hypocrites *turn away stubbornly* — *yaṣuddūna ṣudūdā* (4:61) — when told come to revelations and Messenger, and that the sūrah’s noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26) are blocked where hindering occurs. *ʿAn sabīli Allāhi* — from God’s way, path — was read as the believers’ path (4:115) that was not to be left, the way of Abraham pure (4:125), the straight path He guides to through mercy and grace (4:175). *Kathīran* — many, much — was explained as many hindered: they hinder others by rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming hearts are *ghulf*, demanding visible God, taking calf, and by legal forbidding that remains; the sūrah later says *“those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way have certainly gone far astray”* (4:167) — far straying is hindering’s fruit. Early reports linked hindering to rabbis who concealed description of the Prophet ﷺ in Torah to keep followers, and to usury that consumes wealth unjustly (4:161) — hindering by economic oppression as well as doctrinal concealment. The sūrah has shown that *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah…”* (4:163) — all accepted without distinction (4:152) — hindering is the opposite: to block that acceptance.

**A Verse That Follows Boast Corrected With Law For Hindering**

Placed after the history of the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven, demanded visible God, were struck, took calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant taken, then breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slandering Mary with mighty *buhtān*, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death and witness on the Day (4:153–159), this verse follows boast corrected with law for hindering: for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way, We forbade them *ṭayyibāt* that had been lawful. The sūrah has shown that association is far straying (4:116) and defying the Messenger after clarity is left to what he chose (4:115); hindering many from God’s way is that far straying made social — not only straying self but blocking others, as Satan orders cutting and altering (4:119) to alter creation he blocks God’s creation. The forbidding of *ṭayyibāt* was read as the sūrah’s measure: as the emigrant finds many havens and abundance (4:100) — *saʿah* — the hinderer finds *ṭayyibāt* removed — narrowing where he narrowed others’ way. Where *“He wills to lighten burdens because humanity is weak”* (4:28) — lightening is giving *ṭayyibāt* — hindering many removes lightness.

**Good Things Forbidden as Measure, Not as Origin**

The phrase *ṭayyibātin uḥillat lahum* — good things that had been lawful for them — was explained to show that the foods are *ṭayyib* — good, pure — not foul; forbidding is measure, not origin. The sūrah elsewhere says lawful beyond marriage limits is lawful as long as sought with wealth in lawful marriage (4:24); the *ṭayyibāt* here are lawful in principle yet forbidden as recompense for *ẓulm*. Classical notes added that this forbidding is distinct from Israel’s self-forbidding before Torah (3:93) and that the final Book makes lawful *ṭayyibāt* again except what was forbidden as discipline, showing that the Qur’an’s *ḥalāl* restores where the Tawrāh’s discipline had narrowed, as the Prophet ﷺ was sent to remove burdens — *“he releases them from heavy burdens and yokes”* (7:157). The sūrah has said *“God wishes to lighten burdens”* (4:28) — the final lightening is not for those who persist in *ẓulm* and large *ṣadd*, but for those who believe in what was revealed to you and before (4:162).

**A Short Verse That Anchors Discipline in Hindering**

Though only *“We forbade Jews certain good foods that had been lawful for wrongdoing and for hindering many from God’s way,”* the verse anchors discipline in hindering many. Immediately the next verses add two more *ẓulms* — taking interest despite prohibition and consuming people’s wealth unjustly — painful punishment prepared for disbelievers among them, but those well-grounded in knowledge who believe in what was revealed to you and before, especially those who establish prayer and pay alms — to them great reward (4:160–162). The pattern — forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and *ṣadd* succeeded — shows that economic hindering — interest, unjust consumption — is the material counterpart of doctrinal hindering — concealing description, demanding visible God. For the weak this is an opening: where the hinderer’s *ṭayyibāt* were removed, the well-grounded who believe in what was revealed to you and before are promised great reward — the *ṭayyibāt* restored in Gardens where promise is true, as the emigrant’s many havens were restored after hindering.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:161

> taking interest despite its prohibition, and consuming people’s wealth unjustly. We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Taking Interest Despite Prohibition and Consuming Wealth Unjustly**

The verse continues *wa akhdhihimu al-ribā wa qad nuhū ʿanhu wa aklihim amwāla al-nāsi bi al-bāṭil* — and their taking interest — *ribā* — though they were forbidden it, though prohibition had come, and their consuming people’s wealth wrongly, unjustly, by false means — *bi al-bāṭil*. *Akhdhihimu al-ribā* — their taking ribā — was explained as Jewry taking interest despite Torah forbidding — *“you shall not lend at interest to your brother”* — as earlier warnings against devouring wealth by false means (2:188), against consuming orphans’ wealth as fire (4:10), and against devouring wealth unjustly and killing yourselves though He is Merciful (4:29) make clear. *Wa qad nuhū ʿanhu* — though they were forbidden — was read as that *ribā* is not ignorance but disobedience after *sulṭān mubīn* — compelling proof — Moses was given (4:153) and Mount raised for firm covenant (4:154): where interest is forbidden yet taken, the Mount’s covenant is broken again. *Wa aklihim amwāla al-nāsi bi al-bāṭil* — and eating people’s wealth unjustly — was explained as consuming wealth by false claim, bribery, selling religion, concealing description of Prophet ﷺ for fee — a trade where those given a portion trade it for misguidance wishing you deviate (4:44) and hindering many from God’s way (4:160) includes economic harm. The two — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — were read as the sūrah’s pairing after forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for wrongdoing and hindering many (4:160): as those given a portion trade guidance, here they trade wealth by *ribā* and false consumption.

**We Have Prepared for Disbelievers Among Them a Painful Punishment**

The seal *wa aʿtadnā li al-kāfirīna minhum ʿadhāban alīmā* — and We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful, aching punishment — was explained with *aʿtadnā* — prepared, made ready — as the same preparation for true disbelievers who distinguish between God and messengers — humiliating punishment prepared (4:151) — and for those who consume orphans’ wealth — Fire, and for intentional killer — Hell, anger, curse (4:93). *Li al-kāfirīna minhum* — for the disbelievers among them, from among them — was explained as not all among them: as the sūrah will say *but those well-grounded in knowledge among them who believe in what was revealed to you and before* — to them great reward (4:162) — punishment is for *kāfirīn minhum* — disbelievers among them — not for every Jew, as *we forgave them after calf* (4:153) showed some forgiven. *ʿAdhāban alīmā* — painful punishment — was read as pain matching the pain of consuming fire (4:10), of humiliating punishment for ally seekers (4:102), of lowest depth without helper (4:145). Scripture has shown that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* are evil rewarded accordingly — painful. Where the Book says *“God does not wrong even an atom”* (4:40) — interest even at atom of increase is measured and not wronging to punish, because it wrongs the single soul’s trust.

**A Verse That Follows Forbidding *Ṭayyibāt* With Forbidding Wealth**

Placed after *We forbade Jews certain good foods that had been lawful for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way* (4:160), this verse follows forbidding *ṭayyibāt* — pure foods — with forbidding wealth — *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — for which painful punishment is prepared. That to God belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) shows that wealth taken by *ribā* is taken from His ownership unjustly, as female gods invoked besides Him (4:117) are taken from His worship unjustly. The law lightens because humanity is weak (4:28) yet does not license devouring wealth unjustly (4:29) — *ribā* is the lightening inverted: to make wealth increase by hardship on debtor. Earlier the Book praised charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) as the good secret talk; interest is the evil secret talk that devours. For the weak this is protective: where interest is taken from the debtor and wealth consumed unjustly from people, the sūrah that promised many havens to the emigrant (4:100) and enrichment to both after separation (4:130) declares that to take interest though forbidden will be painful punishment for disbelievers among them, while help is with the well-grounded who give alms (4:162).

**Taking Despite Prohibition as Breaking After Knowledge**

The phrase *wa qad nuhū ʿanhu* — though they were forbidden — was explained as breaking after knowledge, after *sulṭān mubīn* Moses was given (4:153), after Mount raised (4:154), after firm covenant taken (4:154) where Sabbath not to transgress was commanded — prohibition of *ribā* is of that rank. To take despite prohibition was read as the litany’s continuation: demand greater than a book, thunderbolt, calf after clear signs yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, then breaking, rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slandering Mary with *buhtān ʿaẓīm*, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear — now forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and *ṣadd* — now *ribā* despite prohibition and *akl bi al-bāṭil*. The pattern is breaking after knowledge, as *those who believed then disbelieved then increased* (4:137) — increase after being shown. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) here unmasks *ribā* as the secret talk’s economy.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Wealth in Disbelief Among Them**

Though only *“taking interest despite prohibition and consuming wealth unjustly, We have prepared for disbelievers among them painful punishment,”* the verse anchors wealth in disbelief among them, not in all. The exception — *illā* — appears next: *but those well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful who believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before — especially those who establish prayer — and those who pay alms and believe in God and Last Day, to them We will grant great reward* (4:162). Elsewhere the promise says *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) and *with Him are both rewards* (4:134) He hears and sees; to give alms — *zakat* — is the opposite of taking *ribā* and consuming unjustly. The next verse will name those exceptions as proof that the *ḥarramnā ṭayyibāt* — forbidding good foods — is not permanence: to them great reward includes *ṭayyibāt* restored.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:162

> But those of them well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful ˹who˺ believe in what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what was revealed before you—˹especially˺ those who establish prayer— and those who pay alms-tax and believe in Allah and the Last Day, to these ˹people˺ We will grant a great reward.

**Expanded Commentary**

**But Those Well-Grounded in Knowledge Among Them**

The verse states *lākini al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilmi minhum* — but those firmly grounded, deeply rooted, in knowledge, among them — among the People of the Book — whose litany was demand, thunderbolt, calf, breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, slander, boasting murder, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm*, taking *ribā* though prohibited, consuming wealth unjustly — among them the *rāsikhūn*. *Rāsikhūn fī al-ʿilm* — firmly grounded in knowledge — was explained as those rooted deep so that wind does not move them, as the sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers desire a way between (4:150) are not grounded, but these are, as Abraham was *ḥanīf* following the upright (4:125) and as the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105). *Minhum* — among them — was read as not all among them: as the painful punishment was prepared for *kāfirīn minhum* — disbelievers among them (4:161) — great reward is for *rāsikhūn minhum* — grounded among them — keeping the sūrah’s balance: few believe except few (4:155) — here the few are named.

**The Faithful Who Believe in What Was Revealed to You and Before You**

The description *wa al-muʾminūna yuʾminūna bi mā unzila ilayka wa mā unzila min qablika* — and the faithful — believers — who believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, before thee — was explained as comprehensive faith that does not distinguish between any messenger (4:152) and accepts revelation lineage — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him”* (4:163) — Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David given Psalms. To believe in *mā unzila ilayka* — what was revealed to you — and *mā unzila min qablika* — what was revealed before you — was read as that the sūrah commanded *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures He revealed before* (4:136) — steadfast, not selective; the *rāsikhūn* are those who kept that. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever believes in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards”* (4:152) — these are they.

**Especially Those Who Establish Prayer and Pay Alms**

The detail *wa al-muqīmīna al-ṣalāta wa al-muʾtūna al-zakāta* — and especially those who establish, stand firm for, prayer — *muqīmīn* — and those who give, pay, alms — *zakāh* — was explained with two pillars: *iqāmat al-ṣalāh* — establishing prayer — the same *kitāban mawqūtā* — writ at fixed time (4:103) — shortened on travel (4:101), guarded under arms (4:102), remembered standing, sitting, lying (4:103), lazy to be seen by hypocrites (4:142) — the *rāsikhūn* establish it. *Wa al-muʾtūna al-zakāta* — and those who pay alms — was read as the opposite of *akhdh al-ribā* — taking interest though forbidden — and *akl bi al-bāṭil* — consuming wealth unjustly (4:161): to give *zakāh* is to release wealth, to take *ribā* is to increase it wrongly. Early reports noted the grammar — *al-muqīmīna* in accusative as praise, as Arabs single out the praised with accusative — showing special praise for those who establish prayer among the grounded. The sūrah has said *“charge your wealth by mutual consent, do not kill yourselves, He is ever Merciful”* (4:29) — *zakāh* is mutual consent’s alms. The pair was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122): establishing prayer and giving alms are the *ṣāliḥāt* — righteous deeds.

**And Those Who Believe in God and the Last Day — To Them Great Reward**

The seal *wa al-muʾminīna bi Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri ulāʾika sa nuʾtīhim ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and those who believe in God and the Last Day — to these We will surely, will soon, grant a great, mighty reward — was explained with *yuʾminūna bi Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri* as the two articles that anchor all — God and Last Day — without which Articles — denying God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day leads far astray (4:136) — belief incomplete; the *rāsikhūn* affirm them. *Ulāʾika sa nuʾtīhim ajran ʿaẓīmā* — to these We will grant great reward — was explained as the same *ajr ʿaẓīm* promised to those who command charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure (4:114) and to the repentant sincere with believers (4:146) and to comprehensive believers (4:152) — the *rāsikhūn* who establish prayer and give alms are inclusive. The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — great reward is both — world as *murāgham* and *saʿah* and Hereafter as Gardens true. *Sa nuʾtīhim* — We will grant — was read as divine assurance that reward secured upon God as emigrant’s reward secured (4:100) — the same certainty.

**A Verse That Follows Disbelief Among Them With Faith Among Them**

Placed after *We forbade Jews certain good foods for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way* (4:160), *taking interest though forbidden and consuming wealth unjustly, We have prepared for the disbelievers among them painful punishment* (4:161), this verse follows disbelief among them with faith among them: but the firmly grounded in knowledge among them, the faithful who believe in what was revealed to you and before you, especially those who establish prayer and pay alms and believe in God and Last Day — to them great reward. The sūrah has shown that even after litany — demand greater than a book, thunderbolt, calf after clear signs yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf*, denial, slander against Mary with *buhtān ʿaẓīm*, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear — there remain *rāsikhūn* — firmly grounded — who do not distinguish (4:152) and who will receive great reward. The verse was read as the sūrah’s middle after ownership to Him of heavens and earth and encompassing (4:126) — the grounded are those who accept that ownership and witness with His knowledge (4:166). For the weak this is opening: where interest was taken from the debtor and wealth consumed unjustly, the grounded who give alms are the ones who enrich without stripping, as the separator enriched from His bounty (4:130) — the great reward includes *ṭayyibāt* restored.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:163

> Indeed, We have sent revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ as We sent revelation to Noah and the prophets after him. We also sent revelation to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants, ˹as well as˺ Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon. And to David We gave the Psalms.

**Expanded Commentary**

**We Have Sent Revelation to You as We Sent to Noah and Those After Him**

The verse opens *innā awḥaynā ilayka kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin wa al-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — indeed We have inspired, revealed, to you as We inspired to Noah and the prophets after him. *Awḥaynā* — to inspire, to reveal, to convey — was explained as divine communication to heart, as the Book was sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as *“O Prophet, have faith in God, Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before”* (4:136) — revelation is one chain. *Kamā awḥaynā ilā Nūḥin* — as We revealed to Noah — was read as that Nūḥ is first of the chain of law-giving messengers after Adam, as the sūrah earlier says *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* (4:126) — Noah’s ark upon water that belongs to Him is the first rescue of the single soul spread (4:1). *Wa al-nabiyyīna min baʿdih* — and prophets after him — was explained as that the revelation to you is not isolate but continuation, as Abraham pure — *ḥanīf* — was taken as friend (4:125) and his way is best faith. The verse generalises the sūrah’s lineage: from Noah through Abraham to you is one *waḥy* — revelation — whose truth was made clear where Mount was raised (4:154) and whose distinction not made is true belief (4:152).

**Also to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon — And Psalms to David**

The enumeration *wa awḥaynā ilā Ibrāhīma wa Ismāʿīla wa Isḥāqa wa Yaʿqūba wa al-asbāṭi wa ʿĪsā wa Ayyūba wa Yūnusa wa Hārūna wa Sulaymāna wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes — the *asbāṭ* — descendants — and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon; and to David We gave the Psalms — *Zabūr* — was explained as proof of universality. *Ibrāhīma … al-asbāṭ* — Abraham’s line — Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, tribes — was read as the *millata Ibrāhīma* — Way of Abraham upright (4:125) — made concrete: revelation to each branch, not only to the asking People of the Book who demanded a book from heaven (4:153) — the book has already come to many. *ʿĪsā* — Jesus — was read as the Messiah raised to Him (4:158), son of Mary slandered then son slain falsely — now placed among prophets revealed to, not god. *Ayyūba, Yūnusa* — Job, Jonah — were read as the tested: Job with patience, Jonah with repentance after abandonment — both *“We sent revelation”* to them as to you, showing that revelation includes trials. *Hārūna, Sulaymāna* — Aaron, Solomon — were read as brother-helper and king-prophet; Aaron with Moses where the Mount was raised, Solomon with kingdom where *“give them speck on date stone”* (4:53) — even kingdom with prophethood. *Wa ātaynā Dāwūda zabūrā* — and to David We gave Psalms — was explained as book singled: Psalms as *zabūr* — written, inscribed — among books before (4:136), showing that books before are many, not one book from heaven demanded. Where the sūrah says *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah”* — *kamā* — likeness is in source — all from Owner of heavens and earth (4:126) — and in purpose — to judge with truth.

**A Verse That Follows Demand for a Book From Heaven With Revelation Lineage**

Placed after the history — demand for a book from heaven, greater demand visible God, thunderbolt, calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but grounded in knowledge among them believe in what was revealed to you and before, especially establishing prayer and alms, to them great reward (4:153–162), this verse follows demand with lineage: *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him*. Demand for a book from heaven (4:153) is answered with revelation has already been sent to many, including Psalms to David. The sūrah has shown that those who distinguish between God and messengers desire a way between (4:150) — to distinguish is to claim revelation lineage broken; this verse says lineage is one. The sūrah that warns not to go to extremes regarding faith (4:171) — do not say Trinity, Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him — here places Jesus among prophets revealed to, not as god, so that extremity is not needed to honour him.

**Revelation to Many Makes Faith Without Distinction Possible**

The phrase *kamā awḥaynā* — as We revealed — was explained to make *“accepting all, rejecting none”* (4:152) possible: because revelation is one source — *to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth* (4:126) — to accept all is to accept that Owner’s many givings. Where the hypocrites are *mudhabdhab* between neither (4:143) and desire a way between distinguishing (4:150) — wavering — the lineage from Noah to David to you is the firm path — *sabili al-muʾminīn* (4:115) — not wavering. For the weak this is an opening: where you feared settlement is best (4:128) and settlement involves waiver, revelation lineage shows no waiver of any prophet; faith is not settlement that waives some messengers, but *ḥanīf* submission that accepts all. The next verses will extend that lineage: there are messengers whose stories We told you already and others We did not, and to Moses He spoke directly (4:164).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:164

> There are messengers whose stories We have told you already and others We have not. And to Moses Allah spoke directly.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Messengers Whose Stories We Told You and Others We Did Not**

The verse states *wa rusulan qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayka* — and messengers, apostles, whose stories We have already narrated, cut, to you before, and messengers We did not narrate to you. *Rusulan* — messengers — was explained as the continuation of *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him… Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, Solomon, David We gave Psalms”* (4:163) — now as *recounted and not recounted*. *Qad qaṣaṣnāhum ʿalayka min qablu* — whose stories We have told you before — was read as those named in Qur’an — the chain from Adam to Jesus — told as proof that God bears witness with His knowledge (4:166). *Wa rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayka* — and messengers We did not narrate — was explained as that knowledge is with Him who is Fully Aware encompassing everything (4:126) — He sent many more than told, because to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) — among all peoples He sent. The sūrah has shown that those well-grounded in knowledge believe in what was revealed to you and before (4:162) — even those messengers not recounted are among *mā unzila min qablika* — what was revealed before you (4:162) — and to believe accepting all, rejecting none (4:152) includes those not narrated, for their existence is asserted here. To know that some were not told was explained as humility: the Book does not claim to list all His sent, because to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) — among all, He sent, and He knows. The command to be mindful (4:131) therefore rests not on counting messengers but on trusting the Sender who sent many whose names only He encompasses as *Muḥīṭ* (4:126).

**And to Moses God Spoke Directly**

The addition *wa kallama Allāhu Mūsā taklīman* — and God spoke to Moses — *kallama* — speaking — *taklīman* — directly, with speech — was explained with *taklīm* — speaking mouth to ear without intermediary, the honour that Moses is *Kalīmullāh* — Speaker with God. *Taklīman* — emphatic verbal noun — was read as absolute direct speech, not inspiration as to Noah (4:163) — *awḥaynā* — but *kallama*. Early reports linked this to Sinai where Mount was raised over them for covenant (4:154) and where thunderbolt struck them for demand greater than a book — *show God visible* (4:153) — yet to Moses He spoke directly without seeing. The sūrah has shown that *“there is no knowledge except following assumption”* where boasters claim killing Messiah (4:157) — true knowledge is where He speaks, as He spoke to Moses. The verse was also linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — Moses’ direct speech is the witness that revelation is real, against the People of the Book demand *bring down a book from heaven* (4:153) — revelation already spoken.

**A Verse That Follows Revelation Lineage With Limit of Narration**

Placed after *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah and prophets after him… Psalms to David* (4:163), this verse follows lineage with limit of narration: some narrated, some not narrated, and Moses spoken to directly. The sūrah has shown that *“We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful”* (4:131) — revelation before you is many; to not narrate some is not to deny them, as the sūrah says *with Him are both rewards He hears and sees* (4:134) — He knows those sent. The sūrah that warns not to make distinction between messengers (4:150–152) says even those not narrated are included in not distinguishing: to accept all messengers includes the unnamed. The sūrah that warns not to take disbelievers as allies instead of believers (4:144) and describes lowest depth without helper (4:145) makes direct speech to Moses the helper for the weak: where you were told to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), here is the Speaker who can be referred to.

**Direct Speech as Proof After Demand for Visible**

The phrase *kallama Allāhu Mūsā taklīman* was linked to the initial demand — *bring down a book from heaven* (4:153) and *show God visible* — demand for visible proof: Moses heard Him directly, yet his people still demanded visible, took calf after clear signs, broke covenant, so the Mount was raised (4:154). Direct speech thus did not suffice for those who demanded visible; to demand visible after speech is the *ẓulm* for which *ṭayyibāt* were forbidden (4:160). For the Community, direct speech is the proof that the Book was sent with truth — *to judge between people by what He shows* (4:105) — He shows by speaking directly and clearly.

**The Unrecounted Messengers and Comprehensive Faith**

The mention *rusulan lam naqṣuṣhum ʿalayka* — messengers We did not narrate — was explained to include future and distant peoples: revelation not told with story is still revelation believed in, as *“do not let desires deviate from justice”* (4:135) and *“have faith in God, Messenger, Books, angels, Last Day”* (4:136) make faith a guard. The sūrah has shown that even religious error before prayer is covered by pardon (4:43) where seeking is sincere; to not know a messenger’s name does not remove the command to accept all. The next verse will note the purpose of all messengers narrated and not — delivering good news and warnings so excuse is cut — and He remains Almighty, All-Wise (4:165). Elsewhere the Book ties that purpose to mercy, for He wishes to turn toward you in mercy (4:27).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:165

> ˹All were˺ messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity should have no excuse before Allah after ˹the coming of˺ the messengers. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Messengers Delivering Good News and Warnings**

The verse states *rusulan mubashshirīna wa mundhirīna* — messengers, apostles, as bearers of good news and warners, givers of glad tidings and warnings. *Mubashshirīn* — bearing good news — and *mundhirīn* — warning — were explained as the two faces of revelation already named: Gardens forever for those who believe and do good where promise is true (4:122) — good news — and Hell without escape for followers of Satan’s delusion (4:121), painful punishment for hypocrites (4:138), humiliating punishment for true disbelievers (4:151), painful punishment for disbelievers among the Book’s People for *ẓulm* and *ribā* (4:161) — warnings. *Rusulan* — messengers — includes those whose stories We told you before and those We did not narrate, and to Moses He spoke directly (4:164), and those given Psalms to David (4:163), and the chain from Noah through Abraham to Jesus (4:163) — all were *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn*. The sūrah has shown that those who believe accepting all, rejecting none, will be given rewards (4:152), and that those well-grounded believe in what was revealed to you and before (4:162) — good news is for them. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector”* (4:123) — warning is for him.

**So Humanity Should Have No Excuse Before God After Messengers**

The purpose *li allā yakūna li al-nāsi ʿalā Allāhi ḥujjatun baʿda al-rusuli* — so that there be not for humanity against God an argument, excuse, plea, after the messengers — was explained with *ḥujjah* — argument, proof, excuse — the same *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant — given against hostile turners (4:91) and that you give against yourselves if you take disbelievers as allies (4:144) and compelling proof Moses was given (4:153) — here humanity’s *ḥujjah* against Him is removed. *Baʿda al-rusuli* — after the messengers — was read as after the lineage from Noah to you — *“We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah”* (4:163) — there is no *“we did not know”* left, because He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) yet He sent messengers first. Early reports linked this to the sūrah’s *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26) — clarity is via messengers, so excuse is cut. The phrase was linked to *“on Resurrection Day the Messiah will be witness against them”* (4:159) — witnesses are *rusul* against their peoples, as *“We will bring witness from every community and you as witness against yours”* (4:41) — the witness is the *ḥujjah*. Where the hypocrites sought to deceive God while He outwits them (4:142) and argued *we believe in some and disbelieve in some desiring a way between* (4:150) — they claimed a *ḥujjah* of compromise; the verse says none remains.

**And God Is Almighty, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAzīzan Ḥakīmā* — And God is Almighty, All-Powerful, All-Wise, was ever — was explained with *ʿAzīz* — Almighty, Mighty — the One who raises Jesus to Himself (4:158) and can remove humanity (4:133) yet sends warners before removing — and *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — who sends good news and warnings in wisdom, not need. *ʿAzīz Ḥakīm* seals the sending as not weak: the messengers’ *basharah* — good news — and *indhār* — warning — are backed by Almighty who can do as He warns, and Wise who warns where wise to warn, as He is *Qadīr* to pardon though capable (4:149) and *Ghafūr Raḥīm* to reward — good news is mercy from Wise, warning is justice from Mighty. The sūrah has shown that *“He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy”* though you disobey (4:131) — He needs no *ḥujjah* from you, He removes your *ḥujjah*.

**A Verse That Follows Lineage With Purpose**

Placed after *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), *messengers whose stories We told you and others We did not, and to Moses He spoke directly* (4:164), this verse follows lineage with purpose: all were messengers delivering good news and warnings so that humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise. The sūrah has traced the demand for a book from heaven and demand greater — visible God — thunderbolt, calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but grounded among them to great reward — now the *why* of all that sending: so no excuse. The sūrah that asks *“was not God’s earth spacious enough to emigrate?”* (4:97) and promises many havens (4:100) says messengers are the spaciousness of excuse removed, as earth is the spaciousness of refuge opened. For the weak this is clarifying: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), good news is that settlement pleasing to Him is great reward (4:114), warning is that inclining entirely leaving hanging is Hamm; both were told before excuse remains.

**The Excuse Removed Is the Alliance Sought**

The *ḥujjah* removed — *no excuse before God after messengers* — was linked to *“would you give God clear warrant against yourselves?”* (4:144) — *sulṭān mubīn* — by taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers seeking honour (4:139) — that warrant is the excuse that remains for the hypocrite. Messengers sent as *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn* remove that warrant’s claim to ignorance: the honour sought among disbelievers was warned against by the very messengers whose revelation lineage includes Moses directly spoken to. The next verse will set the witness that makes that *ḥujjah* stand: yet if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent down to you — He sent it with His knowledge — angels too bear witness — and God alone suffices as Witness (4:166).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:166

> Yet ˹if you are denied, O Prophet,˺ Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you—He has sent it with His knowledge. The angels too bear witness. And Allah ˹alone˺ is sufficient as a Witness.

**Expanded Commentary**

**If You Are Denied, God Bears Witness to What He Sent Down**

The verse opens *lākini Allāhu yashhadu bi mā anzala ilayka* — yet, but, rather, God bears witness, testifies, to what He has sent down, revealed, to you. *Lākini* — yet, but — was explained as reply to *“humanity should have no excuse after messengers”* (4:165) where Almighty, All-Wise sends good news and warnings; if after that they deny you — *yet if you are denied, O Prophet* — God bears witness. *Yashhadu bi mā anzala ilayka* — bears witness to what He sent down to you — was explained as that the sūrah’s lineage — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), messengers told and not told, Moses spoken to directly (4:164) — all sent as *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn* so no excuse (4:165) — is witnessed by Him who sent: *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126). *Anzala ilayka* — sent down to you — was read as the Qur’an sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as the instruction regarding orphan women already recited (4:127) — all are *mā anzala ilayka*. The sūrah has warned *whoever disobeys, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131) — to deny the One who bears witness is to deny the Owner to whom all belongs.

**He Sent It With His Knowledge — Angels Too Bear Witness**

The detail *anzalahu bi ʿilmihī* — He sent it down with His knowledge, by His knowledge, through His knowledge — was explained with *bi ʿilmihī* — with His knowledge — as that the Book’s content — limits, trusts, prayer at fixed time, settlement best, comprehensive faith accepting all messengers — is known by Him who knows what is in hearts (4:63) and is Fully Aware of what they do (4:108) and is All-Hearing, All-Seeing (4:134) — revelation is not arbitrary. *Wa al-malāʾikatu yashhadūn* — and the angels too bear witness, testify — was explained as the second witness: angels nearest to Him who would never be too proud to be servants (4:172), who guard, who raise Mount, who take souls asking *what were you doing?* (4:97), who stood witness at *“create you from single soul”* (4:1) — they witness to what He sent. Early reports linked this to Jews who denied the Prophet’s prophethood after demanding a book from heaven (4:153); the verse says angels witness to the Book sent to you as they witnessed the Mount raised (4:154). The sūrah has shown that those whose stories We told and did not tell are many — *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* — angels witness to the told and not told.

**And God Alone Is Sufficient as Witness**

The seal *wa kafā bi Allāhi shahīdā* — and God alone is sufficient, enough, as Witness — was explained with *shahīd* — witness — the same *shahīd* as the Bringing of witness from every community (4:41) and Jesus as witness against them (4:159) — here the Supreme Witness suffices. *Kafā bi Allāhi shahīdā* was read as that where People of the Book demand a book from heaven as sign and hypocrites desire a way between distinguishing (4:150) and where night plotters hide from people but He is with them (4:108) — His witness suffices. The phrase was also the sūrah’s answer to *“with Him are both rewards, He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing”* (4:134): He who hears and sees suffices as Witness because witnessing is hearing and seeing. Where the sūrah says *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132) and *“sufficient as Guardian and Helper”* (4:45) — to be sufficient as Witness is to be the Trust upon whom judgment by Book (4:105) rests.

**A Verse That Follows No Excuse With Sufficient Witness**

Placed after *messengers as good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:165), this verse follows no excuse with sufficient witness: yet if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent to you — He sent it with His knowledge — angels too bear witness — He alone suffices as Witness. The sūrah has traced *sulṭān mubīn* — clear warrant — Moses was given (4:153), given over hostile turners (4:91), that you give against yourselves if you take allies instead of believers (4:144); witness is the *sulṭān* that makes warrant true. The sūrah that asks *“who is more truthful than God in speech?”* (4:122) — none — says His *shahādah* — witness — is most truthful. For the weak this is an opening: where you were told to verify reports through Messenger and authority (4:83) and to be sure before fighting (4:94) and to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135), the witness that your verification stands is His witness and angels’ — sufficient, so that you need not be hanging between neither these nor those (4:143) waiting to see.

**The Knowledge With Which He Sent Explains the Law’s Detail**

The phrase *bi ʿilmihī* — with His knowledge — was explained to keep law’s detail intelligible: inheritance shares — * obligatory shares* (4:11–12), dowry graciously waived (4:4), *muḥsanāt* — chaste — marrying with permission and dowry where *shuḥḥ* is present (4:25), settlement best though selfishness present (4:128), not inclining entirely (4:129), enrichment from His bounty (4:130) — all are *bi ʿilmihī*, not guess. Where the sūrah says *“He wishes to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise”* (4:26–28) — *ʿilmihī* is that clarity. The next verse will set the opposite witnesses: *those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way have certainly gone far astray* (4:167) — those who deny the Sufficient Witness and hinder many, their straying is far because witness was sufficient and with knowledge.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:167

> Those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah have certainly strayed far away.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Disbelieve and Hinder From God’s Way — Far Astray**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdā* — surely those who disbelieve and hinder, bar, turn others from God’s way, path, have certainly gone far, strayed far away. *Kafarū* — to disbelieve, to cover — was explained as denial after messengers as good news and warnings removed excuse (4:165) and after sufficient witness bears witness with His knowledge and angels (4:166). *Wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīli Allāhi* — and hinder from God’s way — was explained with *ṣadd* — to block, to hinder, to turn away — the same hindering as *We forbade Jews certain good foods for wrongdoing and hindering many from God’s way* (4:160) — there *bi ṣaddihim ʿan sabīli Allāhi kathīran* — hindering many — here *ṣaddū* — hindering — as act of those who disbelieve. *Sabīli Allāhi* — God’s way, path — was read as the noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), the believers’ path not to be left (4:115), the straight path He guides to through mercy (4:175), the Book sent with truth to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — all are God’s way. *Qad ḍallū ḍalālan baʿīdā* — have certainly gone far astray, strayed far away — was explained as *ḍalāl baʿīd* — far straying — the same seal as *whoever associates has gone far astray* (4:116) and *whoever denies God, angels, Books, messengers, Last Day has gone far astray* (4:136) — to disbelieve and hinder is that far. Early reports linked *ṣaddū* to Jews who concealed description of the Prophet ﷺ and to hypocrites who take disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) and to those who deny revelation being ridiculed yet sit with mockers (4:140) — hindering is both doctrinal concealment and social sitting.

**A Verse That Follows No Excuse and Sufficient Witness With Far Straying**

Placed after *messengers as good news and warnings so humanity have no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise* (4:165), *yet if you are denied, God bears witness to what He sent with His knowledge, angels too bear witness, He alone suffices as Witness* (4:166), this verse follows no excuse and sufficient witness with far straying for those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way. The sequence — lineage from Noah through Jesus to you (4:163), messengers told and not told, Moses spoken to directly (4:164), purpose so no excuse (4:165), sufficient witness (4:166) — now the verdict for deniers and hinderers: they have gone far. Scripture notes that *“neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book”* (4:123) — grace not by wish — and *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — to hinder from His way is to hinder from both rewards where both are with Him whose ownership is heavens and earth (4:126). Elsewhere the principle that *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself”* (4:111) is qualified here: hindering adds others’ misguidance to earnings — therefore *baʿīd* — far.

**Disbelief Alone and Disbelief Plus Hindering**

The pairing — *kafarū* — disbelieved — and *ṣaddū* — hindered — was explained to show two degrees: disbelief alone is straying, disbelief plus hindering is far straying. The principle that *“whoever does evil will be rewarded accordingly”* (4:123) shows that disbelief alone will be *yujza bihī* — rewarded accordingly; hindering adds to it, as throwing sin on innocent adds slander to original sin (4:112). Forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* plus *ṣadd kathīr* — hindering many — (4:160) shows that *ṭayyibāt* removal corresponds to double cause; here *ḍalālan baʿīdā* is for *kufr* plus *ṣadd*. Where the Book says *“do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended”* (4:129) — hindering the suspended from right is the household *ṣadd* — and *“settlement best”* (4:128) — settlement is opposite of hindering. For the weak this is protective: where you are hindered — the helpless who cannot find way (4:98) — the hinderer’s far straying is declared, not yours.

**The Hinderer’s Far Straying as Warning for the Community**

The *ṣaddū* — they hinder — was described as not only blocking others by force but by example: to disbelieve and claim hearts are *ghulf*, to slander Mary, to boast killing Messiah, to take *ribā* though forbidden, all hinder many who observe. The sūrah has taught that those who give charity, kindness, reconciliation seeking His pleasure earn great reward (4:114), the opposite of hindering; the hinderer’s work undoes that good by making God’s way seem blocked. Early commentators noted that *ṣadd* after sufficient witness (4:166) is worse than *ṣadd* before, because the witness — God with knowledge and angels — has already borne testimony that the way is true. That is why the seal is *baʿīd* — far — the distance from truth after truth was made near by messengers as good news and warnings.

**Far Astray After Knowledge Made Clear**

The *baʿīd* — far — was explained as after knowledge made clear where *He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:26–28) — clarity was via messengers, so straying is far because clarity was great. That *“the Messiah will never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest”* (4:172) shows that hindering from God’s way includes calling to worship females besides Him (4:117) and to take Satan as guardian instead of Him (4:119) — far from servanthood. The verse generalises the sūrah’s warning *do not go to extremes regarding faith* (4:171) — Trinity as hindering from His way — far straying is the extreme’s end. The next verse will seal that far straying: those who disbelieve and wrong themselves — surely He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path (4:168) — except that of Hell to stay forever, and that is easy for Him (4:169).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:168

> Those who disbelieve and wrong themselves—surely Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Disbelieve and Wrong Themselves — Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

The verse states *inna alladhīna kafarū wa ẓalamū lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — surely those who disbelieve and wrong, do injustice, will not be — He will not — forgive them nor guide them to any path, way. *Kafarū* — disbelieved — and *ẓalamū* — wronged — was explained with *ẓulm* — wrongdoing, injustice — as addition to *kufr*: disbelief plus hindering from God’s way (4:167) is wronging selves and others, as *“whoever commits evil or wrongs themselves”* (4:110) and *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself”* (4:111) — wronging here is *ẓulm* that exceeds self. *Lam yakuni Allāhu li yaghfira lahum* — He will not forgive them — was explained with *li yaghfira* — to forgive — withheld where *shukr* and *īmān* would remove need for punishment (4:147) — here disbelief and wrong persist. *Wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — nor guide them to any path, way, road — was read as no guidance to *ṭarīq* — way — the same *sabīl* believers follow (4:115) and God guides to noble ways (4:26); to be not guided to any *ṭarīq* is to be left where *“whoever He leaves to stray you will never find a way”* (4:88, 4:143) — no way. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever believed then disbelieved then believed then increased”* (4:137) — He will neither forgive nor guide them to the Right Way — there increased disbelief after oscillation removed forgiveness and guidance; here disbelief plus wrong does. Early reports linked *ẓalamū* to those who disbelieve and also wrong the Prophet by concealing his description, taking interest though forbidden (4:161), consuming wealth unjustly, claiming *we killed Messiah* (4:157) — wrongs upon denial, each increasing the unforgiven burden.

**A Verse That Follows Far Astray With Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

Placed after *those who disbelieve and hinder from God’s way have certainly gone far astray* (4:167), this verse follows far astray with neither forgiven nor guided to any path — except Hell’s path. Scripture notes that association is not forgiven though what is less is for whom He wills (4:116); those who disbelieve and wrong combine association and *ṣadd* and *ẓulm*, so the unforgiven is not less. The principle that *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) shows that forgiveness not given here is because gratitude and faith are absent, while disbelief and wrong persist. The reminder that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) indicates that guidance to *ṭarīq* is with Him whose ownership is heavens and earth (4:126) and who suffices as Trustee (4:132); to be not guided to any *ṭarīq* is to be outside that trust. Where the Book warns *“do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers lest you give clear warrant against yourselves”* (4:144) — *sulṭān mubīn* — wronging plus disbelief gives Him warrant to not forgive nor guide.

**Not Forgiven Nor Guided to Any Path — The Two Denied**
