The two denials — *lam yakun li yaghfira* and *lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — were explained as the Book’s two gifts denied: forgiveness that effaces — *ʿAfuww* — and guidance that shows way — *Hidāyah*. The promise that whoever wrongs themselves then seeks finds Him All-Forgiving (4:110) shows that forgiveness denied here is where seeking is absent; and that *“had it not been for grace they would have deceived you yet they deceive only themselves”* (4:113) shows guidance denied where deception persists. That *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) links forgiveness to Gardens and guidance to the straight path He guides to through mercy and grace (4:175); to deny both is to close both abodes. For the weak this is clarifying: where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were not among those who disbelieve and wrong but among those who cannot find way (*ḥīlah, sabīl*), forgiveness and guidance are hoped; here case is opposite — able, disbelieving, wronging, hindering.

**The *Ṭarīq* Not Given Is Any Path Toward Mercy**

The phrase *wa lā li yahdiyuhum ṭarīqā* — nor guide them to any path — with indefinite *ṭarīqā* — any way — was explained as no path toward mercy remaining, because *ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* — straight path — He guides to through mercy (4:175) is the only *ṭarīq* to Gardens; to be not guided to any *ṭarīq* is to be not guided to that. The declaration that *“He can remove you O humanity and bring others”* (4:133) frames removal as where no *ṭarīq* remains; and *“whoever defies the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows other than believers’ path is left to what he chose then burned”* (4:115) shows that leaving to chosen path is not guiding to true path. The next verse will set the only remaining way — Hell’s path forever, which is easy for Him.

**A Short Verse That Holds the Gate Open One Sentence**

Though only *“those who disbelieve and wrong — He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path,”* the verse holds the gate open one sentence: except Hell’s way — as the sūrah’s pattern holds — lowest depth without helper except those who repent (4:145–146) — the gate is repentance not asserted here because disbelief and wrong persist. The warning *do not go to extremes regarding faith* (4:171) — extremes of Trinity and of killing Messiah boasted are among those who disbelieve and wrong; to persist is to be not forgiven nor guided, as Hell’s path remains the only one left. That path’s ease for Him underscores that mercy elsewhere remains wide for the grateful and faithful (4:147).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:169

> except that of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever. And that is easy for Allah.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Except That of Hell — To Stay There Forever**

The verse completes *illā ṭarīqa Jahannam khālidīna fīhā abadan* — except the way, the path of Hell, staying, abiding, in it forever and ever. *Illā ṭarīqa Jahannam* — except the path of Hell — was explained as the only *ṭarīq* — way — to which those who disbelieve and wrong — not forgiven, not guided to any path (4:168) — will be guided: Hell’s way. *Ṭarīq* — path, way — was read as *sabīl* — the sūrah’s path language — noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), believers’ path not to be left (4:115), associations far straying (4:116), disbelief plus hindering far astray (4:167) — now the *ṭarīq* guided to is Hell’s, as *“whoever defies the Messenger and follows other than believers’ path We will let pursue what he chose then burn, evil destination”* (4:115) — burning is that path. *Khālidīna fīhā abadan* — staying therein forever and ever — was explained with double emphasis — *khālidīn* and *abadan* — the same double for Gardens for those who believe and do good (4:122) — now for Hell’s path where *“they will have Hell as home and find no escape”* (4:121) — no *maḥīṣ*. The sūrah has shown that *“they are true disbelievers, humiliating punishment prepared for disbelievers”* (4:151) — humiliating is Hell’s path; and *“lowest depth of Fire, you will never find helper”* (4:145) — lowest depth is that path’s place. *Abadan* — forever ever — was linked to the sūrah’s promise where Gardens forever (4:122) is for belief and good, here forever for disbelief and wrong — the only *ṭarīq* left is lasting.

**And That Is Easy for God**

The seal *wa kāna dhālika ʿalā Allāhi yasīrā* — and that — guiding to Hell’s path and abiding forever — is easy, light, facile for God, upon Him easy — was explained with *yasīr* — easy, light, not burdensome — the same *yasīr* as *“whoever does this unjustly We will burn in Fire, and that is easy for God”* (4:30) where devouring wealth unjustly and killing yourselves though Merciful was threatened with Fire easy for Him. *ʿAlā Allāhi yasīrā* — easy for God, upon Him easy — was read as that His power to do is not constrained, as He can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) — He is Most Capable to do so — here He can guide to Hell’s path — easy. The sūrah has shown that He is *ʿAzīz Ḥakīm* — Almighty, All-Wise — who raises Jesus (4:158) and sends messengers so no excuse remains (4:165) and bears witness with His knowledge (4:166) — His *ʿizzah* makes Hell’s path easy where He is denied. The phrase was linked to *“Gardens forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — both Gardens and Hell forever are with Him whose awareness encompasses everything (4:126) — both are easy as promise true and threat true.

**A Verse That Completes Neither Forgiven Nor Guided**

Placed after *those who disbelieve and wrong — He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path* (4:168), this verse completes neither forgiven nor guided with except Hell’s path forever, and that is easy for Him. The litany from demand for a book from heaven (4:153) through thunderbolt, calf, pardon, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but grounded among them to great reward, then lineage, messengers told and not, directly spoken, good news and warnings so no excuse, sufficient witness, those who disbelieve and hinder far astray, disbelieve and wrong not forgiven nor guided — now except Hell’s path forever easy — shows that excuse removed and witness sufficient leaves Hell’s path as the only remaining for persisters. For the weak this is an anchor: where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) were not among those who disbelieve and wrong but among those who cannot find *ḥīla* or *sabīl* — Hell’s path is not for helpless but for hinderers and wrongers — the easy for Him is not arbitrary but measure.

**The Only *Ṭarīq* Left Is Hell’s**

The word *illā* — except — was explained to keep Hell’s path as the only *ṭarīq* left where any other *ṭarīq* would be mercy and guidance; to be guided to Hell’s path is not guidance as *hidāyah* to mercy but as *tawlīyah* — letting pursue what he chose (4:115) — the sūrah’s leaving to stray (4:88, 4:143). The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — Hell’s path forever is the other reward’s opposite; Gardens true (4:122) is the *hidāyah* path, Hell forever (4:169) is the allowed stray path. The verse generalises the sūrah’s *yasīr* — easy — where *“burn in Fire, that is easy for God”* (4:30) — devouring wealth is cousin to consuming people’s wealth unjustly and taking *ribā* (4:161) — all are *yasīr* to punish as all are *muḥīṭ* to know. The next passage will turn from history’s litigants to humanity: O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good, if you disbelieve then to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise (4:170) — belief’s call where Hell’s path easy is alternative.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Easy Threat After Far Straying**

Though only *“except that of Hell to stay for ever and ever, and that is easy for God,”* the verse anchors easy threat after far straying declared (4:167) and neither forgiven nor guided (4:168). The sūrah that warns *do not go to extremes regarding faith* (4:171) and declares *Trinity, stop* — *God is only One God, far above having a son* — sees the Trinity boast as part of disbelief and hindering far astray whose path is Hell forever easy; the correction follows. The next verses will address humanity and People of the Book directly: the Messenger has come with truth (4:170), do not go to extremes regarding faith (4:171), Messiah not too proud to be servant nor angels nearest (4:172) — all are the alternative path — belief and good, mercy and grace, straight path (4:174–175) — versus Hell’s easy.

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:170

> O humanity! The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good. But if you disbelieve, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

**Expanded Commentary**

**O Humanity — The Messenger Has Come With Truth From Your Lord**

The verse opens *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakumu al-rasūlu bi al-ḥaqqi min rabbikum* — O humanity, the Messenger — *al-rasūl* — the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ — has certainly come to you with the truth, the true, from your Lord. *Yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as second great humanity address after *“O humanity, be mindful of your Lord who created you from a single soul”* (4:1) and *“O humanity, He can remove you and bring others if He wills, He is Most Capable”* (4:133) — now *“O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth.”* *Qad jāʾakumu al-rasūlu* — has certainly come to you the Messenger — was read as fulfilment of the chain — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Psalms to David* (4:163), messengers told and not, Moses spoken to directly (4:164), messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse after messengers, He is Almighty, All-Wise (4:165), sufficient witness to what He sent with His knowledge and angels witness (4:166) — the Messenger is the told messenger. *Bi al-ḥaqqi* — with truth, as truth — was explained as that He came with true content and true descent, as the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) and as God’s promise is true, whose word more truthful? (4:122). *Min rabbikum* — from your Lord — was read as from the Owner to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126) who is Lord who created from single soul (4:1) — truth from Him.

**So Believe For Your Own Good**

The call *fa āminū khayran lakum* — so believe, have faith, it is better for you, good for you, as good — was explained with *khayran lakum* — better for you, good for you — not for Him, for the addressee, as He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) though you disobey — to Him still belongs all. *Āminū* — have faith, believe — was read as comprehensive faith — *have faith in God, His Messenger, Book He revealed to His Messenger and Scriptures before* (4:136) — steadfast, not wavering, not distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150) — to be among those who accept all, rejecting none, to be given rewards (4:152). *Khayran lakum* was linked to *“Gardens forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — belief’s *khayr* is Gardens and great reward promised to the grounded (4:162) and to those who hold fast to Him guided through straight path (4:175); to believe is to obtain the havens promised to the emigrant (4:100) and enrichment after separation (4:130) — *khayran lakum* is both world and Hereafter. Early reports added that the *fa* — so — makes belief the response after the Messenger has come with truth and after excuse removed (4:165) and witness sufficient (4:166) — belief is not speculation but response.

**But If You Disbelieve — To Him Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth**

The warning *wa in takfurū fa inna li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — but if you disbelieve, cover, then indeed to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — was explained as that disbelief does not harm the Owner: as *We have commanded those before you and you to be mindful, if you disbelieve to Him still belongs all, He is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy* (4:131) — here *if you disbelieve* after the Messenger has come with truth, the same ownership remains. *Li Allāhi mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth — was read as that disbelief after the Messenger’s truth is like the earlier demand greater than a book — *show God visible* — answered with thunderbolt and Mount raised (4:153–154) — to demand while ownership is His is disbelief against Owner. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — punishment is not His need; ownership after disbelief says the same — disbelief impoverishes the disbeliever, not the Owner. The clause was also linked to *“except that of Hell to stay forever, and that is easy for Him”* (4:169) — easy where ownership is all — Hell’s path easy is within that belonging.

**And God Is All-Knowing, All-Wise**

The seal *wa kāna Allāhu ʿAlīman Ḥakīmā* — And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, was ever — was explained with *ʿAlīm* — All-Knowing — hearing disbelief and belief, knowing whether *khayran lakum* — better for you — is chosen — *He is All-Aware of what you do* (4:135) — and *Ḥakīm* — All-Wise — who sent messengers as good news and warnings so no excuse (4:165) and took Mount for covenant and sent Book with truth to judge (4:105) — wisdom is that the Messenger came with *ḥaqq* from Lord. *ʿAlīm Ḥakīm* was also the seal for *“whoever earns sin earns only upon himself, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise”* (4:111) — His knowing and wisdom guarantee that belief and disbelief are measured as not wronging an atom (4:40) and not wronging a speck (*naqīrā* — 4:124). To call to humanity — *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — to believe for your good, yet He is Self-Sufficient, All-Knowing, All-Wise, shows belief is medicine not debt.

**A Verse That Follows Hell’s Path Easy With Humanity’s Call**

Placed after the history — demand for a book from heaven and greater demand visible God, thunderbolt, calf yet forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant, breaking, rejecting signs, killing prophets, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but made to appear, raised, belief before death, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, taking interest though forbidden, consuming unjustly, painful punishment for disbelievers among them, but grounded among them to great reward, then lineage, messengers told and not, directly spoken, good news and warnings so no excuse, sufficient witness, disbelief and hindering far astray, disbelief and wrong not forgiven nor guided except Hell’s path forever easy — now the sūrah turns from third-person litigants to second-person humanity: O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your good, if you disbelieve to Him still belongs all, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. The sūrah that began with single soul now ends its warning segment with humanity’s choice where ownership and knowledge and wisdom guarantee that believing is better for you, not for Him. For the weak this is an opening: where you were told to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), the Messenger has come with truth — refer now — where you were told to verify reports (4:83), verify truth has come. The next passage will address People of the Book directly: do not go to extremes regarding faith, say nothing about God except truth, the Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him, believe in God and His messengers, do not say Trinity, stop — for your own good — He is only One God, far above having a son, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee (4:171).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:171

> O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith; say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit ˹created by a command˺ from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, “Trinity.” Stop!—for your own good. Allah is only One God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs.

**Expanded Commentary**

**O People of the Book — Do Not Go to Extremes Regarding Faith**

The verse opens *yā ahla al-kitābi lā taghlū fī dīnikum wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — O People of the Book, do not go to extremes, exceed limits, in your religion, and say nothing about God except the truth. *Lā taghlū* — do not exceed, go to extremes — was explained with *ghuluww* — excess beyond limit, as the sūrah earlier forbade association not forgiven though what is less is for whom He wills (4:116) and forbade distinguishing between God and messengers desiring a way between (4:150) — to make *ʿĪsā* god is excess, to deny him is neglect. *Fī dīnikum* — regarding your faith, in your religion — was read as the Christian excess of divinising the Messiah and the Jewish neglect of denying him, both excesses. *Wa lā taqūlū ʿalā Allāhi illā al-ḥaqq* — say nothing about God except truth — was explained as that He is sufficient as Witness (4:166) who bears witness with His knowledge, and whose word none is more truthful than (4:122): to say about Him without truth is to claim witness without knowledge. The sūrah has shown that the Book was sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105); *ghuluww* is to judge without that showing. Early reports noted that Christians exceeded in Jesus as Jews did in slandering Mary with *buhtān ʿaẓīm* (4:156); the middle is *ḥaqq* — truth — that Jesus is servant honoured, not god.

**The Messiah, Son of Mary, Was No More Than Messenger and Word Through Mary and Spirit From Him**

The definition *innamā al-masīḥu ʿĪsā ibnu Maryama rasūlu Allāhi wa kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama wa rūḥun minhu* — the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of God and the fulfilment, execution, of His Word — *kalimah* — cast to Mary and a spirit — *rūḥ* — from Him, created by command from Him — was explained with three. *Rasūlu Allāhi* — messenger of God — was read as the chain’s continuity: *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Jesus… to Moses He spoke* (4:163–164), all messengers delivering good news and warnings so no excuse (4:165) — Jesus is among them. *Kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama* — His Word He conveyed to Mary — was explained as *“Be”* — *kun* — He said to Mary, as creation from a word, without father, as *“He creates what He wills when He decrees He says Be and it is”* — the *kalimah* is command not offspring. *Wa rūḥun minhu* — and a spirit from Him, created by command from Him — was explained as *rūḥ* — spirit — from Him as *“We breathed into her Our spirit”* (66:12), given, not part of Him — the sūrah later says *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee”* — the spirit belongs to Him. The phrase *innamā* — only, no more than — was read as restriction: Messiah is only messenger, Word, spirit-from-Him; divinity is excluded as excess. Where the sūrah says *“We have prepared for true disbelievers humiliating punishment”* (4:151) for distinguishing, and *“those who believe in God and messengers accepting all, rejecting none, He will give rewards”* (4:152) — this definition is the acceptance of Jesus as messenger among messengers, not god among gods.

**So Believe in God and His Messengers and Do Not Say Trinity — For Your Own Good**

The command *fa āminū bi Allāhi wa rusulihī wa lā taqūlū thalāthatun* — so believe in God and His messengers and do not say three, Trinity — *thalāthah* — was explained with *thalāthah* — three — as the Trinity doctrine — Father, Son, Holy Spirit as one — the excess the sūrah calls *ghuluww*. *Wa lā taqūlū thalāthah* — do not say Trinity — was read as that *ḥaqq* is *“God is only One God, far above having a son”* — He is *Wāḥid* — One, as *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth”* — to say three is to claim division of ownership. *Intahū khayran lakum* — Stop, desist, for your own good, better for you — was explained with *khayran lakum* — better for you — the same *khayran lakum* as *“O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your own good”* (4:170) — stopping Trinity is better for you, as He is Self-Sufficient (4:131) — not for Him. *Innamā Allāhu ilāhun wāḥid* — God is only One God — was read as the sūrah’s monotheism that association is not forgiven (4:116) and invokes female gods as Satan’s share (4:117) — Three is association far astray.

**Glory Be to Him — Far Above Having a Son — To Him Belongs Whatever Is in Heavens and Earth**

The glorification *subḥānahu an yakūna lahū walad* — glory be to Him, exalted is He, that He should have a son, that there be for Him a child — was explained with *subḥānahu* — glory, exaltation — as the Book’s *tasbīḥ* for the One to whom belongs whatever is in heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131, 4:170). *An yakūna lahū walad* — that He should have a son — was read as impossibility for the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy (4:131) who can remove humanity and bring others (4:133) — a son is not needed. *Lahū mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-arḍ* — to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and whatever on earth — was explained as that ownership denies need for son: *“if you disbelieve, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise”* (4:170) — after the Messenger has come with truth — Trinity divides ownership. *Wa kafā bi Allāhi wakīlā* — and He suffices as Trustee — was read as that *wakīl* suffices as Guardian without son, as the oppressed cry for *walī* and *naṣīr* from grace (4:75) — guardian is Him, not third of three. The sūrah has shown that *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:132) — three is not needed for trusteeship.

**A Verse That Follows Humanity’s Call With People of the Book’s Correction**

Placed after *O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your own good, if you disbelieve to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise* (4:170), this verse follows humanity’s call with People of the Book’s correction where the People of the Book demanded a book from heaven and greater — visible God — took calf yet were forgiven, Mount raised, firm covenant taken, then breaking, rejecting, killing, claiming *ghulf* sealed, denying, slander against Mary, boasting killing Messiah not killed but raised (4:153–158). The correction — do not go to extremes, say nothing but truth, Messiah was but messenger and Word through Mary and spirit from Him, believe in God and messengers, do not say Trinity, stop — better — He is One God far above having a son, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee — is the middle after two extremes: Jewish extremes — denial and slander and boasting murder — and Christian extremes — deification as Trinity. The sūrah that began with single soul spread into humanity (4:1) and declares *“neither by your wishes nor those of People of the Book”* (4:123) makes that middle the truth by which the sūrah has judged: the Book sent with truth, witness sufficient (4:166). For the weak this is an opening: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), Trinity is not settlement between God and messengers; to believe in God and His messengers and not say three is the settlement that is best — better for you.

**The Word Through Mary as Command Not Offspring**

The phrase *kalimatuhū alqāhā ilā Maryama wa rūḥun minhu* was explained to distinguish *kalimah* as *“Be”* commanded, not begotten, and *rūḥ* as created spirit from Him, not part. The sūrah later says *“the Messiah will never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest”* (4:172) — servant is the Word’s rank, worshipped is not. The next verse will set that servitude as proof: the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest — those too proud will be gathered before Him, the believers and doers of good rewarded in full and increased out of grace, the too proud subjected to painful punishment without protector besides Him (4:172–173).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:172

> The Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels nearest to Allah. Those who are too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together.

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Messiah Would Never Be Too Proud to Be Servant Nor Angels Nearest**

The verse states *lan yastankifa al-masīḥu an yakūna ʿabdan li Allāhi wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — the Messiah — *al-masīḥ* — Jesus, son of Mary, messenger and Word through Mary and spirit from Him (4:171) — would never disdain, be too proud, to be a servant, slave, to God, nor would the angels nearest — *al-muqarrabūn* — those brought near. *Lan yastankif* — never be too proud, never disdain, never refuse out of pride — was explained with *istinkāf* — pride that refuses service, as the sūrah has shown that those too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together (now), and as earlier *Satan was proud* — *istakbara* — refusing prostration. *An yakūna ʿabdan li Allāhi* — to be a servant to God — was read as *ʿubūdiyyah* — servitude — the rank of every messenger in lineage — *We have sent revelation to you as We sent to Noah… Jesus taught* (4:163) — all are servants. *Wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — nor the angels nearest — was explained as *muqarrab* — those brought near — *“the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest”* — the highest creatures — Messiah, whose mother was slandered with mighty *buhtān* (4:156), and angels who bear witness with His knowledge (4:166) and who stood witness for Mount raised (4:154) — are servants. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee”* (4:171) — servants belong to Him; to claim the Messiah is beyond servitude is *ghuluww* — going to extremes (4:171) — the Messiah himself would never claim it.

**Those Too Proud to Worship Him Will Be Gathered Before Him**

The warning *wa man yastankif ʿan ʿibādatihī wa yastakbir fa sa yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿā* — and whoever is too proud, disdains, to worship Him, serve Him, and is arrogant, will be gathered, mustered, to Him, toward Him, all together — was explained with *yastankif* — too proud — and *yastakbir* — arrogant, magnifies self — pair already in Satan, cursed (4:118) — who said *I will surely take a share* (4:118). *ʿAn ʿibādatihī* — from His worship, His servitude — was read as that *ʿubūdiyyah* is not debasement but honour, as Abraham taken as *khalīl* (4:125) was servant, as Moses spoken to directly (4:164) was servant, as angels nearest are servants. *Fa sa yaḥshuruhum ilayhi jamīʿā* — He will gather them to Him all together — was explained with *ḥashara* — to gather, to muster — the same gathering as *He will gather you on the Day about which there is no doubt* (4:87) and *He will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell* (4:140) and *those who disbelieve and wrong, He will not forgive nor guide except Hell’s path forever* (4:168–169) — the too proud are gathered for reckoning. The phrase *jamīʿan* — all together — was explained as that the Messiah not too proud and angels not too proud, yet the proud among humanity will be gathered with the proud — *jamīʿan* — as hypocrites gathered together in Hell.

**A Verse That Follows Do Not Say Trinity With Messiah Not Too Proud**

Placed after *O People of the Book, do not go to extremes, say nothing but truth, Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him, believe in God and messengers, do not say Trinity, stop — better — He is One God far above having a son, to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He suffices as Trustee* (4:171), this verse follows *do not say Trinity* with *the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest*. The correction — Messiah is but messenger — is proven by his own attitude: he would never disdain servitude; to claim him god is to claim for him what he would disdain. The sūrah has shown that *“Satan promises only delusion”* (4:120) yet his share is those who take female gods besides Him (4:117) — to make the Messiah more than servant is delusion, not his wish. The sūrah has shown that *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — servitude is the worship that receives both, as the emigrant’s many havens are *ʿibādah* rewarded. For the weak this is an anchor: where you were told to be grateful and faithful — *why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful?* (4:147) — servitude is grateful faith; to be too proud to worship is ingratitude.

**The Angels Nearest as Witness to Servitude**

The addition *wa lā al-malāʾikatu al-muqarrabūn* — nor the angels nearest — was explained as witness: angels nearest to Him — *muqarrabūn* — who bear witness to what He sent with His knowledge (4:166), who guard, who raise Mount, who take souls — are servants not too proud; their nearness is servitude, not partnership. The sūrah has shown that *“everyone of People of the Book will believe in him before his death, and on the Day he will be witness against them”* (4:159) — Messiah as witness is servant witness, as angels are witness servants. Where the sūrah says *“do not incline entirely leaving the other suspended”* (4:129) — to make the Messiah god is to incline entirely to him leaving the One suspended as son — the verse corrects incline: Messiah not too proud, angels not too proud; to worship is to worship Him alone whose ownership is all (4:126). The next verse will briefly note how the gathered are then rewarded or punished (4:173).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:173

> As for those who believe and do good, He will reward them in full and increase them out of His grace. But those who are too proud and arrogant, He will subject them to a painful punishment. And besides Allah they will find no protector or helper.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Believe and Do Good — Rewarded in Full and Increased Out of Grace**

The verse opens *fa ammā alladhīna āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti fa yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa yazīduhum min faḍlihī* — as for those who believe and do good, do righteous deeds, He will repay, fulfil, their rewards fully and increase them out of His bounty, grace. *Āmanū wa ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāt* — faith and righteous deeds — was explained as the sūrah’s shorthand for the faithful: opposed to those too proud to worship Him (4:172) and those who disbelieve and hinder far astray (4:167). *Fa yuwaffīhim ujūrahum* — He will fulfil their wages, repay fully — was read with *waffā* — to give in full, to complete — the same root for *“God does not wrong even an atom, if it is good He multiplies”* (4:40) — fulfilling is not wronging even speck (*naqīrā* — 4:124) — the atom not wronged is the wage given full. *Wa yazīduhum min faḍlihī* — and increase them out of His grace, bounty — was explained with *faḍl* — grace, bounty — the same *faḍl* without which a group would have deceived you yet they deceive only themselves (4:113), and *“great is His favour upon you”* (4:113) — increase is from grace, not debt, as Gardens forever where promise is true (4:122) — increase is Rivers under, not cut. Early reports linked increase to *“He will admit them into Gardens … under rivers flow”* and to abundant Havens for emigrant (4:100) — world and Hereafter.

**But Those Too Proud Will Be Subjected to Painful Punishment**

The contrast *wa ammā alladhīna istankafū wa istakbarū fa yuʿadhdhibuhum ʿadhāban alīmā* — but as for those who were too proud, disdained, and were arrogant, magnified themselves — He will punish them with a painful, aching punishment — was explained with *istankafū wa istakbarū* — too proud and arrogant — the same pair as *the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest; those too proud and arrogant will be gathered* (4:172) — now gathered to punishment. *Fa yuʿadhdhibuhum ʿadhāban alīmā* — He will punish them with painful punishment — was explained with *ʿadhāb alīm* — painful — the same *alīm* announced to hypocrites as good news of painful punishment (4:138) and prepared for disbelievers among the Book’s People for *ribā* and *akl bi al-bāṭil* (4:161) — painful matches proud: to be too proud to serve (4:172) is to earn pain as servant’s opposite. The sūrah has shown that *“lowest depth of Fire, you will never find helper”* (4:145) — painful is lowest depth; and *“He will neither forgive nor guide them to any path except Hell’s path forever, and that is easy for Him”* (4:168–169) — easy where Almighty — here painful as promised.

**And Besides Him They Will Find No Protector or Helper**

The closure *wa lā yajidūna lahum min dūni Allāhi waliyyan wa lā naṣīrā* — and they will not find for themselves besides Him, apart from Him, any protector, guardian, nor helper — was explained with *walī* and *naṣīr* — the same pair the oppressed cry for from grace (4:75) and that God alone suffices as (4:45) and that hypocrites sought among disbelievers as allies seeking honour (4:139) — the too proud sought *ʿizzah* among disbelievers and among pride itself, yet will find no *walī* and no *naṣīr* besides Him where punishment is. *Min dūni Allāhi* — besides Him, apart from Him — was read as that no female god invoked (4:117) and no Satan as guardian taken instead of Him (4:119) and no disbeliever as ally (4:144) will avail on the Day where all are gathered before Him all together (4:172). The sūrah has said *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — protection besides Him is not needed where both rewards are with Him; to seek it is to find none. Where the sūrah says *“He is sufficient as Trustee”* (4:171) — Messiah’s case — the too proud find no trustee.

**A Verse That Follows Gathering With Repaying and Punishing**

Placed after *the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest; those too proud and arrogant will be gathered before Him all together* (4:172), this verse follows gathering with repaying and punishing: as for those who believe and do good — fulfilled wages and increase from grace; but those too proud and arrogant — painful punishment, no protector or helper besides Him. The sūrah has shown that *“whoever does good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck”* (4:124) — fulfilled wages is that entry; and *“whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly and find no protector besides Him”* (4:123) — painful where disbelief and wrong are — now applied to pride. The sūrah that warns not to deviate by following desires (4:27) and not to let desires deviate from justice (4:135) sees *istinkāf wa istikbār* — being too proud and arrogant — as the pride that deviates most, because *ʿubūdiyyah* — servitude — is the sūrah’s ethic: to stand for justice though against yourselves (4:135) is servitude, to not incline entirely leaving hanging (4:129) is servitude, to verify before fighting (4:94) is servitude.

**Repaying in Full and Increase as Grace**

The phrase *fa yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa yazīduhum min faḍlihī* was explained to keep repaying in full as justice — not wronging even atom (4:40) — and increase as grace — *faḍl* — the same grace that taught you what you did not know (4:113) and that makes *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) true: appreciation is increase from grace. The sūrah has shown that the emigrant finds many havens and abundance (4:100) — increase from grace — and enrichment after separation (4:130) — increase from His bounty. For the weak this is steadying: where you were told settlement is best though selves brought with *shuḥḥ* (4:128), to be among those who believe and do good is to have wages fulfilled and grace increase; where you were too proud to worship, wage is painful and no protector. The next passage will turn from history to humanity: O humanity, there has come to you conclusive evidence from your Lord, We have sent down to you a brilliant light (4:174).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:174

> O humanity! There has come to you conclusive evidence from your Lord. And We have sent down to you a brilliant light.

**Expanded Commentary**

**O Humanity — Conclusive Evidence Has Come From Your Lord**

The verse states *yā ayyuhā al-nāsu qad jāʾakum burhānun min rabbikum* — O humanity, there has certainly come to you a proof, evidence, demonstration, from your Lord. *Yā ayyuhā al-nāsu* — O humanity — was explained as third great humanity address after *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* (4:1) and *“if He wills He can remove you and bring others”* (4:133) and *“the Messenger has come with truth from your Lord, so believe for your own good”* (4:170) — now *“conclusive evidence has come.”* *Qad jāʾakum* — has certainly come to you — was read with emphasis: the evidence has arrived, not pending, as lineage from Noah through Jesus to you (4:163) was already sent as *mubashshirīn wa mundhirīn* so no excuse remains (4:165) — now evidence. *Burhānun min rabbikum* — proof from your Lord — was explained with *burhān* — conclusive proof, demonstration — the same root *brh* as clarity where *He wills to make clear* (4:26) and *taught you what you did not know* (4:113) — *burhān* is the Prophet ﷺ himself with miracles and the Qur’an as proof. Early reports linked *burhān* to the Prophet, while *nūr* — light — after is Qur’an, showing two proofs: messenger and book. The sūrah has shown that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126) — proof from your Lord who owns and encompasses is the most near. The phrase was linked to *“Gardens for those who believe and do good”* (4:122) — proof’s purpose is Gardens, as *“O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your own good”* (4:170) — better for you.

**And We Have Sent Down to You a Brilliant Light**

The second clause *wa anzalnā ilaykum nūran mubīnā* — and We have sent down to you a clear, brilliant, manifest light — was explained with *nūr* — light — *mubīn* — clear, manifest — the same *nūr* and *mubīn* as *sulṭān mubīn* — compelling proof — Moses was given (4:153) and as clear light where association is not forgiven (4:116) — light shows far straying. *Anzalnā ilaykum* — We sent down to you — was read as the Qur’an sent with truth — *bi al-ḥaqq* — to judge between people by what He shows (4:105) — light shows judgment, as the Mount raised (4:154) was physical light of proof. *Nūr mubīn* was explained as Qur’an that makes clear, as *“He wills to lighten burdens”* (4:28) — light lightens; the sūrah that taught prayer at fixed time (4:103) as *kitāban mawqūtā* — light times. Early reports added that the *burhān* and *nūr* are the two witnesses: God bears witness with His knowledge and angels bear witness (4:166) — His knowledge is light, angels’ witness is proof. Where the sūrah says *“do not go to extremes regarding faith, say nothing but truth”* (4:171) — do not say Trinity — truth is the light that makes extremes visible as extremes, as Satan’s promises only delusion (4:120) are darkness.

**A Verse That Follows Humanity’s Call With Complement**

Placed after *O humanity, the Messenger has come with truth, so believe for your own good* (4:170), *O People of the Book, do not go to extremes, Messiah was but messenger, Word through Mary and spirit from Him, do not say Trinity* (4:171), *Messiah would never be too proud to be servant, nor angels nearest, those too proud will be gathered then repaid in full and increased or punished painful without protector* (4:172–173), this verse follows humanity’s call and messiah’s correction with its complement: conclusive evidence has come from your Lord — messenger — and brilliant light sent down — Qur’an. The sūrah has shown that those who disbelieve and hinder far astray (4:167), disbelieve and wrong not forgiven nor guided except Hell’s path forever easy (4:168–169) — light is the opposite hindering: to send light is to unhinder. The sūrah that warns *most secret talks have no good except charity, kindness, reconciliation* (4:114) — light is the *najwā* made good: the Book’s light as charity. For the weak this is an opening: where you feared rising or turning away and settlement is best (4:128), light shows settlement; where helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99), light shows pardon hoped is light; where emigrant finds many havens (4:100), light shows havens.

**The Brilliant Light That Makes Disproof Visible**

The phrase *nūran mubīnā* — brilliant, clear light — was explained to include future guidance: light manifest makes Trinity’s *thalāthah* — three — visible as excess, makes *buhtān ʿaẓīm* against Mary visible as slander, makes boasting killing Messiah not killed visible as assumption, makes *ribā* though forbidden visible as unjust consumption. The sūrah has shown that *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — light is gratitude’s tool: to be grateful you see what He gave, light shows. The verse generalises the sūrah’s *“He wills to make clear”* (4:26) — *burhān* and *nūr* are that making clear. The next verse will describe believers who hold fast being admitted into mercy and guided (4:175).

**A Short Verse That Anchors Evidence Before Guidance**

Though only *“O humanity, conclusive evidence has come from your Lord, We have sent down to you a brilliant light,”* the verse anchors evidence before guidance to be given. The chapter that began *“be mindful of your Lord who created you from single soul”* (4:1), showed ownership to Him of heavens and earth, sufficiency as Trustee, capability to replace, both rewards with Him Hearing and Seeing, justice though against yourselves, comprehensive faith, oscillation without forgiveness, hypocrite portrait, lowest depth without helper except those who repent, discipline of speech, distinction between God and messengers, demand for a book from heaven as litany, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, well-grounded to great reward, lineage, messengers told and not, direct speech, good news and warnings, sufficient witness, far straying, Hell’s path easy, humanity’s call, correction of People of the Book, servitude of Messiah and angels, repaying, here says evidence and light have come — so that excuse is cut where light is. The next verses will address the final asking: they ask you for a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents — God gives ruling regarding inheritance of siblings (4:176).

## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:175

> As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the Straight Path.

**Expanded Commentary**

**Those Who Believe and Hold Fast — Admitted Into Mercy and Grace**

The verse states *fa ammā alladhīna āmanū bi Allāhi wa iʿtaṣamū bihī fa sa yudkhiluhum fī raḥmatin minhu wa faḍlin* — as for those who believe in God and hold fast, cling, to Him, He will admit, will enter them, into mercy from Him and grace, bounty. *Āmanū bi Allāhi* — believe in God — was explained with comprehensive faith — *have faith in God, Messenger, Book and Scriptures, angels, Last Day* (4:136) — steadfast, not wavering, not distinguishing (4:150–152) — the faith that accepts all messengers whose stories told and not (4:164) after lineage from Noah through Jesus (4:163). *Wa iʿtaṣamū bihī* — and hold fast, cling, to Him, to it — was read with *iʿtiṣām* — holding fast — the same *iʿtiṣām* that repentant hypocrites must do — *hold fast to God* (4:146) — and that those well-grounded do — establishing prayer (4:162) — and that the emigrant to God has reward secured (4:100). *Iʿtaṣamū bihī* was explained as *bih* — to Him, to it — both: to God and to His rope — the Qur’an — the brilliant light — *nūr mubīn* — evidence — *burhān* (4:174) — and to the Book sent with truth to judge between people (4:105). *Fa sa yudkhiluhum fī raḥmatin minhu wa faḍlin* — He will admit them into mercy from Him and grace — was explained with *raḥmah* — mercy — and *faḍl* — grace, bounty — the two that make Gardens true (4:122) — mercy as forgiveness for faults, grace as increase. The sūrah has said *“why should He punish if you are grateful and faithful? He is ever Appreciative”* (4:147) — admission into mercy and grace is the Appreciative’s response to holding fast. Where *“with Him are both rewards He hears and sees”* (4:134) — mercy and grace are those rewards.

**And Guide Them to Himself Through the Straight Path**

The second promise *wa yahdīhim ilayhi ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* — and He will guide them to Him, toward Him, through, as, the straight — upright, direct — path — was explained with *yahdīhim ilayhi* — guide them to Him, toward Him — not only to Gardens but to Himself, as the emigrant emigrates to God and Messenger (4:100) — reward falls upon Him. *Ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* — straight path — was explained as the sūrah’s path — noble ways He wishes to make clear (4:26), believers’ path not to be left (4:115), the path He guides to through mercy (now), as the sūrah wills to make clear, guide, turn. *Mustaqīm* — straight, upright — was read as the opposite of *ghuluww* — going to extremes (4:171) — Trinity and denial both deviate; straight is middle — Messiah as servant not god, Mary pure not slandered, Moses spoken to directly — true. The sūrah has shown that *“the Messiah would never be too proud to be servant”* (4:172) — servitude is straight; to be too proud is deviant. *Yahdīhim ilayhi* was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — Gardens are mercy and grace guided to Him.

**A Verse That Follows Evidence and Light With Response**

Placed after *O humanity, conclusive evidence has come from your Lord, We have sent down to you a brilliant light* (4:174), this verse follows evidence and light with response: as for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him — to evidence and light — He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the straight path. The sūrah has shown that those who disbelieve and hinder far astray (4:167), disbelieve and wrong not forgiven nor guided except Hell’s path forever easy (4:168–169) — opposite of mercy and grace and straight path. The sūrah that warns not to take disbelievers as allies instead of believers (4:144) and describes lowest depth without helper (4:145) makes *iʿtiṣām bihī* — holding fast to Him — the opposite alliance: to take Him as trustee suffices (4:132). For the weak this is steadying: where you were told to refer disputes to God and Messenger (4:59), holding fast is referral; where you were told to verify reports (4:83), evidence and light is verification; where you were told to be sure before fighting (4:94), holding fast is sureness.

**Mercy and Grace Guided Through Straight Path**

The pair *raḥmah minhu wa faḍl* — mercy from Him and grace — was explained as mercy that pardons the helpless hoped to be pardoned (4:99) — *ʿAfuww Ghafūr* — and forgives the mistaken by fasting (4:92) — and grace that gives many havens to the emigrant (4:100) — *murāgham kathīr wa saʿah* — and great reward to the grounded (4:162) — *ajran ʿaẓīmā* — and repays doers of good in full and increases out of grace (4:173). *Yahdīhim ilayhi ṣirāṭan mustaqīman* was linked to *“He wills to make clear, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26–28) — making clear is *burhān* and *nūr* (4:174), guiding to noble ways is *ṣirāṭ mustaqīm* now, turning in mercy is *raḥmah minhu wa faḍl*. To be guided to Him through straight path is to be among those who believe and do good in Gardens where promise is true (4:122) — straight is the sūrah’s law for orphans, women, inheritance, trust, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham, settlement, enrichment — all are straight.

**A Short Verse That Anchors Holding Fast Before Final Ruling**

Though only *“as for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him, He will admit into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the straight path,”* the verse anchors holding fast before final ruling regarding siblings. The chapter that began with single soul and honouring ties (4:1), showed orphan girls deprived, settlement best, total inclining prohibited, enrichment after separation, universal command to be mindful, ownership and encompassing, demand for a book from heaven as litany, forbidding *ṭayyibāt* for *ẓulm* and hindering, well-grounded to great reward, lineage, messengers, good news and warnings, sufficient witness, calling humanity, correcting People of the Book, servitude of Messiah, evidence and light, now says holding fast to that evidence and light is the act that places into mercy and grace and straight path. The next verse will set the final asking: they ask you for a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents — God gives ruling regarding siblings — male and female shares as prescribed so you do not go astray (4:176).

---
## Sūrah al-Nisāʾ 4:176

> They ask you ˹for a ruling, O Prophet˺. Say, “Allah gives you a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents.” If a man dies childless and leaves behind a sister, she will inherit one-half of his estate, whereas her brother will inherit all of her estate if she dies childless. If this person leaves behind two sisters, they together will inherit two-thirds of the estate. But if the deceased leaves male and female siblings, a male’s share will be equal to that of two females. Allah makes ˹this˺ clear to you so you do not go astray. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

**Expanded Commentary**

**They Ask You for a Ruling Regarding One Without Children or Parents**

The verse opens *yastaftūnaka quli Allāhu yuftīkum fī al-kalālati* — they ask you, seek your ruling, your *fatwā* — say, God gives you ruling regarding the *kalālah* — the one who dies without children or parents, without direct ascendant or descendant. *Yastaftūnaka* — they ask you — was explained as second asking in the sūrah after *“they ask you regarding women, God instructs you, instruction already recited concerning orphan women deprived yet wished to marry, helpless children, orphans’ rights, whatever good you do is well known to Him”* (4:127) — now they ask regarding *kalālah*. *Quli Allāhu yuftīkum* — say, God instructs you, gives ruling — was read as that *“to Him belongs whatever is in heavens and earth, He is Fully Aware”* (4:126) — so He instructs, as evidence and light have come from your Lord (4:174) — instruction is light. *Fī al-kalālati* — regarding *kalālah* — was explained with *kalālah* — one who leaves neither parent nor child, the one whose line is cut at both ends, whose estate is therefore to siblings, as the sūrah earlier said *“you will inherit half of what your wives leave if childless, but if they have children then one-fourth… And if a man or woman leaves neither parents nor children but only a sibling then…”* (4:12) where *kalālah* rule began for maternal siblings — here it is extended to paternal/full siblings. Early reports noted this verse was among the last revealed, answering Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh’s illness where he was *kalālah* without parent or child, asking about his sisters’ shares — the sūrah’s closing is personal.

**If a Man Dies Childless Leaving a Sister — She Inherits One-Half, Brother Inherits All**

The details *in imruʾun halaka laysa lahū waladun wa lahū ukhtun fa lahā niṣfu mā taraka wa huwa yarithuhā in lam yakun lahā walad* — if a man dies, perishes, is destroyed — *halaka* — leaves no child, and has a sister, then for her is half what he leaves, and he — her brother — inherits her — all of her — if she dies childless — were explained with two mirrors. *Imruʾun halaka* — a man perishes — *laysa lahū waladun* — he has no child — was read as the *kalālah* male; *wa lahū ukhtun* — and has a sister — one sister alone; *fa lahā niṣfu mā taraka* — for her half what he leaves — after bequest and debt, as obligatory shares (4:7: little or much, obligatory) — half for one female, as earlier one female alone inherits one-half (4:11) where daughter alone half — here sister half. *Wa huwa yarithuhā in lam yakun lahā walad* — and he inherits her — her brother inherits all of her estate if she dies childless without parent — was explained as that brother as sole sibling inherits entirety where sister alone half — the imbalance was read as not unfair because sibling inheritance here is for full/paternal siblings where male’s share will be equal to two females where together (next), and where no child the brother assumes clan protection, as the single soul spread into humanity (4:1) — brother inherits all to sustain ties. The sūrah has shown that inheritance is *farīḍah* — obligation (4:11) — and that limits set by God admit to Gardens (4:13) and exceeding casts into Hell (4:14) — *kalālah* shares are limits.

**If Two Sisters — They Inherit Two-Thirds**

The case *fa in kānatā ithnatayni fa lahumā al-thuluthāni mimmā taraka* — but if the two — sisters — are two, then for them two-thirds of what he leaves — was explained with *ithnatayni* — two sisters together — as the female pair, as earlier *if you leave only two or more females, their share is two-thirds* (4:11) where daughters two-plus two-thirds — here sisters two two-thirds. *Mimmā taraka* — of what he leaves — after bequest and debt, as *“after fulfilment of bequests and debts without harm”* (4:12) — harm not to heirs. The sūrah has shown that shares for men and women whether little or much are obligatory (4:7), that orphan women deprived yet wished to marry are protected (4:127), that helpless children are stood for with justice (4:127): sisters as *kalālah* heirs are that justice applied at death without child or parent. Early notes added that two sisters as *kalālah* share two-thirds leaving one-third to others where present; the sūrah’s light — *We have sent down brilliant light* (4:174) — makes that clear so you do not go astray.

**But If Siblings Male and Female — Male Equal to Two Females**

The general *wa in kānū ikhwatan rijālan wa nisāʾan fa li al-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi al-unthayayn* — but if they — the deceased’s siblings — are brothers and sisters — male and female — brothers and sisters together — then for the male the like of the share of two females, male’s share equal to that of two females — was explained with *ikhwatan rijālan wa nisāʾan* — brothers and sisters male and female — the mixed group. *Fa li al-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi al-unthayayn* — for the male the like of two females — was read as the sūrah’s arithmetic where *share of male is twice that of female* where children are heirs (4:11) — here siblings share after *kalālah* as children share — principle one: male twice female where survival depends on male’s provision, as *men are maintainers of women as they have been provisioned over women and tasked with supporting them* (4:34) — so inheritance corresponds to expenditure. The sūrah has shown that both do good male or female with faith will enter Paradise not wronged a speck (4:124) — inheritance not Paradise — there male and female both enter; inheritance as world’s division reflects world’s expenditure division. The rule was linked to *“Gardens under rivers forever, promise ever true”* (4:122) — world’s shares are *khayran lakum* — better for you — if you accept, as Light shows.

**God Makes This Clear So You Do Not Go Astray — He Knows All**

The seal *yubayyinu Allāhu lakum an taḍillū wa Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin ʿalīm* — God makes clear to you, explains, lest you go astray, so you do not stray, and God has perfect knowledge of all things, of every thing — was explained with *yubayyinu lakum* — He makes clear to you — the same *yubayyin* as *“He wills to make clear to you, guide to noble ways, turn in mercy”* (4:26) and *burhān* and *nūr mubīn* — evidence and brilliant light — have come (4:174) — now *kalālah* clear. *An taḍillū* — lest you go astray, so you do not stray — was read as that inheritance without clarity would be *ẓulm* — wrongdoing — and *ṣadd* — hindering many from God’s way — the same wrong for which *ṭayyibāt* were forbidden (4:160); to make clear is to prevent straying. *Wa Allāhu bi kulli shayʾin ʿalīm* — and God has perfect knowledge of every thing, of all things — was explained with *bi kulli shayʾ* — of every thing — the same *muḥīṭ* — encompassing everything (4:126) — knowledge that counts every *walad* — child — and every *ukht* — sister — and every *akh* — brother — and every bequest and debt without harm, as He is Fully Aware of everything (4:126) and All-Aware of what you do (4:128, 4:135) — the One who owns heavens and earth (4:126, 4:131) knows *kalālah* shares. The sūrah that began with single soul spread into humanity (4:1) and commanded honouring ties, ends with ties’ shares at death where single soul’s line is cut at both ends — *kalālah* — yet ties remain as siblings, and God makes clear so you do not stray, as He is *ʿAlīm* of all.

**A Verse That Follows Evidence and Light With Inheritance Clear**

Placed after *O humanity, conclusive evidence has come from your Lord, We have sent down to you a brilliant light* (4:174), *as for those who believe in God and hold fast to Him, He will admit into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the straight path* (4:175), this verse follows evidence and light with inheritance clear: they ask you for a ruling regarding *kalālah*, God gives ruling: one sister half, brother inherits all, two sisters two-thirds, mixed male twice female, He makes clear so you do not go astray, He knows all. The sūrah has shown that *“those who believe in God and hold fast”* are admitted into mercy and guided through straight path (4:175) — straight is inheritance shares made clear. The sūrah that began with limits set by God for orphans, women, inheritance, trust, prayer, judgment, charity, Abraham, settlement, enrichment, universal command to be mindful, ownership, capability, both rewards, justice though against yourselves, comprehensive faith, oscillation without forgiveness, hypocrite portrait, lowest depth, speech discipline, distinction, demand for a book from heaven as litany, forbidding *ṭayyibāt*, well-grounded to great reward, lineage, messengers, good news and warnings, sufficient witness, far straying, Hell’s path easy, humanity’s call, correction of People of the Book, servitude of Messiah, evidence and light — now ends where it began: family law — so you do not go astray. For the weak this is an opening: where helpless children were stood for with justice (4:127) and sisters deprived yet wished to marry were protected (4:127), *kalālah* sisters now share as half or two-thirds or with brothers male twice female — all made clear lest you stray, by the One whose earth is spacious and whose promise is true, who is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing, Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Fully Aware encompassing everything.
